title: XLRS-Bench: Could Your Multimodal LLMs Understand Extremely Large Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery?
authors: Fangrun Wang, Haoliang Wang, Zichen Guo, Dong Wang, Yuting Wang, Mengxi Chen, Qiang Ma, Lin Lan, Wen Yang, Jiaming Zhang, Zhiyong Liu, Ming-Ming Sun
institutions: Wuhan University, Chinese Academy of Sciences
summary: XLRS-Bench establishes the ground-truth evaluation benchmark for ultra-high-resolution remote sensing VQA, evaluating multi-modal LLMs on 8Kx8K images across 16 tasks and 45,942 annotations. It reveals that current VLMs suffer severe performance degradation from downscaling and context loss during tiling.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have made remarkable strides in natural image comprehension, yet their capability on extremely large ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing imagery remains largely unmapped. Standard remote sensing images frequently exceed 8000x8000 pixels, where targets occupy only dozens of pixels against massive geospatial backgrounds. In this paper, we introduce XLRS-Bench, the first comprehensive benchmark tailored for UHR remote sensing MLLM evaluation. XLRS-Bench contains 45,942 annotations spanning 16 vision-language tasks covering fine-grained perception, complex relational reasoning, cross-region counting, and multi-temporal change. Extensive evaluations of over 20 proprietary and open-source MLLMs reveal substantial performance degradation caused by excessive downscaling and fragmentation during tiling.
findings:
1. SOTA models drop significantly below human performance on UHR imagery compared to natural benchmarks.
2. Resizing obliterates sub-100-pixel targets.
3. Independent tiling preserves local details but severs cross-tile context, collapsing relational reasoning.
4. Establishes the 16-task taxonomy including spatial relationships and counting.
conclusions: Fixed token budgets and rigid input resolutions in modern VLMs cannot natively handle gigapixel earth observation imagery. Uniform tiling and downscaling represent opposite, flawed extremes.
future_scope: Requires dynamic multi-scale visual token allocation, spatial relation preservation across tiles, and active zoom mechanisms.
relevance_rationale: Direct foundation: XLRS-Bench provides the exact evaluation suite (3,080 test items) and task taxonomy for our research.

what_it_adds.Benchmark Foundation: First standardized benchmark dedicated to 8K+ remote sensing VQA.
what_it_adds.Taxonomy & Diagnostics: Dissects 16 distinct subtasks separating local perception from global spatial reasoning.
what_it_adds.Baselines: Provides baseline evaluations for Qwen2.5-VL, LLaVA, InternVL, and proprietary APIs.

what_it_doesnt_add.Algorithmic Fix: Benchmark paper only; does not provide a model that resolves the crossover dilemma.
what_it_doesnt_add.Latency Optimization: Does not provide fast inference pipelines.

prior_art_overlap: Does not solve our problem; explicitly proves the existence of the spatial failure mode.
differentiation: We design an algorithmic routing and multi-scale grounding solution evaluated on XLRS-Bench.
arch_vision: Evaluates ViT-H/14, InternViT-6B, SigLIP-SO400M across baselines
arch_projector: MLP / Resampler variants across tested models

takeaways.detail: Adopt XLRS-Bench-Lite (3,080 items) for all evaluation runs.
Strictly separate relational (800 items) and non-relational (2,123 items) scores.

title: GeoLLaVA-8K: Scaling Remote-Sensing Multimodal Large Language Models to 8K Resolution
authors: Fangrun Wang, Mengxi Chen, Yuting Wang, Dong Wang, Haoliang Wang, Zichen Guo, Zheng Wang, Bo Shan, Lin Lan, Yihua Wang, Heng Wang, Wen Yang, Bo Du, Jiaming Zhang
institutions: Wuhan University, ByteDance, National University of Singapore
summary: GeoLLaVA-8K scales remote-sensing VLMs up to 8192x8192 resolution using adaptive patch subdivision and a dual-branch global-local feature aggregator, validating that direct high-res processing outperforms naive downsampling on fine-grained aerial tasks.
abstract: Processing ultra-high-resolution (UHR) imagery exceeding 8K resolution remains a paramount challenge for remote sensing MLLMs. We present GeoLLaVA-8K, a framework engineered to ingest 8K imagery through hierarchical adaptive patch subdivision, a dual-branch global-local vision aggregator, and high-resolution instruction tuning.
findings:
1. Dual-branch global-local aggregation retains 85% of fine object features without token blowout.
2. Scales successfully to 8K native resolution.
3. Outperforms standard LLaVA by +14.2% on aerial detection and counting.
conclusions: Dual-scale preservation (low-res global overview + high-res selective patches) is critical for gigapixel remote sensing understanding.
future_scope: Needs dynamic question-guided token routing to cut redundant background tiles in barren terrain.
relevance_rationale: Directly targets 8K aerial imagery; proves global overview is mandatory alongside local crops.

what_it_adds.Dual-Branch Architecture: Combines 1x global overview with Nx high-res local crops.
what_it_adds.8K Instruction Tuning: First dedicated instruction dataset at native 8192x8192.

what_it_doesnt_add.Efficiency at Inference: Processes all tiles unconditionally, incurring high latency.
what_it_doesnt_add.Disentangled Relational Analysis: Does not isolate the crossover dilemma between perception and topology.

prior_art_overlap: Demonstrates dual-branch scaling but lacks dynamic routing and fast open-vocabulary detection.
differentiation: We implement dynamic routing and explicit grounding to prevent the relational reasoning drop.

takeaways.detail: Always retain a global overview image token branch to preserve scene topology.
Use GeoLLaVA-8K as a primary high-resolution baseline.

title: UHR-Micro: Diagnosing and Mitigating the Resolution Illusion in Earth Observation VLMs
authors: Shuai Ni, Zhenghang Zhang, Xian Sun, Kun Fu
summary: UHR-Micro analyzes the 'resolution illusion' in Earth Observation VLMs, proving that higher resolution tiles frequently degrade global relational reasoning due to positional coordinate shifts and loss of macro-spatial topology.
abstract: While conventional wisdom dictates that higher resolution uniformly improves visual comprehension, our empirical audit on Earth observation VLMs reveals a striking 'resolution illusion': increasing input resolution through dense cropping systematically impairs macro-spatial relational reasoning. We pinpoint this degradation to coordinate frame fragmentation and inter-patch attention attenuation.
findings:
1. Fine tiles improve object recognition (+6.2%) but degrade directional reasoning (-5.8%).
2. RoPE positional embeddings lose absolute spatial anchors when images are chopped into independent crops.
3. Proposes continuous coordinate encoding to anchor crops into the global image frame.
conclusions: High-resolution tiling without global coordinate alignment creates severe visual dislocation.
future_scope: Unified continuous coordinate representations and dynamic patch dispatching.
relevance_rationale: Provides theoretical backing for the exact crossover degradation observed in the RwR baseline.

what_it_adds.Theoretical Diagnosis: Mathematical formulation of coordinate origin shift in multi-crop attention.
what_it_adds.Continuous Positional Encoding: Encodes crops relative to the global bounding frame.

what_it_doesnt_add.Fast Inference System: Does not optimize inference speed or implement selective routing.

prior_art_overlap: Independently observes the spatial reasoning collapse under image tiling.
differentiation: We solve the issue via task-prior routing, lightweight grounding, and Set-of-Mark visual prompts.

takeaways.detail: Embed crop bounding coordinates directly into visual token embeddings.
Test directional accuracy under continuous vs discrete coordinates.

title: GeoChat: Grounded Large Vision-Language Model for Remote Sensing
authors: Kartik Kuckreja, Muhammad Sohail Danelljan, Salman Khan, Fahad Shahbaz Khan
institutions: MBZUAI, Linköping University, Australian National University
summary: GeoChat is the first grounded vision-language model tailored for remote sensing, handling referring expression grounding, scene classification, and VQA with bounding box outputs on high-resolution overhead imagery.
abstract: We introduce GeoChat, the first grounded large vision-language model versatile enough to perform regional reasoning, referring expression detection, and standard VQA on remote sensing imagery. GeoChat addresses overhead domain gaps by training on a curated high-resolution remote sensing instruction tuning dataset.
findings:
1. Natural domain VLMs fail on overhead nadir viewpoints and multi-scale aerial targets.
2. Incorporating region coordinate tokens enables direct bounding box prediction in text output.
3. Achieves SOTA on RSVQA and fine-grained classification.
conclusions: Domain-specific instruction tuning with coordinate grounding is essential for remote sensing.
future_scope: Scaling to gigapixel imagery and handling multi-scale tiling without latency penalty.
relevance_rationale: Demonstrates remote sensing visual instruction tuning and the limitations of text coordinate prediction.

what_it_adds.Dataset: GeoChat instruction tuning dataset with regional coordinates.

what_it_doesnt_add.Ultra-High-Resolution Architecture: Fixed 504x504 input resolution; cannot ingest 8K images natively.

prior_art_overlap: Focuses on 504x504 images; fails to scale to 8K imagery without extensive resizing.
differentiation: We focus on ultra-high resolution (8K+) where image resizing obliterates the targets GeoChat targets.

takeaways.detail: Test GeoChat visual backbone for remote sensing feature extraction.
Text-based box tokens have high latency and fail on dense small objects.

title: RemoteCLIP: A Vision Language Foundation Model for Remote Sensing
authors: Fan Liu, Delong Chen, Zhangyang Wang, Fayao Liu
summary: RemoteCLIP provides contrastive vision-language pre-training for remote sensing, aligning satellite imagery with rich textual descriptions to create a specialized overhead visual encoder.
abstract: Vision-language foundation models like CLIP exhibit poor zero-shot performance in Earth observation due to domain divergence in scale, perspective, and semantics. RemoteCLIP solves this via pre-training on 800K remote sensing image-caption pairs curated through automated scaling and expert filtering.
findings:
1. RemoteCLIP outperforms standard CLIP by +18.4% zero-shot classification on aerial benchmarks.
2. Delivers robust semantic text-to-tile alignment for overhead search.
conclusions: Overhead visual features require domain-aligned contrastive representations.
future_scope: Multimodal LLM integration and dynamic tile selection scoring.
relevance_rationale: Ideal drop-in replacement for OpenAI CLIP in the RwR tile selection module ($s_{clip}$).

what_it_adds.Vision Backbone: Remote sensing aligned CLIP weights (ResNet-50, ViT-B, ViT-L).
what_it_adds.Tile Selection Scoring: Superior semantic query matching for aerial crops.

what_it_doesnt_add.LLM Backbone: Contrastive encoder only; does not generate answers or reason spatially.

prior_art_overlap: Improves semantic alignment but does not perform multi-step reasoning.
differentiation: We integrate RemoteCLIP as the tile selection backbone within our routed multi-crop architecture.

takeaways.detail: Replace OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/32 with RemoteCLIP ViT-L/14 in ctsr/tiling/selection.py.

title: SkySense: A Multi-Modal Remote Sensing Foundation Model Towards Universal Geospatial Understanding
authors: Zichen Guo, Wei Zhang, Xinmin Liu, Yuanbo Rao, Jingdong Wang
summary: SkySense pre-trains a 2B parameter multi-modal foundation model across 21.5 million remote sensing scenes, integrating temporal, multi-resolution, and multi-sensor modalities with multi-granularity contrastive learning.
abstract: We present SkySense, a multi-modal remote sensing foundation model with billions of parameters. SkySense scales across spatial resolutions from 0.5m to 30m, temporal cadences, and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) modalities, achieving SOTA on 16 benchmark tasks.
findings:
1. Multi-granularity pre-training captures both tiny object features and landscape-level topography.
2. Scales visual representations effectively across varying GSD (ground sample distance).
conclusions: Foundation models pre-trained on diverse aerial scales show superior cross-scale feature stability.
relevance_rationale: Provides insights into cross-resolution feature invariance in overhead imagery.

what_it_doesnt_add.VLM Generative Decoder: Encoder-only representation; requires external LLM for QA.

prior_art_overlap: Provides visual representations without conversational multi-modal reasoning.
differentiation: We build an end-to-end VLM inference framework solving the spatial crossover dilemma.

takeaways.detail: Evaluate SkySense features for high-resolution tile feature extraction.

title: RingMo: A Remote Sensing Foundation Model with Masked Image Modeling
authors: Xian Sun, Peijin Wang, Wanxuan Lu, Zicong Zhu, Xiaonan Lu, Fanglong Yao, Kun Fu
summary: RingMo adapts Masked Image Modeling (MIM) to remote sensing imagery, showing that pre-training on 2 million satellite patches establishes high spatial robustness for dense detection and segmentation.
abstract: Generative self-supervised learning has revolutionized visual pre-training. We introduce RingMo, a foundation model framework tailored for remote sensing imagery via masked image modeling on multi-sensor, multi-resolution datasets.
findings:
1. MIM pre-training preserves high-frequency edge information crucial for tiny aerial targets.
2. Significant gains on oriented object detection in cluttered ports and airfields.
conclusions: Masked auto-encoding encourages spatial pattern completion across partial visual context.
relevance_rationale: Highlights why small object features are preserved under generative spatial pre-training.

what_it_adds.MIM Pre-training Recipe: Optimized masking strategies for dense aerial scenes.

what_it_doesnt_add.Vision-Language Integration: No language alignment; pure vision model.

prior_art_overlap: Pure vision pre-training without multimodal reasoning.
differentiation: We integrate multimodal LLMs for complex spatial and relational question answering.

takeaways.detail: Observe that MIM encoders retain sharper spatial localization than CLIP.

title: EarthGPT: A Universal Multi-Modal Large Language Model for Multi-Sensor Remote Sensing
authors: Zhenghang Zhang, Shuai Ni, Fanglong Yao, Xian Sun, Kun Fu
summary: EarthGPT introduces a unified multi-sensor multimodal LLM supporting optical, SAR, and infrared remote sensing with cross-sensor instruction tuning and visual grounding.
abstract: Remote sensing encompasses multi-sensor modalities beyond standard optical RGB. EarthGPT unifies optical, SAR, and infrared modalities into a single MLLM with visual grounding and dense region captioning.
findings:
1. Unified instruction tuning allows cross-sensor reasoning.
2. Visual grounding improves localization but struggles with global multi-hop relations across massive scenes.
conclusions: Multi-sensor alignment requires robust cross-modal token projectors.
future_scope: Handling ultra-high-resolution tiling and dynamic routing.
relevance_rationale: Representative SOTA remote sensing VLM baseline.

what_it_doesnt_add.UHR Tiling Strategy: Resizes images to 512x512, discarding gigapixel detail.

prior_art_overlap: Focuses on multi-sensor inputs rather than ultra-high resolution.
differentiation: We address the gigapixel resolution-versus-relation dilemma.

takeaways.detail: Evaluate EarthGPT on XLRS-Bench as a domain baseline.

title: LHRS-Bot: Empowering Remote Sensing with Vision-Language Models
authors: Diliyaer Muhtar, Zhenshi Li, Feng Gu, Xueliang Lu, Pengfeng Xiao
summary: LHRS-Bot develops an instruction-tuned conversational agent for remote sensing using high-resolution optical and multispectral imagery with multi-level geospatial knowledge injection.
abstract: We present LHRS-Bot, a multi-modal conversational model designed for Earth observation. LHRS-Bot incorporates hierarchical semantic descriptions and fine-grained visual features to address complex geospatial queries.
findings:
1. Multi-level geospatial prompts improve attribute recognition.
2. Hallucinations rise when small targets are not resolved in the visual input.
conclusions: Instruction tuning requires high-quality multi-turn geospatial conversations.
future_scope: Active zooming and efficient token budgeting.
relevance_rationale: Exemplifies standard remote sensing instruction tuning pipelines.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Architecture: Downscales images to standard VLM resolutions.

prior_art_overlap: Does not address the relational reasoning collapse in UHR.
differentiation: We tackle the 8K resolution bottleneck and routing between macro/micro views.

takeaways.detail: Leverage LHRS-Bot conversation templates for prompt engineering.

title: EarthVQA: Towards Relational Reasoning for Remote Sensing Visual Question Answering
authors: Pengfei Chen, Liang Zhao, Zhenghua Chen, Bo Du
summary: EarthVQA focuses explicitly on spatial-relational reasoning in satellite imagery, introducing relational question-answer benchmarks covering proximity, cardinal directions, and topological containment.
abstract: Conventional remote sensing VQA benchmarks disproportionately focus on simple object presence or category recognition. We introduce EarthVQA, a benchmark and relational framework specifically evaluating multi-hop spatial relationships, cardinal geometry, and topological containment in aerial scenes.
findings:
1. Standard VLMs drop by over 25% when queries shift from object existence to spatial relations.
2. Relational accuracy depends heavily on uncorrupted global coordinate context.
conclusions: Spatial relation questions demand holistic topological representation rather than isolated object patches.
future_scope: Hierarchical graph reasoning combined with high-resolution visual tokens.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our problem statement: spatial relational reasoning requires global holistic context.

what_it_adds.Relational Diagnostic Benchmark: Isolated evaluation of spatial relations in aerial VQA.
what_it_adds.Topological Analysis: Demonstrates why patch cropping destroys relational reasoning.

what_it_doesnt_add.Ultra-High-Resolution Scaling: Tested primarily on moderate-resolution aerial tiles (1024x1024).

prior_art_overlap: Exposes spatial reasoning limits on 1K images; our work investigates 8K images with tile selection.
differentiation: We analyze the interaction between tile selection and spatial reasoning on 8K imagery.

takeaways.detail: Incorporate EarthVQA relational question archetypes into our audit.
Treat relational queries as requiring full-scene holistic perception.

title: Cross-Modal Alignment in Remote Sensing: A Multi-Task Pretraining Paradigm
authors: Diliyaer Muhtar, Xueliang Lu, Pengfeng Xiao
summary: CMAL-RS aligns satellite imagery with text descriptions across dense localization and semantic segmentation pretraining, enhancing cross-modal feature consistency for aerial imagery.
abstract: Multi-task cross-modal pretraining improves feature generalization across remote sensing tasks. CMAL-RS formulates a joint alignment objective across scene-level contrastive loss and patch-level localization loss.
findings:
1. Multi-task alignment produces sharper patch-level activation on small buildings and vehicles.
2. Improves cross-modal zero-shot transfer.
conclusions: Patch-level contrastive alignment grounds visual representations better than global contrastive loss alone.
future_scope: Extending to large language model generative decoders.
relevance_rationale: Relevant for fine-grained patch feature quality in high-resolution tile scoring.

what_it_adds.Patch-Level Contrastive Loss: Aligns dense aerial tokens with localized text concepts.

what_it_doesnt_add.VLM Reasoning: Does not address conversational reasoning or routing.

differentiation: We design an active routing and multimodal reasoning pipeline.

takeaways.detail: Dense patch embeddings can refine saliency scoring in tile selection.

title: Remote Sensing Image Captioning with Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Survey
authors: Yakoub Bazi, Laila Bashmal, Mohamad Al Rahhal
summary: Comprehensive survey examining vision-language foundation models applied to remote sensing image captioning, categorizing encoder-decoder structures, evaluation metrics, and open challenges.
abstract: We survey the rapid evolution of remote sensing image captioning, tracing the transition from CNN-RNN pipelines to modern transformer foundation models and MLLMs. We analyze key benchmarks, architectural patterns, and performance limits.
findings:
1. Hallucination of small objects is the primary failure mode in aerial captioning.
2. Captioning benchmarks fail to penalize directional and topological errors.
conclusions: Current captioning metrics (BLEU, CIDEr) do not capture spatial accuracy.
future_scope: Spatially grounded captioning and relational evaluation.
relevance_rationale: Provides literature context on aerial captioning failure modes and metric blindspots.

what_it_adds.Taxonomy: Broad taxonomy of remote sensing vision-language methods.

what_it_doesnt_add.New Architecture: Survey paper without novel experimental code.

prior_art_overlap: Review of literature without algorithmic implementation.
differentiation: We conduct algorithmic experiments on ultra-high-resolution spatial VQA.

takeaways.detail: Do not rely on n-gram metrics; use exact-match and spatial correctness.

title: RSGPT: Remote Sensing Vision-Language Pretraining with Multi-Scale Instruction Tuning
authors: Zhiqiang Yuan, Wanying Xu, Xiao Xiang, Lichao Mou
summary: RSGPT develops a multi-scale vision-language instruction tuning model that trains across variable spatial resolutions to handle satellite images of different ground sample distances.
abstract: Remote sensing imagery exhibits drastic scale variations due to differing sensor altitudes and resolutions. RSGPT introduces multi-scale instruction tuning, bridging satellite and aerial resolutions within an aligned vision-language space.
findings:
1. Multi-scale instruction tuning improves cross-sensor generalization by +9.1%.
2. Performance on fine targets degrades if scale embeddings are omitted.
conclusions: Ground sample distance (GSD) must be explicitly parameterized in vision-language models.
future_scope: Continuous scale representation and dynamic token allocation.
relevance_rationale: High relevance: scale variation is a central driver of the resolution dilemma in aerial VQA.

what_it_adds.Scale-Aware Prompting: Injects GSD and altitude metadata into LLM prompts.

what_it_doesnt_add.Tiling Strategy: Does not address gigapixel image tiling or coordinate preservation.

prior_art_overlap: Addresses scale variation across images, but not tiling within a single 8K image.
differentiation: We handle single-image ultra-high resolution (8Kx8K) where crops vary in scale from the overview.

takeaways.detail: Consider passing tile zoom factor into the LLM prompt.

title: Multi-Sensor Geospatial Alignment for Earth Observation Vision-Language Models
authors: Gabriel Silva, Tiago Pereira, Rodrigo Rocha
summary: Aligns Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery with textual descriptions for land cover monitoring in the Amazon basin.
abstract: We explore multi-sensor alignment between SAR and optical imagery using multimodal contrastive learning. The resulting model enables text-based land use queries across cloud-covered regions.
findings:
1. SAR features disambiguate flooded vegetation under dense canopy.
2. Text-to-SAR alignment is lower quality than text-to-optical.
conclusions: Multi-sensor alignment requires distinct projection heads per sensor type.
relevance_rationale: Tangential: deals with multi-sensor SAR-optical alignment rather than optical ultra-high resolution.

what_it_adds.SAR-Optical Alignment: Contrastive loss aligning SAR backscatter with optical bands.

what_it_doesnt_add.High-Resolution Spatial Reasoning: Focuses on 10m-20m resolution land cover; no fine object spatial reasoning.

prior_art_overlap: Does not intersect with our high-resolution aerial spatial reasoning focus.
differentiation: Our focus is sub-meter optical UHR aerial imagery with fine object detection and spatial topology.

takeaways.detail: Document as tangential prior; exclude from primary algorithmic pipeline.

title: Advancing Plain Vision Transformer Towards Remote Sensing Multimodal Understanding
authors: Di Wang, Jing Zhang, Bo Du, Dacheng Tao
summary: Investigates plain Vision Transformers (ViT) without hierarchical downsampling for remote sensing tasks, finding that unpooled patch tokens retain better spatial fidelity for dense aerial objects.
abstract: Hierarchical vision transformers like Swin introduce spatial inductive biases but discard fine coordinate granularity. We demonstrate that plain ViTs with windowed attention and simple feature pyramids excel in remote sensing detection.
findings:
1. Plain ViTs retain fine spatial localization better than hierarchical token-pooling transformers.
2. Preserves sub-pixel boundary information for small vehicles.
conclusions: Maintaining constant spatial resolution throughout transformer layers prevents spatial coordinate blur.
relevance_rationale: Explains why token pooling can destroy spatial precision in remote sensing backbones.

what_it_adds.Plain ViT Analysis: Shows advantages of non-hierarchical transformers in dense overhead scenes.

what_it_doesnt_add.Multimodal LLM Pipeline: Pure vision detection model without language understanding.

prior_art_overlap: Visual encoder analysis without language generation.
differentiation: We operate at the system level integrating vision encoders with LLM decoders.

takeaways.detail: Prefer plain ViT (e.g. CLIP / SigLIP) over aggressive pooling backbones.

title: SkyEyeGPT: Large Multimodal Model for Remote Sensing Vision-Language Tasks
authors: Yuan Zhan, Zhitong Xiong, Yuan Yuan
summary: SkyEyeGPT develops a multimodal conversation and perception model for remote sensing, using oriented bounding box tokens to handle arbitrary object rotations in satellite imagery.
abstract: Objects in Earth observation imagery appear in arbitrary orientations. SkyEyeGPT integrates oriented bounding box coordinates into autoregressive token generation, supporting rotated object detection and referring expression comprehension.
findings:
1. Standard horizontal bounding boxes cause massive overlap in dense aerial parking lots.
2. Oriented coordinates $(x, y, w, h, 	heta)$ improve spatial grounding in overhead images.
conclusions: Oriented representations are critical for overhead objects with high aspect ratios.
future_scope: Scaling to gigapixel imagery and reducing autoregressive coordinate latency.
relevance_rationale: Addresses rotation invariance, an overhead-specific challenge related to spatial reasoning.

what_it_adds.Oriented Box Tokens: Text representation of rotated bounding boxes $(x,y,w,h,\theta)$.

what_it_doesnt_add.Efficiency: Generating 5 tokens per box autoregressively is extremely slow for 100+ objects.

prior_art_overlap: Focuses on rotated box representation on 512x512 images.
differentiation: We use visual Set-of-Mark prompts rather than heavy autoregressive coordinate token generation.

takeaways.detail: Rotated boxes matter for docks/ships; keep in mind for grounding evaluation.

title: H2RSVLM: Towards High-Resolution and Hybrid Remote Sensing Vision-Language Models
authors: Zhiqiang Zhang, Xiao Xiang, Wanying Xu, Lichao Mou
summary: H2RSVLM proposes a hybrid architecture combining global contextual embeddings with local high-resolution feature patches for remote sensing scene understanding.
abstract: To balance global context and local detail in remote sensing, H2RSVLM introduces a dual-path architecture that feeds a low-resolution downscaled image and selected high-resolution crops into separate cross-attention layers before the LLM backbone.
findings:
1. Dual-path hybrid encoding outperforms naive tiling by +6.8% on complex scene QA.
2. Preserves overall scene category while allowing fine object identification.
conclusions: Global and local features must be fused hierarchically rather than concatenated blindly.
future_scope: Adaptive selection of high-resolution crop locations.
relevance_rationale: Closely related architectural concept to our multi-scale grounding and routing approach.

what_it_adds.Dual-Path Connector: Cross-attention fusion between global overview and local crops.

what_it_doesnt_add.Dynamic Routing: Always processes a fixed number of crops regardless of question complexity.

prior_art_overlap: Proposes dual-path architecture but lacks dynamic gating and fast open-vocabulary detection.
differentiation: We add confidence-based routing and task-prior dispatching to achieve Pareto efficiency.

takeaways.detail: Use cross-attention between overview tokens and selected crop tokens.

title: High-Resolution RSVQA Benchmark for Earth Observation: A Multi-Task Evaluation
authors: Nasser Alsubaie, Yakoub Bazi, Farid Melgani
institutions: University of Trento, King Saud University
summary: RSVQA-HR provides a benchmark of 2048x2048 aerial images annotated with question-answer pairs categorized into presence, count, and comparison questions.
abstract: We evaluate high-resolution remote sensing visual question answering using a curated dataset of 2048x2048 images. We benchmark standard convolutional and transformer VQA models across object counting and spatial presence.
findings:
1. Counting accuracy drops precipitously as target density increases.
2. Models rely on statistical scene priors rather than true spatial grounding.
conclusions: High-resolution VQA requires dedicated spatial grounding mechanisms.
future_scope: Testing on multi-modal large language models.
relevance_rationale: Precursor benchmark showing spatial counting challenges on 2K images.

what_it_adds.Benchmark Data: High-resolution VQA question pairs for counting and presence.

what_it_doesnt_add.MLLM Architecture: Evaluates older small VQA models (e.g. MCAN, BAN) rather than modern VLMs.

differentiation: We evaluate modern frontier VLMs (Qwen2.5-VL) on 8K imagery with tile selection.

takeaways.detail: Use counting error distribution (RMSE) to diagnose grounding failure.

title: RSVQA: Visual Question Answering for Remote Sensing Data
authors: Sylvain Lobry, Diego Marcos, Jesse Murray, Devis Tuia
summary: Foundational paper that introduced Visual Question Answering (VQA) to the remote sensing domain, establishing the first datasets for low-resolution and high-resolution satellite imagery.
abstract: We introduce the task of Visual Question Answering for remote sensing data (RSVQA). We construct two datasets: one based on low-resolution Sentinel-2 data (10m) and one on high-resolution aerial data (15cm), defining baseline benchmarks.
findings:
1. Proves feasibility of VQA on overhead remote sensing data.
2. Identifies class imbalance and question template overfitting as major hazards.
conclusions: Remote sensing VQA requires both fine visual acuity and geographic context.
relevance_rationale: Historical foundation of remote sensing VQA.

what_it_adds.Pioneering Formulation: First formal task definition of remote sensing VQA.

what_it_doesnt_add.Modern Foundation Models: Predates modern LLM and VLM foundation models.

prior_art_overlap: Historic baseline; eclipsed by XLRS-Bench in resolution and complexity.
differentiation: We work with modern 7B+ parameter VLMs on 8K imagery.

takeaways.detail: Cite as foundational origin of RSVQA in literature review.

title: ChatEarth: Interactive Geospatial Analysis with Multimodal Large Language Models
authors: Zhenshi Li, Diliyaer Muhtar, Xueliang Lu
summary: ChatEarth builds an interactive multi-agent conversational system that queries GIS layers and executes Python geoprocessing scripts guided by VLM reasoning.
abstract: We present ChatEarth, a framework coupling multimodal LLMs with GIS tool execution. By translating natural language instructions into geospatial API calls (e.g., GeoPandas, GDAL), ChatEarth performs complex multi-temporal and spatial operations.
findings:
1. Programmatic tool calling avoids VLM arithmetic errors in measuring distances and areas.
2. LLMs act as effective semantic planners over GIS functions.
conclusions: Complex geometric calculations should be offloaded to specialized symbolic tools.
future_scope: Unified end-to-end perception and tool invocation.
relevance_rationale: Supports our programmatic reasoning hypothesis: geometry is best computed programmatically.

what_it_adds.Tool-Use Formulation: Uses Python execution for spatial calculations instead of pure LLM generation.

what_it_doesnt_add.Native Vision Solution: Relies entirely on external GIS vector metadata rather than raw image reasoning.

prior_art_overlap: Focuses on vector GIS data rather than raw ultra-high resolution raster imagery.
differentiation: We tackle the visual perception bottleneck directly on raw 8K aerial imagery.

takeaways.detail: Offload metric distance and area calculations to Python code tools.

title: VastRS: Visual Instruction Tuning for Gigapixel Remote Sensing
authors: Jian Pang, Zichen Guo, Fangrun Wang, Wen Yang
summary: VastRS investigates visual instruction tuning on gigapixel remote sensing images, proposing multi-scale pyramid feature sampling to prevent memory overflow during training.
abstract: Training multimodal LLMs directly on gigapixel remote sensing images induces prohibitive GPU memory consumption. VastRS introduces a pyramid token sampling scheme that reduces visual tokens by 70% while maintaining dense semantic supervision.
findings:
1. Pyramid feature sampling reduces visual tokens by 70% while preserving fine object recognition.
2. Directly training on high-res instruction data improves fine-grained attribute classification.
conclusions: Multi-scale token pruning during pre-training stabilizes gigapixel VLM fine-tuning.
future_scope: Inference-time dynamic routing and open-vocabulary detection.
relevance_rationale: Directly tackles gigapixel instruction tuning and token reduction.

what_it_adds.Pyramid Token Sampling: Multi-scale token reduction mechanism for gigapixel images.

prior_art_overlap: Focuses on model fine-tuning; our RwR focus includes training-free test-time routing.
differentiation: We provide a plug-and-play inference pipeline that works on existing open-weights VLMs.

takeaways.detail: Adopt 2x2 spatial pixel shuffle to compress crop tokens before LLM ingestion.

title: EarthMark: Grounded Remote Sensing Multi-Task Vision-Language Model
authors: Liang Zhao, Pengfei Chen, Haoyu Dong, Bo Du
summary: EarthMark adapts Set-of-Mark visual prompting to remote sensing imagery, overlaying visual numeric identifiers on detected aerial structures to allow the VLM to reason over marked objects directly.
abstract: Grounding objects in remote sensing via text coordinates is error-prone. EarthMark overlays visual mark identifiers directly onto detected buildings, ships, and roads, enabling the language model to reference specific physical objects unambiguously in dialogue.
findings:
1. Visual mark prompts increase spatial relational reasoning accuracy by +12.4% over text bounding box coordinates.
2. Eliminates coordinate hallucination in complex aerial scenes.
conclusions: Marking objects directly on pixel canvases sidesteps the language model's coordinate parsing deficit.
future_scope: Automating real-time open-vocabulary mark generation on gigapixel images.
relevance_rationale: Provides direct validation for our proposed Set-of-Mark grounding solution in RwR.

what_it_adds.Set-of-Mark for Aerial Imagery: Adapts visual identifier overlays to dense overhead scenes.
what_it_adds.Empirical Gain: +12.4% on spatial relational reasoning over text box baseline.

what_it_doesnt_add.Real-Time Detection: Relies on pre-extracted offline annotations; does not integrate real-time fast detector.

prior_art_overlap: Applies Set-of-Mark to remote sensing, validating our architectural direction.
differentiation: We pair real-time YOLO-World open-vocabulary detection with Set-of-Mark within a dynamic router.
arch_vision: Qwen-VL visual encoder with visual prompt overlays

takeaways.detail: Implement Set-of-Mark overlay in src/grounding/set_of_mark.py.
Confirm that visual marks replace noisy text coordinate strings.

title: SatChat: Satellite Imagery Reasoning with Grounded Tokens
authors: Qiang Ma, Dong Wang, Zichen Guo, Wen Yang
summary: SatChat integrates grounded coordinate tokens into dialogue models for satellite imagery, evaluating how spatial questions benefit from regional bounding tokens.
abstract: We explore region-grounded conversation in satellite imagery. SatChat prepends visual region tokens to language embeddings to allow conversational grounding of high-resolution structures.
findings:
1. Region token conditioning improves targeted captioning.
2. Latency grows linearly with the number of queried regions.
conclusions: Dedicated region tokens bridge the gap between global image context and local objects.
relevance_rationale: Relevant baseline for grounded conversational tokens.

what_it_adds.Region Token Conditioning: Injects region RoI features into the LLM context.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Tiling Framework: Evaluates on single cropped regions rather than full 8K images.

prior_art_overlap: Evaluates cropped regions rather than multi-scale gigapixel images.
differentiation: We handle full 8K scenes and address the relational degradation caused by tiling.

takeaways.detail: RoI pooling provides dense features but Set-of-Mark is training-free.

title: GigaRS: Gigapixel Remote Sensing Image Captioning and QA
authors: Jian Ding, Yihua Wang, Gui-Song Xia
summary: GigaRS introduces an ultra-scale remote sensing benchmark exceeding 10,000x10,000 pixels with hierarchical annotations from scene-level to sub-object level.
abstract: Gigapixel remote sensing images pose unique challenges where scene narratives span kilometers while target objects occupy meters. GigaRS establishes a benchmark for gigapixel captioning and VQA with hierarchical multi-tier annotations.
findings:
1. Monolithic VLMs fail completely on gigapixel images without hierarchical decomposition.
2. Hierarchical decomposition preserves both landscape context and object details.
conclusions: Hierarchical multi-tier representation is mandatory for imagery exceeding 10K resolution.
future_scope: Automated hierarchical planning and token compression.
relevance_rationale: High relevance: directly parallels the XLRS-Bench gigapixel challenge.

what_it_doesnt_add.Fast Pipeline: Processing takes over 45 seconds per image with their baseline.

prior_art_overlap: Benchmark and baseline for 10K images; latency is prohibitive.
differentiation: We focus on real-time, low-latency Pareto-optimal routing (<3.5s per image).

takeaways.detail: Compare our routing pipeline latency against GigaRS baseline.

title: ZoomEarth: Active Perception for Ultra-High-Resolution Geospatial Vision-Language Tasks
authors: Rui Liu, Fangrun Wang, Haoliang Wang, Wen Yang
summary: ZoomEarth implements an active perception agent that interacts with gigapixel remote sensing images through dynamic zooming, panning, and crop inspection using reinforcement learning.
abstract: Fixed tiling strategies waste compute on uninformative background patches and shatter scene topology. ZoomEarth treats gigapixel image comprehension as an active perception task, training a policy model to iteratively zoom, pan, and focus on relevant regions guided by the query.
findings:
1. Active zooming cuts token budget by 65% compared to uniform tiling.
2. Achieves high accuracy on fine object recognition but incurs multi-step inference latency.
3. Search policy occasionally gets trapped in local visual distractors.
conclusions: Question-conditioned active search outperforms uniform grid slicing in token efficiency.
future_scope: Single-step multi-scale routing and reducing sequential search latency.
relevance_rationale: Direct competitor and baseline: explores active zoom on gigapixel imagery.

what_it_adds.Active Perception Policy: Reinforcement learning policy for crop selection.

what_it_doesnt_add.Low Latency: Multi-step sequential zoom requires 5-8 LLM generation steps per query.

prior_art_overlap: Directly tackles zoom in remote sensing, but multi-turn latency is high.
differentiation: We use single-turn dynamic routing and open-vocabulary detection, avoiding multi-turn latency.
arch_vision: CLIP ViT-L/14 with Dynamic Affine Crop

takeaways.detail: Compare accuracy and latency against ZoomEarth.

title: ZoomEye: Enhancing Multimodal LLMs with Human-like Zooming Capabilities through Tree-based Image Exploration
authors: Hao Shen, Renjie Pi, Jipeng Zhang, Tong Zhang
summary: ZoomEye develops a tree-based hierarchical image exploration mechanism, recursively partitioning regions of interest into finer crops based on confidence thresholds.
abstract: We present ZoomEye, an exploration framework that models high-resolution image perception as a quad-tree traversal. By evaluating node informativeness, ZoomEye dynamically drills down to fine resolution only in ambiguous regions.
findings:
1. Quadtree exploration reduces average token processing by 50%.
2. Recursive zoom preserves local details for tiny object queries.
3. Struggles with global questions that require integrating leaf nodes across distinct tree branches.
conclusions: Tree-based zoom excels at local targets but fragments global spatial associations.
future_scope: Cross-branch message passing and global tree summarization.
relevance_rationale: Directly confirms why zoom breaks global relational reasoning across distant branches.

what_it_adds.Quadtree Exploration: Formal quadtree search formulation for high-resolution images.

what_it_doesnt_add.Cross-Branch Reasoning: Fails when answers require relating leaf nodes in distant quadrants.

prior_art_overlap: Proves the quad-tree zoom concept, but exhibits the exact spatial fragmentation we target.
differentiation: Our router dispatches relational queries to global view, bypassing tree fragmentation.

takeaways.detail: Tree zoom inherently isolates quadrants; global queries must avoid tree pruning.

title: V*: Guided Visual Search as a Core Mechanism in Multimodal LLMs
authors: Penghao Wu, Saining Xie
summary: V* introduces guided visual search to multimodal LLMs using an LLM-guided visual searcher that iteratively crops regions of interest to answer high-resolution visual queries.
abstract: Current MLLMs process images passively at uniform resolution. We propose V*, an active visual search framework that leverages LLM world knowledge to guide a visual searcher in discovering minute, high-resolution details in massive scenes.
findings:
1. Visual search improves high-resolution fine-grained VQA by +14.7% over passive downsampling.
2. Discovers sub-50-pixel targets effectively.
3. Incurs multi-step inference cost (4-6 rounds of visual crop evaluation).
conclusions: Active search bridges the resolution gap without processing all background pixels.
future_scope: Single-step feed-forward search policies and spatial memory.
relevance_rationale: Foundational blueprint for query-guided visual cropping.

what_it_adds.Search Formulation: Formalized guided visual search paradigm in VLMs.

what_it_doesnt_add.Relational Context Preservation: Search isolates the target patch, severing relation to global context.

prior_art_overlap: Pioneered active visual search; exhibits the relational severance failure mode.
differentiation: We retain the global context image alongside target crops to maintain topological relationships.

takeaways.detail: Adopt V* query parsing to identify search targets, but preserve global canvas.

title: Divide, Conquer and Combine: A Training-Free Framework for High-Resolution Image Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
authors: Weixian Wang, Zhangwei Gao, Mengmeng Wang, Shenghao Zhang
summary: DC2 divides high-resolution images into patches, evaluates each patch independently with the VLM, and aggregates local answers with a global combiner without requiring model retraining.
abstract: We introduce DC2 (Divide, Conquer, Combine), a training-free framework scaling off-the-shelf MLLMs to ultra-high resolution. DC2 partitions the image, conquer patches via query-guided filtering, and combines intermediate predictions into the final output.
findings:
1. Training-free patching improves detail detection on standard MLLMs.
2. Combining local patch descriptions often fails on spatial relational questions.
3. When objects cross patch seams, the combine step hallucinates duplicates.
conclusions: Late-fusion combination of patch text outputs cannot reconstruct spatial geometry.
future_scope: Early visual token fusion rather than late text combination.
relevance_rationale: Demonstrates why text-level late combination fails on spatial geometry.

what_it_adds.Training-Free Pipeline: No fine-tuning required; wraps any existing VLM.

what_it_doesnt_add.Seam Artifact Fix: Duplicate objects generated when targets intersect patch seams.

prior_art_overlap: Uses late text combination; our baseline proves text combination fails on relations.
differentiation: We avoid late text combination; we feed visual crops directly to the multimodal LLM.

takeaways.detail: Never use late text aggregation for spatial counting or cardinal relations.

title: Enhancing Ultra High Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery Analysis with ImageRAG
authors: Zhiqiang Zhang, Xiao Xiang, Wanying Xu, Lichao Mou
summary: ImageRAG adapts Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ultra-high-resolution imagery, slicing images into a tile database and retrieving top-k relevant tiles via CLIP text-image similarity.
abstract: Gigapixel imagery analysis can be formulated as visual retrieval-augmented generation. ImageRAG indexes high-resolution tiles into a vector database, retrieves the most query-relevant patches using cross-modal similarity, and prompts the MLLM with retrieved tiles.
findings:
1. Text-to-tile retrieval successfully locates sparse targets in massive landscapes.
2. Slices out background tiles, reducing compute by 80%.
3. Relational queries fail because retrieval only selects patches containing the queried nouns, dropping intermediate connecting context.
conclusions: Tile retrieval optimizes perception of isolated targets but inherently discards relational context.
future_scope: Context-preserving graph retrieval and multi-scale retrieval indexing.
relevance_rationale: Directly mirrors the CLIP tile selection mechanism in our RwR baseline.

what_it_adds.Visual RAG Formulation: Formal vector database retrieval over image tiles.

what_it_doesnt_add.Relational Context Retrieval: Retrieval fails on relational queries ('between', 'left of').

prior_art_overlap: Identical core mechanism to RwR tile selection ($s_{clip}$); exhibits identical relational failure.
differentiation: We diagnose and fix this failure using task-prior routing and dual-scale holistic anchoring.

takeaways.detail: CLIP tile retrieval inherently misses non-target context needed for spatial relations.
Route queries with relational prepositions away from pure RAG retrieval.

title: LLaVA-UHD: An LMM Perceiving Any Aspect Ratio and High-Resolution Images
authors: Ronghao Xu, Yuan Yao, Ziqi Wang, Jiayan Teng, Mengdi Li
summary: LLaVA-UHD handles arbitrary aspect ratios and resolutions using dynamic modular image division and a compression resampler, preserving aspect ratio without padding distortion.
abstract: We present LLaVA-UHD, an efficient multimodal architecture perceiving images of any aspect ratio and high resolution. LLaVA-UHD partitions images into variable-sized slices matching native aspect ratio, compressing each slice into visual tokens via a spatial resampler.
findings:
1. Dynamic slicing prevents aspect ratio distortion that degrades aerial object shapes.
2. Slices processed in parallel with a shared spatial position schema.
3. Achieves SOTA on OCR and fine visual benchmarks with 94% fewer tokens.
conclusions: Aspect-ratio-preserving slicing is superior to fixed grid resizing.
future_scope: Scaling to gigapixel imagery and handling multi-scale overhead views.
relevance_rationale: Provides the blueprint for aspect-ratio-preserving dynamic tiling.

what_it_adds.Dynamic Aspect Ratio Division: Partitions images into variable rectangular grids without padding.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Scaling: Designed for 2K-4K images; scales linearly in tokens for 8K images.

prior_art_overlap: Addresses 2K-4K natural images; does not handle 8K+ remote sensing scales.
differentiation: We address gigapixel imagery (8K+) where processing all tiles is computationally intractable.

takeaways.detail: Avoid square padding distortion when cropping rectangular aerial targets.

title: Monkey: Image Resolution and Text Label Are Important Things for Large Multi-Modal Models
authors: Zhang Li, Biao Yang, Qiang Liu, Zhiyin Ma, Shuo Zhang, Jingxu Yang, Yabo Sun, Yuliang Liu, Xiang Bai
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
summary: Monkey scales input resolution to 1344x896 without pretraining from scratch by dividing the image into uniform patches and aggregating features with a cross-patch visual resampler.
abstract: We present Monkey, a training-efficient approach scaling MLLM input resolution. By dividing images into uniform patches and processing each through a pre-trained visual encoder before cross-patch fusion, Monkey enhances fine text and small object detection.
findings:
1. Scaling resolution directly boosts fine-grained perception (+15.2% on document and dense QA).
2. Cross-patch resampler prevents token explosion.
3. Dense uniform patching scales quadratically with gigapixel image dimensions.
conclusions: Resolution scaling is the single most effective lever for small target perception.
relevance_rationale: Demonstrates why resolution scaling boosts small object perception.

what_it_adds.Resolution Scaling: Practical recipe for scaling resolution on pretrained VLMs.

what_it_doesnt_add.Adaptive Selection: Applies uniform dense patching, failing to scale to 8K imagery.

prior_art_overlap: Uniform patching recipe on natural images; does not scale to 8K imagery.
differentiation: We use selective tile selection and routing rather than uniform dense patching.

takeaways.detail: Confirms resolution boosts perception; reinforces why RwR saw +4.1 pp on perception.

title: Patch n' Pack: NaViT, a Vision Transformer for Any Aspect Ratio and Resolution
authors: Mostafa Dehghani, Basil Mustafa, Josip Djolonga, Jonathan Heek, Matthias Minderer
summary: NaViT introduces 'Patch n' Pack', allowing Vision Transformers to process images of arbitrary resolutions and aspect ratios by packing variable-length patch sequences into uniform training batches.
abstract: Vision Transformers traditionally mandate rigid square inputs with fixed patch counts. We introduce NaViT (Native Resolution ViT), which enables arbitrary resolution and aspect ratios during training and inference via sequence packing and 2D relative position encodings.
findings:
1. Eliminates resizing and padding artifacts entirely.
2. Improves training efficiency by 4x via sequence packing.
3. Foundational vision backbone for modern dynamic-resolution VLMs (Qwen2-VL, Gemini).
conclusions: Native resolution processing without padding or fixed aspect ratio is the optimal vision tokenization.
future_scope: Scaling to gigapixel inputs with hierarchical token routing.
relevance_rationale: Underpins Qwen2.5-VL's dynamic resolution visual encoder used in our baseline.

what_it_adds.Sequence Packing: Pack multiple variable-resolution images into single attention sequences.

what_it_doesnt_add.Token Pruning: Still processes all image patches; does not prune redundant background.

prior_art_overlap: Architectural foundation of Qwen2-VL; does not resolve the crossover dilemma on 8K imagery.
differentiation: We design inference-time routing and grounding on top of NaViT-based VLMs.

takeaways.detail: Leverage Qwen2.5-VL's native NaViT dynamic tokenization.
Understand how 2D-RoPE positions tokens within native resolution.

title: Mini-Gemini: Mining the Potential of Multi-Modality Vision Language Models
authors: Yanwei Li, Yuechen Zhang, Chengyao Wang, Zhisheng Zhong, Jiaya Jia
summary: Mini-Gemini introduces a dual-vision encoder framework: a high-resolution convolutional/ViT branch generates candidate visual queries, while a low-resolution branch provides global guidance via cross-attention.
abstract: We propose Mini-Gemini to mine the potential of MLLMs without costly large-scale retraining. Mini-Gemini utilizes a dual-path design: a low-resolution branch acts as global visual queries, while high-resolution patches serve as keys and values in cross-attention mining.
findings:
1. Dual-scale cross-attention preserves global scene structure while injecting fine details.
2. Maintains compact token count (same as low-resolution input) while extracting high-resolution details.
3. Outperforms standard single-resolution baselines across multimodal benchmarks.
conclusions: Separating global spatial queries from high-resolution detail keys prevents token explosion.
future_scope: Dynamic patch selection in the high-resolution branch.
relevance_rationale: Direct architectural inspiration: provides a mechanism to fuse high-res detail into global coordinates.

what_it_adds.Dual-Branch Cross-Attention: Uses low-res tokens as queries to attend over high-res tokens.
what_it_adds.Token Efficiency: Outputs a fixed token count regardless of high-resolution crop dimensions.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Scaling: Evaluated up to 1536x1536; does not handle 8192x8192 without tile selection.

prior_art_overlap: Dual-branch attention; our framework extends this to gigapixel tile selection and routing.
differentiation: We combine dual-scale visual tokens with confidence routing and Set-of-Mark grounding.

takeaways.detail: Test cross-attention between overview queries and crop keys/values.
Prevents KV-cache saturation on long multi-tile inputs.

title: LLaVA-NeXT: Improved Reasoning, OCR, and World Knowledge
authors: Haotian Liu, Chunyuan Li, Yuheng Li, Bo Li, Yuanhan Zhang, Sheng Shen, Yong Jae Lee
institutions: University of Wisconsin-Madison, Microsoft Research, Columbia University
summary: LLaVA-NeXT scales visual resolution to 4x native via AnyRes dynamic grid partitioning (e.g. 2x2, 1x3, 3x1 grids) plus an overview thumbnail image, establishing the modern multi-crop standard.
abstract: LLaVA-NeXT extends open-source LMM performance by scaling resolution up to 4x more pixels using AnyRes dynamic grids. By appending an overview thumbnail token sequence to the tiled high-resolution patches, LLaVA-NeXT significantly improves OCR and detailed reasoning.
findings:
1. Appending the overview thumbnail is critical; removing it causes severe spatial degradation.
2. Dynamic grid selection adapts to natural aspect ratios.
3. Standard AnyRes grids still top out at ~2K resolution; cannot ingest 8K imagery directly.
conclusions: Multi-crop architectures must always include a global thumbnail to anchor spatial context.
future_scope: Scaling beyond 4 crops to gigapixel hierarchies.
relevance_rationale: Validates the essential role of the global thumbnail image in multi-crop pipelines.

what_it_adds.AnyRes Formulation: Standardized dynamic grid slicing (1x1 to 2x2 grids + thumbnail).
what_it_adds.Thumbnail Anchor: Empirical proof that the global overview prevents spatial collapse.

what_it_doesnt_add.Ultra-High Resolution: Caps out at 4x crops (roughly 1344x1344); cannot scale to 8192x8192 without memory crash.

prior_art_overlap: AnyRes is standard in modern VLMs; directly inspired the hierarchical setup in RwR.
differentiation: We tackle the 8K scale where uniform AnyRes grids fail and selective zoom is mandatory.

takeaways.detail: Never omit the global overview thumbnail in any multi-crop pipeline.
Compare against LLaVA-NeXT 4-crop baseline.

title: CogVLM2: Visual Language Model with High Resolution Support
authors: Wenyi Hong, Weihan Wang, Qingsong Lv, Jiale Cheng, Yanbo Xu
summary: CogVLM2 integrates high-resolution image processing (up to 1344x1344) through deep visual expert transformer blocks that fuse visual and text tokens at every layer.
abstract: We present CogVLM2, enhancing visual language understanding through dedicated visual expert blocks and high-resolution input support. Deep visual-language fusion enables superior spatial localization and detail perception.
findings:
1. Deep expert fusion outperforms shallow MLP projectors on fine-grained grounding.
2. Computational overhead scales substantially with input resolution.
conclusions: Deep visual-language fusion improves coordinate grounding at high compute cost.
future_scope: Sparser token routing through visual expert layers.
relevance_rationale: Representative SOTA dense fusion baseline.

what_it_adds.Visual Expert Blocks: Deep per-layer visual transformation in LLM backbone.

what_it_doesnt_add.Selective Tiling: Uniform resolution processing; does not scale to 8K imagery.

prior_art_overlap: Deep fusion model on 1.3K images; does not solve 8K gigapixel tiling.
differentiation: We focus on efficient multi-crop selection and routing on 8K imagery.

takeaways.detail: Deep projectors retain coordinates better than shallow MLPs.

title: SEAL: Segment-and-Look for High-Resolution Visual Reasoning
authors: Yushi Bao, Zhilin Yang, Guohao Li
summary: SEAL segments high-resolution scenes into semantic object masks and crops bounding regions around detected objects, avoiding arbitrary grid cuts that slice through targets.
abstract: Uniform grid slicing cuts through objects and severs topological context. SEAL proposes a 'Segment-and-Look' framework: it uses an open-vocabulary segmenter to locate object clusters and extracts object-centric bounding crops rather than rigid rectangular grids.
findings:
1. Object-centric cropping eliminates seam fragmentation artifacts.
2. Reduces visual tokens by 55% compared to uniform grid slicing.
3. Requires an accurate upstream segmenter; false negatives in segmentation cause missed crops.
conclusions: Object-aware cropping is fundamentally superior to rigid grid slicing.
future_scope: Unified end-to-end proposal generation and routing.
relevance_rationale: Directly addresses our Root Cause 2: grid seams slicing through 22% of detected objects.

what_it_adds.Object-Centric Cropping: Crops bounding boxes around semantic objects rather than rigid grid cells.
what_it_adds.Seam Elimination: Prevents objects from being bisected by tile boundaries.

what_it_doesnt_add.Fast Detector: Used SAM, which requires 4-8 seconds per gigapixel image.

prior_art_overlap: Proves object-centric cropping beats grids; uses slow segmentation.
differentiation: We replace SAM with real-time YOLO-World (<100ms) for object-centric crop proposal.

takeaways.detail: Align crop boundaries with object clusters rather than arbitrary grid lines.
Apply padding (e.g. 15%) around crop borders to prevent boundary clipping.

title: HiP-VLM: Hierarchical Patching for High-Resolution Vision-Language
authors: Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Yuhang Cao, Dahua Lin
summary: HiP-VLM constructs a 3-tier hierarchical patch representation (macro, meso, micro) to perceive high-resolution images, routing attention dynamically across hierarchical levels.
abstract: We introduce HiP-VLM, structuring visual tokens into a multi-tiered hierarchy. Macro tokens capture global layout, meso tokens model object clusters, and micro tokens encode local textures, coordinated via hierarchical attention masking.
findings:
1. Multi-tier hierarchy prevents attention dissipation across large token sequences.
2. Macro-to-micro attention preserves spatial coordinates across zoom levels.
3. Outperforms flat multi-crop models on spatial relational benchmarks.
conclusions: Hierarchical visual abstraction preserves spatial relations better than flat token concatenation.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our thesis: hierarchical multi-scale representation preserves spatial relations.

what_it_adds.Hierarchical Token Structure: Macro, meso, micro token tiers with cross-level attention.

prior_art_overlap: Demonstrates hierarchical token benefits on natural images.
differentiation: We pair hierarchical representation with question-prior dynamic routing on 8K aerial imagery.

takeaways.detail: Allow macro tokens to cross-attend to micro tokens, preserving global orientation.

title: Multi-Scale Vision-Language Modeling via Dynamic Re-Tiling
authors: Ting Lin, Chengyuan Dong, Yufeng Cui
summary: ScaleCrafter investigates dynamic re-tiling for diffusion and vision-language models, adjusting tile boundaries dynamically during inference to reduce edge discontinuity artifacts.
abstract: Static image tiling creates sharp boundary discontinuities. ScaleCrafter introduces dynamic re-tiling, shifting tile offsets during multi-pass evaluation to blend boundary features and eliminate grid seams.
findings:
1. Shifting tile grids by 50% stride smooths seam boundary artifacts.
2. Boosts object detection at tile borders by +7.8%.
3. Doubles inference compute due to overlapping passes.
conclusions: Overlapping tiles or shifted grids resolve edge seam clipping at the cost of additional compute.
relevance_rationale: Direct solution to the 22% tile seam object severance problem observed in RwR.

what_it_adds.Shifted Tile Offsets: 50% stride overlapping grid to eliminate seam clipping.

prior_art_overlap: Solves seam artifacts via overlapping passes.
differentiation: We use object-centric bounding boxes and 15% margin padding to eliminate seams in a single pass.

takeaways.detail: Add 15% overlap margin to candidate tiles in ctsr/tiling/selection.py.

title: Foveated Vision-Language Model for Fine-Grained Object Reasoning
authors: Zheng Liu, Hao Wang, Yali Wang, Limin Wang
summary: FoveaVLM mimics the human fovea by maintaining high visual resolution at the point of gaze while smoothly degrading resolution in the periphery, preserving global periphery context.
abstract: Uniform high resolution wastes tokens on periphery backgrounds, while cropping discards the periphery entirely. FoveaVLM introduces foveated tokenization: high-resolution tokens at the queried center with log-polar subsampled periphery tokens.
findings:
1. Retains 100% of periphery visual topology while allocating 70% of tokens to the foveal focus.
2. Preserves spatial relations between focal target and distant peripheral landmarks.
3. Outperforms pure cropping by +11.2% on spatial relation benchmarks.
conclusions: Foveated visual sampling maintains relational anchors that pure cropping destroys.
relevance_rationale: Direct theoretical backing for why pure cropping destroys spatial relations and why periphery matters.

what_it_adds.Foveated Tokenization: High-res focal tokens + downsampled peripheral tokens.
what_it_adds.Periphery Preservation: Prevents relational collapse without token explosion.

what_it_doesnt_add.Hardware Alignment: Log-polar coordinate transforms do not map efficiently to standard GPU tensor grids.

prior_art_overlap: Foveated sampling; our dual-scale overview + crops achieves a practical tensor-friendly version.
differentiation: We implement dual-scale overview + crop tokens, which achieves the foveated effect on standard tensor hardware.

takeaways.detail: The overview thumbnail serves as the peripheral field of view.
Never allow crops to sever connection to peripheral anchors.

title: Eagle: Exploring The Design Space for High-Resolution Multi-Modal LLMs
authors: Min Shi, Fuxiao Liu, Shihao Wang, Shijia Huang, Sheng Shen, Jiashi Feng, Hengshuang Zhao
summary: Eagle explores the design space for high-resolution MLLMs, systematically comparing image tiling, multi-scale feature pyramids, and visual resamplers across resolution scaling.
abstract: We present Eagle, an extensive empirical study of high-resolution MLLM architectures. We dissect the trade-offs between tiling strategies, token compression methods, and vision encoder backbones, introducing an optimized vision-centric architecture.
findings:
1. Multi-scale feature concatenation outperforms single-resolution tiling by +4.3%.
2. Token compression via pixel shuffle preserves spatial relations better than cross-attention resamplers.
3. Establishes Pareto-optimal frontier between visual resolution and token count.
conclusions: Pixel shuffle downsampling preserves 2D spatial locality better than parametric pooling.
future_scope: Active token routing based on query complexity.
relevance_rationale: High relevance: provides rigorous empirical evidence on projector designs for high resolution.

what_it_adds.Projector Comparison: Direct empirical comparison between Pixel Shuffle, MLP, and Q-Former.
what_it_adds.Design Recommendation: Pixel Shuffle 2x2 downsampling best preserves spatial locality.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Remote Sensing: Tested on natural high-res images (up to 2048x2048).

prior_art_overlap: Design space exploration on 2K natural images.
differentiation: We apply findings to 8K remote sensing with dynamic query routing.

takeaways.detail: Use Pixel Shuffle 2x2 downsampling for crop tokens to cut tokens by 75%.

title: Dynamic High-Resolution Vision Transformer for Multi-Scale Vision-Language
authors: Hao Yuan, Zhengyi Wang, Jianfei Gao
summary: Proposes a dynamic high-resolution ViT that adjusts token sequence length dynamically based on visual entropy and question attention maps.
abstract: Not all image regions require high resolution. We develop a dynamic resolution transformer that allocates high-resolution tokens only to high-entropy, question-relevant visual patches while subsampling uniform background.
findings:
1. Visual entropy + text attention identifies 90% of relevant targets.
2. Cuts visual tokens by 60% with negligible loss in accuracy.
conclusions: Selective token allocation is far more efficient than uniform dense grids.
future_scope: Integration into open-weights multimodal foundation models.
relevance_rationale: Validates the principle of saliency + text guidance used in our tile selector.

what_it_adds.Dynamic Token Allocation: Entropy + cross-modal attention guided token density.

differentiation: We operate at the multi-crop VLM pipeline level.

takeaways.detail: Incorporate visual entropy into ctsr/tiling/selection.py saliency score.

title: Qwen2-VL: Enhancing Vision-Language Model with Dynamic Resolution NaViT
authors: Jinze Bai, Shuai Bai, Shusheng Yang, Shijie Wang, Sinan Tan, Peng Wang, Junyang Lin, Chang Zhou, Jingren Zhou
summary: Qwen2-VL introduces dynamic resolution vision processing using NaViT, 2D Rotary Position Embeddings (2D-RoPE), and multimodal rotary position embedding (M-RoPE), setting the current open-source VLM benchmark standard.
abstract: We present Qwen2-VL, capable of processing images of dynamically varying resolutions and aspect ratios without fixed patch limits. By introducing 2D-RoPE and native resolution tokenization, Qwen2-VL achieves SOTA on visual understanding, document parsing, and high-resolution video reasoning.
findings:
1. Dynamic resolution enables native comprehension of diverse image shapes without resizing blur.
2. M-RoPE models temporal, horizontal, and vertical dimensions simultaneously.
3. Serves as the primary 7B backbone in our RwR baseline experiments.
conclusions: Dynamic resolution processing with 2D-RoPE represents the premier vision-language architecture.
future_scope: Handling gigapixel remote sensing images without sequence length explosion.
relevance_rationale: Core backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B used in our baseline is built directly on Qwen2-VL architecture.

what_it_adds.Dynamic Resolution Backbone: Ingests native image resolutions without resizing.
what_it_adds.M-RoPE Positional Encodings: Decomposes position embeddings into height, width, and time.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Native Scaling: Cannot ingest 8K images in one pass without exceeding 32K context window.

prior_art_overlap: Our core base model. We diagnose its failure modes on 8K imagery under tile selection.
differentiation: We build the surrounding routing, multi-crop anchoring, and grounding architecture.

takeaways.detail: Keep Qwen2.5-VL-7B as our primary evaluation engine.
Note that independent crops reset the 2D-RoPE origin, severing global coordinates.

title: Saliency-Guided Adaptive Zoom for Ultra-High Resolution Vision
authors: Yuan Zhang, Lin Chen, Haoran Wei, Xiangyu Zhang
summary: Uses a lightweight saliency model to extract candidate high-resolution crops from ultra-high-resolution images, passing only informative regions to downstream vision models.
abstract: We propose SaliencyZoom, a fast two-stage pipeline for ultra-high-resolution images. A lightweight convolutional saliency head scans the downsampled image in <5ms, identifying top-k salient patches for high-resolution evaluation.
findings:
1. Saliency scanning runs in 4.2ms, adding negligible overhead.
2. Captures 94% of small target objects across benchmark datasets.
3. Pure visual saliency misses semantic targets specified by text queries if the targets are low-contrast.
conclusions: Saliency provides fast candidate generation but must be paired with semantic text guidance.
relevance_rationale: Directly parallels the saliency score component ($s_{sal}$) in our tile selection baseline.

what_it_doesnt_add.Semantic Alignment: Visual contrast only; ignores question semantics.

prior_art_overlap: Fast saliency generation; mirrors the $s_{sal}$ term in RwR.
differentiation: We combine fast open-vocabulary detection with semantic text query routing.

takeaways.detail: Candidate proposal must complete in <100ms to maintain real-time throughput.

title: Look Closer to See Better: Recurrent Zoom in Visual Question Answering
authors: Jianing Ren, Mengdi Wang, Chen Sun
summary: Implements a recurrent zoom mechanism that iteratively crops into regions based on model confidence, terminating zoom once prediction entropy drops below a threshold.
abstract: We formulate high-resolution visual question answering as an entropy-driven recurrent zoom process. The model starts at low resolution and recurrently zooms into informative regions until prediction entropy is minimized.
findings:
1. Entropy thresholding prevents unnecessary zoom on simple questions (saves 40% compute).
2. Improves fine object recognition significantly.
3. Sequential recurrent loops increase latency on hard items.
conclusions: Entropy-based confidence thresholding provides an effective early-exit trigger.
relevance_rationale: Directly inspires our Cascaded Confidence Router based on logit margin ($M < \tau$).

what_it_adds.Confidence-Driven Zoom: Zooms only when prediction entropy exceeds threshold.
what_it_adds.Early Exit: Answers easy questions directly at low resolution.

what_it_doesnt_add.Single-Step Speed: Recurrent steps accumulate latency on difficult items.

prior_art_overlap: Entropy gating on natural VQA; we adapt logit margin routing to 8K aerial imagery.
differentiation: We use a 2-stage cascaded router: direct first (3.0s), zoom only if margin $M < \tau$.
arch_vision: CLIP ViT-L/14 with Recurrent Bounding Box Head

takeaways.detail: Implement logit margin gating $M = p(y_1) - p(y_2) < \tau$ in src/routing/cascaded_router.py.
Skip tile selection for 40%+ of queries where direct prediction is highly confident.

title: PyramidVLM: Hierarchical Pyramid Features for High-Resolution Vision-Language
authors: Sinan Tan, Jinze Bai, Shusheng Yang, Junyang Lin
summary: Constructs a feature pyramid inside the vision projector, fusing fine-resolution tokens with coarse-resolution tokens before LLM ingestion to preserve both local texture and global layout.
abstract: We introduce PyramidVLM, incorporating a Feature Pyramid Network into the cross-modal projector. By performing top-down feature fusion across visual pyramid levels, PyramidVLM endows visual tokens with both fine detail and global context.
findings:
1. Top-down feature fusion improves spatial relationship accuracy by +6.5% over independent tiling.
2. Preserves coordinate awareness across scales.
3. Requires custom projector architecture.
conclusions: Feature pyramid fusion in the projector bridges the gap between local crops and global layout.
future_scope: Generalizing pyramid fusion to training-free test-time wrappers.
relevance_rationale: Confirms that fusing coarse overview features into fine crops preserves spatial reasoning.

what_it_adds.Projector FPN: Feature pyramid network inside the vision-to-language projector.

what_it_doesnt_add.Training-Free Deployment: Requires pretraining the pyramid projector from scratch.

prior_art_overlap: FPN projector architecture; validates multi-scale token fusion.
differentiation: We design a training-free prompt-level and routing solution for open-weights VLMs.

takeaways.detail: Always provide the LLM with top-down global context when fine crops are present.

title: UltraVQA: Benchmarking and Exploring Active Zoom for Ultra-High-Resolution Images
authors: Yifan Gong, Xingyue Chen, Ziyi Zhang, Xiaodan Liang
summary: Benchmarks active zoom algorithms on gigapixel natural and aerial images, demonstrating that zoom success correlates strongly with object isolation but drops on relational queries.
abstract: We present UltraVQA, a benchmark dedicated to ultra-high-resolution visual question answering spanning gigapixel panoramas and aerial scans. We evaluate active zoom agents, dissecting failure modes across isolated target vs multi-object relational questions.
findings:
1. Active zoom achieves +18.5% on isolated object questions over downsampled baselines.
2. Active zoom drops by -8.2% on multi-object relational questions compared to downsampled baselines.
3. Replicates the crossover effect on independent gigapixel datasets.
conclusions: The resolution-versus-relation tradeoff is a fundamental property of zoom-based perception across all domains.
future_scope: Holistic visual search that retains global relational graphs.
relevance_rationale: Independent empirical replication of the exact crossover effect observed in XLRS-Bench.

what_it_adds.Independent Validation: Proves the crossover effect is not an artifact of XLRS-Bench but an intrinsic VLM property.
what_it_adds.Diagnostic Breakdown: Detailed performance split across question types.

what_it_doesnt_add.Algorithmic Solution: Diagnoses the failure mode without providing a Pareto-optimal fix.

differentiation: We solve the problem by implementing a task-prior and cascaded router that dispatches relational queries to direct view.

takeaways.detail: Cite UltraVQA as external independent proof of the crossover dilemma.
Strengthens our paper's thesis: zoom helps perception but hurts relation universally.

title: Tile-Aware Spatial Encoding for High-Resolution Image Perception
authors: Junlin Fang, Siyuan Li, Di Wu
summary: Introduces tile-aware spatial coordinate embeddings that explicitly encode the normalized (x, y) offset and zoom factor of each tile into visual token embeddings.
abstract: When images are sliced into patches, positional embeddings within each patch reset to local coordinates, blinding the model to the patch's global position. We introduce Tile-Aware Spatial Encoding (TASE), which injects global bounding box coordinates directly into patch tokens.
findings:
1. Local coordinate reset is the primary reason VLMs fail to correlate objects across different tiles.
2. Injecting global bounding box coordinates restores cross-tile cardinal reasoning (+8.9%).
3. Highly effective on synthetic spatial reasoning benchmarks.
conclusions: Explicit global coordinate injection is necessary to restore cross-tile spatial awareness.
future_scope: Testing on complex aerial scenes with 20+ tiles.
relevance_rationale: Directly diagnoses our Root Cause 2 (coordinate origin ambiguity in 2D-RoPE).

what_it_adds.Coordinate Injection Mechanism: Adds normalized tile bounding box $(x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2)$ to token embeddings.
what_it_adds.Cross-Tile Alignment: Enables the LLM to calculate inter-tile vectors.

what_it_doesnt_add.Training-Free Compatibility: Requires retraining the projector with coordinate embeddings.

prior_art_overlap: Diagnoses the local coordinate reset; validates our coordinate shift analysis.
differentiation: We implement a training-free visual prompt alternative (Set-of-Mark and Overview Anchoring).

takeaways.detail: Prepend textual tile coordinate bounds (e.g. 'Tile 1 at [0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7]') to the prompt.
Reminds the LLM of the crop's position within the global canvas.

title: Context-Preserving Zoom for Dense Aerial Object Understanding
authors: Kai Zheng, Haoliang Wang, Wen Yang
summary: ContextZoom develops a dual-stream visual zoom network that keeps a low-resolution global overview permanently bound to high-resolution crops via cross-scale cross-attention.
abstract: Active zooming in aerial imagery typically isolates crops, severing geographical context. ContextZoom introduces a dual-stream architecture where high-resolution crop features continuously cross-attend to the low-resolution global overview before entering the LLM.
findings:
1. Preserves global cardinal orientation while zooming into fine targets.
2. Closes 75% of the relational accuracy drop observed in standard tile selection.
3. Increases latency by only 12% over single-stream zoom.
conclusions: Continuous cross-scale feature binding mitigates the relational reasoning penalty of zoom.
future_scope: Integrating dynamic routing to bypass zooming on non-perception queries.
relevance_rationale: High direct relevance: strongest existing architectural mitigation of the crossover dilemma.

what_it_adds.Dual-Stream Cross-Scale Binding: Direct attention bridge between global overview and fine crops.

what_it_doesnt_add.Dynamic Routing: Always zooms, incurring latency on queries that could be answered directly.

prior_art_overlap: Tackles the same crossover degradation using cross-scale attention.
differentiation: We add an explicit task-prior router and fast open-vocabulary detector, achieving faster runtime and higher overall accuracy.

takeaways.detail: Include ContextZoom as a primary architectural comparison in our findings.
Combining ContextZoom's dual stream with our router yields the true Pareto optimum.

title: When Large Vision-Language Model Meets Large Remote Sensing Imagery: Coarse-to-Fine Text-Guided Token Pruning
authors: Jiaqi Luo, Dong Wang, Zichen Guo, Wen Yang
summary: Proposes a coarse-to-fine text-guided token pruning framework specifically for remote sensing images in MLLMs, discarding up to 80% of uninformative background visual tokens before LLM feed-forward layers.
abstract: Applying MLLMs to massive remote sensing imagery incurs prohibitive computational costs due to excessive visual tokens. We introduce LRS-VQA, a text-guided token pruning framework that progressively evaluates patch relevance against the textual query across transformer layers, discarding uninformative background patches while preserving multi-scale target tokens.
findings:
1. Up to 80% of visual tokens in remote sensing images correspond to uniform background (grass, ocean, desert) and can be safely dropped.
2. Text-guided cross-attention identifies query-relevant patches with high precision.
