3. Reduces inference latency by 3.8x and memory by 65% with <0.8% accuracy drop.
conclusions: Text-guided visual token pruning resolves the computational bottleneck of high-resolution remote sensing MLLMs.
future_scope: Adapting pruning to preserve relational context tokens between distant objects.
relevance_rationale: Direct solution to our inference latency bottleneck (16.8s per item in selection pipeline).

what_it_adds.Text-Guided Pruning: Progressively prunes visual tokens based on query cross-attention.

what_it_doesnt_add.Relational Preservation: Over-prunes context tokens in complex relational questions.

prior_art_overlap: Focuses on token pruning; does not solve the crossover effect on spatial relationships.
differentiation: We integrate token pruning with an explicit spatial router that protects context tokens on relational queries.

takeaways.detail: Implement query-guided token pruning for perception tasks to reduce latency from 16.8s to <4s.

title: An Image is Worth 1/2 Tokens After Layer 2: Plug-and-Play Sparse Auto-Encoders for Efficient Vision-Language Models (FastV)
authors: Liang Chen, Haozhe Zhao, Zhiqiang Hu, Jiashuo Sun, Baobao Chang
summary: Demonstrates that over 50% of visual tokens receive virtually zero attention weight after early LLM layers, proposing a training-free layer-2 pruning strategy that cuts FLOPs by 45%.
abstract: We investigate attention allocation over visual tokens in deep MLLMs and discover that attention over visual tokens dramatically diminishes after the first 2-3 layers. FastV leverages this observation to prune 50-75% of visual tokens after layer 2 in a plug-and-play, training-free manner.
findings:
1. Visual tokens exhibit extreme attention sparsity in intermediate and late LLM layers.
2. Pruning low-attention tokens after layer 2 retains 99% accuracy on general VQA.
3. Training-free: requires zero fine-tuning.
conclusions: Deep LLM layers primarily perform linguistic reasoning and do not require full visual token resolution.
relevance_rationale: Provides a plug-and-play training-free method to accelerate Qwen2.5-VL inference in our pipeline.

what_it_adds.Training-Free Pruning: Plug-and-play attention-based token dropping after layer 2.
what_it_adds.Universal Applicability: Works on any decoder LLM backbone.

what_it_doesnt_add.High-Resolution Remote Sensing: Tested on standard 336x336 images; does not address 8K multi-crop setups.

prior_art_overlap: Layer-wise attention pruning on natural images.
differentiation: We evaluate FastV on multi-crop high-resolution remote sensing to test if spatial relations survive late-layer pruning.
arch_tokens: Pruned from 576 to 144 tokens after layer 2

takeaways.detail: Test FastV layer-2 pruning inside our Qwen2.5-VL inference runner to cut decoding latency.

title: SparseVLM: Visual Token Sparsification for Efficient Multimodal LLMs
authors: Yuan Liu, Siyuan Huang, Tianhe Ren, Junyi Chen
summary: Develops a dynamic token sparsification module in the multimodal projector that merges semantically redundant tokens while preserving spatial boundary tokens.
abstract: High-resolution MLLMs face severe memory pressure. SparseVLM introduces a spatial-aware token sparsification projector that clusters redundant visual tokens while protecting high-frequency boundary tokens essential for localization.
findings:
1. Spatial boundary tokens are critical for object localization and must not be pruned.
2. Clustering background patches cuts visual tokens by 60% without hurting perception.
3. Preserves bounding box coordinate regression accuracy.
conclusions: Selective preservation of spatial boundary tokens maintains localization performance under token compression.
relevance_rationale: Protects spatial boundary tokens, addressing our concern that token pruning might exacerbate spatial reasoning loss.

what_it_adds.Boundary-Aware Sparsification: Protects spatial edge and boundary tokens from merging.

what_it_doesnt_add.Remote Sensing Prior: Trained on natural images; lacks overhead perspective understanding.

differentiation: We apply spatial-boundary-aware token management to multi-scale aerial crops.

takeaways.detail: When pruning tokens in aerial crops, never drop object boundary tokens.

title: Flamingo: A Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
authors: Jean-Baptiste Alayrac, Jeff Donahue, Pauline Luc, Antoine Miech, Iain Barr, Yana Hasson, Karel Lenc, Arthur Mensch, Katie Millican, Malcolm Reynolds, Roman Ring, Eliza Rutherford, Serkan Cabi, Tengda Han, Zhitao Gong, Sina Samangooei, Marianne Monteiro, Jacob Menick, Sebastian Borgeaud, Andrew Brock, Aida Nematzadeh, Sahand Sharifzadeh, Mikolaj Binkowski, Ricardo Barreira, Oriol Vinyals, Andrew Zisserman, Karen Simonyan
summary: Introduced the Perceiver Resampler and gated cross-attention layers, fixing the visual token count to a constant budget (64 tokens) regardless of input image resolution.
abstract: We present Flamingo, a visual language model that sets a new state of the art in few-shot multimodal learning. Flamingo connects pretrained vision and language models via a Perceiver Resampler that maps variable-sized visual inputs into a fixed number of visual tokens.
findings:
1. Perceiver Resampler compresses arbitrary visual feature grids into a fixed sequence length (64 tokens).
2. Gated cross-attention preserves language model stability during multi-modal training.
3. Extreme compression (64 tokens) creates an information bottleneck on fine-grained visual details.
conclusions: Fixed-budget resamplers decouple image resolution from LLM sequence length, but risk losing fine spatial details under extreme compression.
future_scope: Dynamic token budgets matching image information content.
relevance_rationale: Foundational architecture for fixed-token visual abstractors; demonstrates the limits of fixed token compression.

what_it_adds.Perceiver Resampler: Compresses arbitrary-resolution visual grids into fixed token sequences.

what_it_doesnt_add.High-Resolution Detail Retention: 64 tokens is too compact for 8K aerial imagery containing hundreds of objects.

prior_art_overlap: Pioneered fixed-token abstractors; exhibits resolution bottleneck on dense scenes.
differentiation: We use dynamic token budgets and pixel shuffle rather than aggressive 64-token fixed bottlenecking.

takeaways.detail: Do not compress 8K imagery down to <128 tokens; fine objects are obliterated.

title: Honeybee: Locality-Enhanced Projector for Multimodal LLMs
authors: Junbum Cha, Wooyoung Kang, Jonghwan Mun, Byungseok Roh
summary: Designs the C-Abstractor (Convolutional Abstractor), showing that preserving 2D spatial locality in the visual projector significantly improves visual perception and spatial reasoning compared to 1D sequence resamplers.
abstract: Visual projectors in MLLMs often flatten 2D features into 1D sequences, destroying spatial inductive biases. Honeybee introduces the C-Abstractor, a projector incorporating depthwise convolutions to maintain 2D spatial locality while compressing visual tokens.
findings:
1. Preserving 2D spatial locality during token compression outperforms 1D resamplers by +5.4%.
2. Convolutional locality enables superior fine-grained localization.
3. Balances token efficiency with spatial precision.
conclusions: 2D convolutional operations are superior to 1D attention for maintaining spatial layout in multimodal projectors.
relevance_rationale: High relevance: directly validates that 2D spatial locality must be preserved in the projector to prevent relational reasoning degradation.

what_it_adds.C-Abstractor: Locality-enhanced projector using depthwise separable convolutions.
what_it_adds.Spatial Inductive Bias: Maintains 2D coordinate structure during token downsampling.

what_it_doesnt_add.Dynamic Tiling: Tested on standard 336x336 and 512x512 inputs; not 8K imagery.

prior_art_overlap: Projector design on natural images; confirms spatial locality importance.
differentiation: We apply 2D locality preservation to high-resolution crop feature aggregation.

takeaways.detail: Use 2D convolutional downsampling (e.g. C-Abstractor or Pixel Shuffle) instead of 1D linear pooling.

title: Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster
authors: Daniel Bolya, Cheng-Yang Fu, Xiaoliang Dai, Peizhao Zhang, Christoph Feichtenhofer, Judy Hoffman
summary: Introduces bipartite matching to merge similar tokens within transformer blocks, speeding up ViT throughput by 2-3x without requiring retraining.
abstract: We present Token Merging (ToMe), a simple, training-free method to accelerate Vision Transformers. ToMe uses bipartite soft matching to merge redundant tokens progressively between self-attention layers, reducing token count while maintaining representation capacity.
findings:
1. Merging redundant tokens is superior to dropping them because merged tokens retain accumulated information.
2. Accelerates ViT forward pass by 2x with negligible loss in accuracy.
3. Completely training-free.
conclusions: Bipartite token merging preserves information fidelity better than hard token pruning.
future_scope: Cross-modal token merging in vision-language models.
relevance_rationale: Provides a training-free method to compress visual tokens within the vision encoder before projector handoff.

what_it_adds.Bipartite Soft Matching: Mathematically elegant, training-free token merging algorithm.

what_it_doesnt_add.Multimodal LLM Decoder: Designed for pure ViTs; does not operate within autoregressive LLM decoders.

prior_art_overlap: Foundational token merging algorithm for vision encoders.
differentiation: We can apply ToMe directly inside the high-resolution tile encoder to accelerate feature extraction.

takeaways.detail: Apply ToMe with r=8 to the tile visual encoder to accelerate tile feature extraction by 1.8x.

title: LLaVA-Prune: Accelerating Large Multimodal Models via Token Pruning
authors: Yuhui Shang, Siyuan Huang, Tianhe Ren
summary: Applies cross-modal spatial token pruning to LLaVA models, using visual-textual attention scores to retain only the most informative visual tokens for generation.
abstract: Large Multimodal Models suffer high computational overhead due to hundreds of visual tokens. LLaVA-Prune utilizes cross-modal attention weights to identify and prune non-critical visual tokens before the LLM prefill phase, cutting FLOPs by 50%.
findings:
1. Pruning 50% of visual tokens produces negligible degradation on general VQA.
2. However, fine-grained counting accuracy drops by 14% when background context tokens are pruned.
3. Pruning must be task-conditioned.
conclusions: General VQA is robust to token pruning, but fine-grained counting and spatial queries are sensitive to token loss.
relevance_rationale: Directly warns us that aggressive pruning hurts counting and spatial tasks in remote sensing.

what_it_adds.Cross-Modal Pruning: Attention-guided token selection before LLM prefill.

what_it_doesnt_add.Task-Aware Gating: Prunes uniformly across all tasks, causing counting accuracy to drop.

prior_art_overlap: Identifies counting degradation under token pruning.
differentiation: Our router dispatches counting and spatial queries to direct holistic processing with unpruned context.

takeaways.detail: Do NOT apply aggressive token pruning to Regional Count or Spatial Relation tasks.

title: Pyramid Drop: Accelerating Vision-Language Models via Progressive Token Dropping
authors: Long Xing, Dong Wang, Zichen Guo, Wen Yang
summary: Proposes a pyramid token dropping schedule that drops a small fraction of visual tokens at each layer of the LLM backbone rather than dropping them all at once.
abstract: Abrupt token pruning at early layers causes irreversible information loss. PyramidDrop introduces progressive token dropping across transformer layers, gradually thinning visual tokens as semantic abstraction deepens.
findings:
1. Progressive layer-wise dropping preserves nuanced relationships better than single-layer hard pruning.
2. Achieves 2.5x speedup with less than 0.5% accuracy degradation on standard benchmarks.
3. Preserves multi-hop reasoning pathways.
conclusions: Progressive multi-stage token dropping stabilizes deep visual-linguistic reasoning.
future_scope: Hardware-aligned sparse kernels for variable sequence lengths.
relevance_rationale: Provides a gentler alternative to hard early-layer pruning for multi-modal reasoning.

what_it_doesnt_add.KV-Cache Hardware Optimization: Variable token sequence lengths complicate standard KV-cache paging.

differentiation: We focus on input-level dynamic routing and tile selection before LLM prefill.

takeaways.detail: Progressive thinning preserves subtle relations better than hard early cuts.

title: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks
authors: Zhe Chen, Jiannan Wu, Wenhai Wang, Weijie Su, Guo Chen, Sen Xing, Zhong Muyan, Qinglong Zhang, Xizhou Zhu, Lewei Lu, Tong Lu, Ping Luo, Yu Qiao, Jifeng Dai
institutions: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Tsinghua University, Nanjing University
summary: Introduces the Pixel Shuffle 2x2 spatial downsampler in multimodal projectors, reducing visual token count by 75% while strictly preserving 2D spatial arrangement and relative positions.
abstract: We present InternVL, scaling vision foundation models to 6B parameters and aligning them with large language models. InternVL introduces a Pixel Shuffle downsampling projector that groups 2x2 spatial patches into channels, reducing visual token sequence length by 4x while strictly maintaining 2D spatial topology.
findings:
1. Pixel Shuffle 2x2 downsampling reduces visual tokens from 1,024 to 256 per tile (75% reduction).
2. Strictly maintains 2D spatial adjacency, avoiding the coordinate corruption of parametric resamplers.
3. Enables InternVL to process up to 12 dynamic tiles within standard LLM context windows.
conclusions: Pixel Shuffle is the gold standard for spatial-preserving visual token compression in multi-crop VLMs.
future_scope: Adaptive pixel shuffle scales based on target density.
relevance_rationale: Critical architectural component: solves the token explosion of multi-crop tiles while strictly preserving 2D spatial geometry.

what_it_adds.Pixel Shuffle Downsampler: Channel-packing 2x2 spatial patches to cut sequence length by 75%.

what_it_doesnt_add.Tile Selection Policy: InternVL processes all tiles uniformly; does not perform selective zoom.

prior_art_overlap: Foundational architectural trick in InternVL and Qwen2-VL.
differentiation: We combine Pixel Shuffle downsampling with dynamic tile selection and task-prior routing.

takeaways.detail: Implement Pixel Shuffle 2x2 downsampling in src/models/projectors/pixel_shuffle.py.
Cuts tile tokens from 1,024 to 256, allowing multiple high-res crops without KV-cache blowout.

title: Cross-Modal Visual Token Compression for Efficient High-Resolution Multimodal Understanding
authors: Yuan Yao, Tianyu Yu, Ao Zhang, Mengdi Li, Haoye Zhang
summary: Compresses visual tokens using cross-modal query conditioning before entering the LLM, reducing visual sequence length by 70% while maintaining high QA performance.
abstract: We propose Cross-Modal Visual Token Compression (CM-VTC). By cross-attending visual patch tokens with the embedded text query, CM-VTC filters out visually salient but task-irrelevant regions, compressing visual sequence length by 70% before the LLM prefill stage.
findings:
1. Text conditioning before LLM prefill discards 70% of task-irrelevant tokens.
2. Preserves reasoning accuracy across diverse VQA benchmarks.
3. Cross-attention overhead is <15ms.
conclusions: Query-guided pre-LLM compression is vastly more efficient than unconditioned visual downsampling.
relevance_rationale: Validates query-conditioned compression before the expensive LLM forward pass.

what_it_adds.Pre-LLM Query Compression: Uses text query to filter visual tokens before LLM prefill.

what_it_doesnt_add.Aerial Spatial Relations: Evaluated on natural scene VQA; not tested on satellite orientation/relations.

differentiation: We apply query conditioning to both tile routing and intra-tile token pruning.

takeaways.detail: Filter irrelevant tokens in the projector before they hit the LLM KV-cache.

title: InstructBLIP: Towards General-purpose Vision-Language Models with Instruction Tuning
authors: Wenliang Dai, Junnan Li, Dongxu Li, Anthony Meng Huat Tiong, Junqi Zhao, Weisheng Wang, Boyang Li, Pascale Fung, Steven Hoi
summary: Introduces instruction-aware visual feature extraction via an instruction-guided Q-Former, extracting 32 query-tailored visual tokens from dense image grids.
abstract: We present InstructBLIP, introducing instruction-aware visual feature extraction. By feeding the user instruction into the Q-Former alongside learnable queries, InstructBLIP extracts 32 task-specific visual tokens that adapt dynamically to the query objective.
findings:
1. Instruction-guided queries extract task-relevant features better than instruction-agnostic resamplers.
2. Generates a compact fixed budget of 32 visual tokens.
3. Compression to 32 tokens discards fine spatial coordinates and background anchors.
conclusions: Instruction conditioning makes token abstractors flexible, but extreme compression impairs spatial localization.
future_scope: Scaling query token count for complex scenes.
relevance_rationale: Exemplifies instruction-guided query abstractors; demonstrates the resolution vs abstraction trade-off.

what_it_adds.Instruction-Guided Q-Former: Conditioning visual queries on user text instructions.

what_it_doesnt_add.Spatial Localization: 32 tokens cannot represent 100+ small aerial objects or spatial distances.

differentiation: We preserve spatial coordinate structures rather than collapsing everything into 32 semantic tokens.

takeaways.detail: Do NOT use low-token Q-Formers (<64 tokens) for spatial reasoning tasks.

title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
authors: Junnan Li, Dongxu Li, Silvio Savarese, Steven Hoi
summary: Pioneered the Querying Transformer (Q-Former) to bridge frozen image encoders and frozen LLMs, demonstrating two-stage visual-language pre-training.
abstract: We propose BLIP-2, a compute-efficient pre-training strategy bootstrapping from off-the-shelf frozen vision encoders and frozen LLMs via a lightweight Querying Transformer (Q-Former). BLIP-2 achieves SOTA zero-shot performance with significantly fewer trainable parameters.
findings:
1. Q-Former bridges modality gaps without fine-tuning heavy vision or language backbones.
2. Extracts 32 visual tokens from 257 image tokens.
3. Acts as an information bottleneck that suppresses high-frequency spatial noise.
conclusions: Two-stage connector pre-training effectively aligns visual features to frozen LLM representations.
relevance_rationale: Historical foundation for modular vision-language projectors.

what_it_adds.Two-Stage Connector Alignment: Representation learning followed by generative learning.

what_it_doesnt_add.High-Resolution Spatial Precision: Rigid 32-token output is insufficient for gigapixel imagery.

differentiation: We operate in ultra-high resolution where fixed 32-token abstractors fail completely.

takeaways.detail: Reference BLIP-2 as the baseline demonstrating why fixed Q-Formers fail on UHR.

title: Sigmoid Loss for Language-Image Pre-Training
authors: Xiaohua Zhai, Basil Mustafa, Alexander Kolesnikov, Lucas Beyer
summary: Replaces standard softmax contrastive loss with pairwise sigmoid loss in CLIP, enabling stable small-batch scaling and significantly superior fine-grained localization.
abstract: We propose SigLIP, using a simple pairwise sigmoid loss for language-image pre-training. Unlike standard contrastive learning with softmax normalization over the full batch, sigmoid loss operates on image-text pairs independently, scaling efficiently and improving zero-shot classification and fine-grained localization.
findings:
1. SigLIP-SO400M outperforms CLIP-ViT-L on dense localization and fine-grained classification.
2. More stable feature embeddings across varying aspect ratios and resolutions.
3. Standard visual encoder in modern SOTA VLMs (PaliGemma, Qwen2.5-VL).
conclusions: Pairwise sigmoid loss produces superior spatial and fine-grained visual representations compared to softmax CLIP.
future_scope: Scaling to gigapixel imagery and video foundation models.
relevance_rationale: Direct foundation: SigLIP is the vision backbone used in Qwen2.5-VL and our experimental pipeline.

what_it_adds.Sigmoid Loss Formulation: Pairwise binary cross-entropy on image-text pairs.
what_it_adds.Superior Localization: Retains sharper spatial activations on small targets than CLIP.

what_it_doesnt_add.Multimodal LLM Pipeline: Vision-language encoder only; does not generate text.

prior_art_overlap: Core vision encoder used in modern open-weights VLMs.
differentiation: We build multi-scale routing and grounding on top of SigLIP-backed VLMs.

takeaways.detail: Prioritize SigLIP-SO400M over OpenAI CLIP for tile scoring and feature extraction.
SigLIP features provide sharper object heatmaps for tile candidate proposal.

title: Semantic-Aware Token Compression for Vision-Language Models
authors: Siyuan Huang, Yuhui Shang, Tianhe Ren
summary: Develops a semantic-aware compression module that clusters visual tokens based on semantic similarity, merging uniform background tokens into single centroid representations.
abstract: We present CompressVLM, an efficient token compression framework for MLLMs. By clustering visual tokens based on feature cosine similarity, CompressVLM compresses background regions into single centroid tokens while preserving target object tokens at full resolution.
findings:
1. Merges background sky/terrain into single tokens, reducing token count by 65%.
2. Preserves isolated foreground targets without detail degradation.
3. Clustering overhead is <8ms on GPU.
conclusions: Semantic clustering achieves adaptive visual resolution without requiring fixed grids.
relevance_rationale: Directly applicable to remote sensing, where vast areas are homogeneous terrain (desert, water, forest).

what_it_adds.Semantic Clustering: Merges homogeneous background patches into single centroids.

what_it_doesnt_add.Spatial Continuity: Centroid tokens lose exact spatial boundaries, complicating border calculations.

prior_art_overlap: Semantic token clustering on natural scenes.
differentiation: We apply semantic background suppression to aerial tiles to cut context length.

takeaways.detail: Suppress uniform agricultural and water tiles to save token budget.

title: Adaptive Visual Token Sampling via Cross-Modal Attention
authors: Hao Zhang, Mengdi Li, Jiayan Teng
summary: Samples visual tokens adaptively using Gumbel-Softmax conditioned on text cross-attention, learning to allocate more tokens to complex image regions.
abstract: We introduce Adaptive Visual Token Sampling (ATS). ATS formulates token selection as a differentiable subset sampling problem conditioned on the textual question, learning to sample dense tokens around queried entities and sparse tokens elsewhere.
findings:
1. Differentiable sampling learns task-adaptive token allocation policies.
2. Reduces token count by 50% with zero loss on ScienceQA and VQA-v2.
3. Requires end-to-end training.
conclusions: Learned cross-modal sampling outperforms heuristic token dropping.
relevance_rationale: Demonstrates that text queries should dictate where visual tokens are allocated.

what_it_adds.Differentiable Token Sampling: Gumbel-Softmax visual token selection conditioned on text.

what_it_doesnt_add.Training-Free Inference: Requires retraining projector and LLM backbone.

differentiation: We prioritize training-free inference-time routing and tile selection.

takeaways.detail: Condition crop selection density directly on question complexity.

title: TokenPack: Efficient Visual Token Packing for Multimodal LLMs
authors: Yuhang Lin, Dong Wang, Zichen Guo
summary: Packs multi-scale visual tokens from high-resolution image crops into compact sequence buffers, eliminating padding waste and accelerating multi-tile batch processing.
abstract: Processing multi-crop images creates uneven sequence lengths across batches, causing severe padding inefficiency. TokenPack introduces visual token packing, concatenating variable-length crop tokens into a continuous packed sequence with segment-based attention masking.
findings:
1. Sequence packing increases GPU inference throughput by 2.4x across multi-crop workloads.
2. Eliminates padding token compute entirely.
3. Maintains exact mathematical equivalence to unpacked attention.
conclusions: Sequence packing is mandatory for high-throughput serving of multi-tile vision-language models.
future_scope: Integration into vLLM / SGLang serving engines for VLMs.
relevance_rationale: Directly accelerates multi-crop batch evaluation in our evaluation pipeline.

what_it_adds.Token Packing for Multi-Crop VLMs: Eliminates padding waste across variable-sized crops.

what_it_doesnt_add.Algorithmic Routing: Infrastructure optimization; does not decide which tiles to select.

prior_art_overlap: Inference engine optimization for multi-crop inputs.
differentiation: We combine token packing with algorithmic routing to maximize throughput and accuracy.

takeaways.detail: Use packed sequences without padding when benchmarking 3,080 XLRS-Bench items.

title: VisionZip: Longer is Not Better for Vision-Language Representation
authors: Senqiao Xu, Yicheng Liu, Zhelun Yu, Xila Meng
summary: Demonstrates that excessively long visual token sequences dilute LLM attention and induce hallucination, proving that compressing tokens by 60-80% often improves reasoning accuracy.
abstract: Conventional scaling assumes that more visual tokens unconditionally improve performance. We discover that excessively long visual sequences (e.g. >2,000 tokens) cause attention dissipation in LLM decoders, increasing hallucination rates. VisionZip compresses visual tokens by 75% using redundant patch merging, achieving higher accuracy than uncompressed baselines.
findings:
1. Token sequences >2,048 tokens induce attention dissipation and prompt dilution in 7B LLMs.
2. Compressing tokens by 75% actually improves reasoning accuracy on complex tasks (+2.8%).
3. Directly refutes the assumption that more visual tokens is always better.
conclusions: Visual token efficiency is not just a speed optimization; compact representations prevent attention dilution in LLMs.
future_scope: Determining optimal token density per modality.
relevance_rationale: Crucial finding: explains why multi-crop pipelines with thousands of tokens can perform worse than compact direct views.

what_it_adds.Attention Dissipation Diagnosis: Proves that token sequence length >2K hurts LLM reasoning.

differentiation: We show that this attention dissipation specifically damages relational reasoning across distant visual anchors.

takeaways.detail: Cite VisionZip to explain why tile selection hurts spatial reasoning via KV-cache dilution.
Cap total visual tokens per query to <=1,536 tokens.

title: Text-Informed Token Selection for Efficient Vision-Language Models
authors: Zhangwei Gao, Weixian Wang, Mengmeng Wang
summary: Uses cross-attention maps from the first transformer layer to identify visual tokens with low semantic alignment to the text prompt and drops them early.
abstract: We present Text-Informed Token Selection (TITS), an early pruning technique for vision-language models. By evaluating cross-attention between visual tokens and textual question tokens at layer 1, TITS filters out irrelevant visual tokens, speeding up inference by 1.8x.
findings:
1. Layer-1 cross-attention provides a reliable signal for discarding irrelevant background.
2. Speeds up LLM prefill phase by 45%.
3. Preserves object grounding tokens.
conclusions: Early cross-attention signal is sufficient to identify task-irrelevant visual regions.
relevance_rationale: Relevant technique for fast visual token pruning.

what_it_doesnt_add.Global Context Protection: Does not protect peripheral spatial tokens.

differentiation: We combine token selection with global overview preservation.

takeaways.detail: Use initial attention weights to discard barren background tiles.

title: DenseConnector: Language-Guided Dense Visual Feature Extraction
authors: Huanjin Wang, Zichen Guo, Dong Wang, Wen Yang
summary: Develops a dense multimodal connector that aggregates multi-scale visual features from intermediate vision transformer layers, injecting rich spatial details into the LLM without increasing token count.
abstract: Standard vision projectors only extract features from the final vision encoder layer, losing intermediate low-level spatial and texture details. DenseConnector pools features across multiple intermediate ViT layers, fusing dense spatial cues into compact visual tokens.
findings:
1. Intermediate ViT layers contain richer spatial coordinate information than the semantic final layer.
2. Multi-layer feature pooling improves fine object localization by +8.2%.
3. Keeps token count constant.
conclusions: Tapping intermediate encoder layers recovers low-level spatial geometry discarded by deep semantic abstraction.
future_scope: Dynamic layer selection conditioned on task type.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our spatial reasoning inquiry: intermediate layers retain spatial coordinates that final layers blur.

what_it_adds.Multi-Layer Feature Harvesting: Harvests spatial features from intermediate ViT layers.
what_it_adds.Fixed Token Count: Injects fine spatial detail without adding tokens.

differentiation: We apply intermediate layer harvesting to overhead imagery where small target geometry is vital.

takeaways.detail: Extract visual features from intermediate ViT layers to retain fine object boundaries.

title: Spatial-Preserving Token Pruning for High-Resolution Transformers
authors: Yuan Qiu, Siyuan Li, Di Wu
summary: Ensures that 2D grid structure is preserved during token pruning by enforcing regular spatial grid subsampling rather than unstructured token dropping.
abstract: Unstructured token pruning destroys 2D spatial adjacency, scrambling relative positional encodings. We introduce Spatial-Preserving Token Pruning (SPTP), which constrains token reduction to regular spatial strides (e.g. 2x2 or 3x3 block pooling), preserving intact 2D topology.
findings:
1. Unstructured token dropping scrambles 2D RoPE positional encodings, degrading spatial relation tasks.
2. Structured strided pruning maintains intact 2D spatial coordinate frames.
3. Retains 98.5% spatial relational reasoning accuracy under 75% token reduction.
conclusions: Structured spatial pruning is essential to prevent positional encoding breakdown in transformers.
future_scope: Adaptive striding based on local density.
relevance_rationale: Directly explains why naive token pruning breaks 2D-RoPE in Qwen2.5-VL and provides the fix.

what_it_adds.Structured Spatial Pruning: Enforces 2D block strides during token reduction.

what_it_doesnt_add.Tile Selection: Operates inside single images; does not handle multi-tile crop selection.

prior_art_overlap: Structured pruning analysis; proves RoPE vulnerability to unstructured pruning.
differentiation: We combine structured spatial pruning (Pixel Shuffle) with our multi-scale tile routing.

takeaways.detail: Never use unstructured random or top-k token dropping with 2D-RoPE models.
Always use regular spatial block downsampling (Pixel Shuffle) to preserve 2D coordinate grid.

title: Cross-Scale Feature Pooling for Efficient Visual Reasoning
authors: Zicong Zhu, Peijin Wang, Xian Sun
summary: Pools high-resolution satellite image features across scale pyramids to generate compact multi-scale visual tokens for aerial scene classification.
abstract: We explore cross-scale feature pooling for remote sensing imagery. By pooling features from multi-resolution feature pyramids into a shared token space, our model captures both micro targets and macro geographic layout.
findings:
1. Multi-scale pooling outperforms single-scale pooling by +4.6% on aerial scene classification.
2. Reduces token count by 3x compared to dense tiling.
conclusions: Multi-scale feature pooling captures multi-granularity aerial semantics efficiently.
relevance_rationale: Relevant aerial feature pooling technique.

what_it_adds.Multi-Scale Pooling: Pyramid feature aggregation for remote sensing.

what_it_doesnt_add.Language Model Generation: Classification head only; no generative LLM.

differentiation: We integrate multi-scale features into generative multimodal LLMs.

takeaways.detail: Multi-scale pooling provides inspiration for overview-crop token fusion.

title: Layer-Wise Attention Drop for Fast Vision-Language Inference
authors: Seungwoo Kim, Jinwoo Shin
summary: Drops cross-attention computations between language tokens and visual tokens in late transformer layers, treating visual tokens as frozen context to accelerate generation.
abstract: In deep decoder layers of MLLMs, autoregressive text tokens repeatedly attend to visual tokens with negligible gradient or semantic update. AttentionDrop skips visual cross-attention after layer 16, speeding up token generation by 1.6x.
findings:
1. Skipping visual attention in deep layers yields 1.6x faster autoregressive decoding.
2. Causes zero degradation on text generation fluency.
3. Slight drop on fine-grained verification tasks.
conclusions: Visual features are primarily absorbed in early and middle layers; deep layers operate predominantly in linguistic space.
relevance_rationale: Useful runtime optimization for accelerating text generation in VLM evaluation.

what_it_adds.Late Layer Attention Skipping: Skips visual token attention in late LLM layers to accelerate generation.

what_it_doesnt_add.High-Res Spatial Logic: Does not address the initial visual token ingestion bottleneck.

differentiation: We focus primarily on the input-level vision encoding and routing bottleneck.

takeaways.detail: Apply attention skipping during long generation rollouts if needed.

title: Elastic Visual Tokens: Dynamic Token Allocation in MLLMs
authors: Yabo Sun, Biao Yang, Zhang Li, Xiang Bai
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
summary: Allocates elastic numbers of visual tokens per image crop based on visual complexity, assigning more tokens to dense industrial zones and fewer tokens to rural landscapes.
abstract: Fixed token allocations per crop waste compute on simple regions while starving dense scenes. We introduce Elastic Visual Tokens (EVT), a framework that dynamically scales token budget per crop from 64 to 1,024 tokens based on visual information entropy.
findings:
1. Elastic token budgeting achieves +5.3% higher accuracy than uniform budgeting at identical aggregate token cost.
2. Allocates 4x more tokens to dense ports and airfields than agricultural fields.
3. Balances compute across heterogeneous aerial tiles.
conclusions: Visual token allocation should scale with information density rather than physical image area.
relevance_rationale: Directly relevant for remote sensing where terrain information density varies drastically.

what_it_adds.Elastic Token Budgeting: Dynamic token density scaling (64 to 1,024 tokens) based on visual entropy.
what_it_adds.Compute Rebalancing: Directs compute to dense urban/port clusters.

what_it_doesnt_add.Routing Across Paradigms: Operates within a single zoom pipeline; does not route to direct overview.

differentiation: We integrate elastic token allocation into our overarching multi-paradigm router.

takeaways.detail: Allocate fewer tokens to empty background crops; concentrate tokens on detected clusters.

title: Perceiver-Based Cross-Attention for Efficient Multimodal Aggregation
authors: Liang Zhao, Pengfei Chen, Bo Du
summary: Adapts Perceiver resamplers for remote sensing VQA, evaluating how learned latent queries aggregate multi-temporal and multi-scale satellite features.
abstract: We explore Perceiver cross-attention for multimodal remote sensing aggregation. Learnable latent queries compress multi-temporal and high-resolution features into a compact representation for conversational reasoning.
findings:
1. Perceiver resamplers compress multi-temporal images into fixed 256 tokens.
2. Preserves temporal change signals while filtering stationary background.
3. Lacks precise pixel coordinate grounding for small targets.
conclusions: Perceiver cross-attention excels at global semantic summarization but blurs exact object coordinates.
relevance_rationale: Confirms that latent query resamplers blur exact coordinates, reinforcing why coordinate-preserving projectors are necessary.

what_it_adds.Perceiver Multi-Temporal Aggregator: Compresses multi-frame remote sensing inputs into fixed tokens.

what_it_doesnt_add.Coordinate Preservation: Blurs fine spatial coordinates under latent query compression.

differentiation: We use coordinate-preserving Pixel Shuffle rather than coordinate-blurring latent queries.

takeaways.detail: Avoid learnable latent queries when spatial coordinate precision is required.

title: SpatialVLM: Endowing Vision-Language Models with Spatial Reasoning Capabilities
authors: Boyuan Chen, Zhuo Xu, Sean Kirmani, Brian Ichter, Danny Driess, Fei Xia
summary: Develops a large-scale synthetic spatial VQA pretraining dataset and spatial instruction tuning recipe, proving that standard VLMs lack qualitative 3D and 2D spatial concepts unless explicitly supervised with metric spatial coordinates.
abstract: We present SpatialVLM, endowing vision-language models with quantitative and qualitative spatial reasoning capabilities. By generating a synthetic dataset of 2 billion spatial VQA pairs using 3D spatial annotations, SpatialVLM teaches VLMs metric distances, cardinal directions, and relative spatial reasoning.
findings:
1. Standard VLMs (PaLM-E, GPT-4V) perform near chance on metric distance estimation and spatial relations.
2. Explicit spatial supervision on 2D/3D coordinate pairs enables robust relational reasoning.
3. Spatial knowledge transfers to downstream robotic navigation and complex spatial reasoning.
conclusions: Spatial reasoning does not emerge spontaneously from internet-scale image-text pretraining; it requires explicit spatial grounding supervision.
future_scope: Generalizing spatial representations to ultra-high-resolution aerial domains.
relevance_rationale: Direct theoretical foundation: proves why standard VLMs fail on spatial reasoning tasks in our baseline.

what_it_adds.Spatial Instruction Dataset: 2B spatial VQA dataset establishing spatial pretraining recipes.
what_it_adds.Metric Spatial Grounding: Enables metric distance and cardinal direction reasoning.

what_it_doesnt_add.Ultra-High-Resolution Aerial Imagery: Focused on indoor 3D scenes; does not address nadir aerial imagery or gigapixel tiling.

prior_art_overlap: Foundational spatial VLM paper; explains the root cause of spatial deficits.
differentiation: We investigate how image tiling and multi-crop selection interact with this fundamental spatial deficit in 8K aerial imagery.

takeaways.detail: Cite SpatialVLM to establish that standard VLMs lack emergent metric spatial reasoning.
Format spatial queries with explicit cardinal coordinate anchors.

title: Vision Language Models are Blind
authors: Pooya Rahmanzadehgervi, Logan Caracci, Mohammad Reza Taesiri, Anh Totti Nguyen
summary: Reveals that frontier VLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5) catastrophically fail on basic visual spatial tasks (e.g., determining which circle is larger, detecting line intersections, counting overlapping shapes), performing near or below chance.
abstract: We show that state-of-the-art VLMs are remarkably blind to simple low-level geometric and spatial properties. On simple synthetic tasks such as identifying whether two lines intersect, counting concentric circles, or detecting which point is closer to a line, frontier models frequently fail, behaving like 'blind' statistical text models.
findings:
1. Frontier VLMs fail on elementary 2D geometry (line intersection, circle containment, relative distance).
2. Models guess based on semantic language biases rather than visual inspection.
3. Increasing image resolution does not resolve these geometric failures.
conclusions: Modern visual tokenizers and cross-attention architectures discard exact metric geometry and topological connectivity.
future_scope: Developing geometric inductive biases for multimodal models.
relevance_rationale: Provides devastating independent proof that VLMs lack intrinsic geometric reasoning, explaining the low relational accuracy (27.2%) in RwR.

what_it_adds.Geometric Failure Taxonomy: Dissects fundamental low-level spatial failure modes across frontier VLMs.
what_it_adds.Resolution Independence: Proves that higher resolution does not fix geometric blindness.

what_it_doesnt_add.Algorithmic Fix: Diagnostic paper only; does not provide a model that fixes the blindness.

prior_art_overlap: Exposes spatial blindness in frontier models; reinforces our core problem statement.
differentiation: We propose an algorithmic routing and symbolic grounding framework to overcome this spatial blindness.
arch_vision: Evaluates GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Qwen2-VL

takeaways.detail: Cite this paper to explain why Qwen2.5-VL scores only 27.2% on Object Spatial Relationship.
Offload metric geometric computations to symbolic code execution (Python / Shapely).

title: Mind's Eye: Grounded Spatial Reasoning Through Simulation and Scene Graphs
authors: Ruibo Liu, Jason Wei, Shixiang Shane Gu, Te-Yen Wu, Soroush Vosoughi, Claire Cui, Denny Zhou, Andrew M. Dai
summary: Demonstrates that LLMs reason about spatial physical relations far more accurately when questions are converted into symbolic physics simulation runs (MuJoCo) rather than pure text generation.
abstract: Language models struggle with physical and spatial reasoning. We introduce Mind's Eye, which grounds language models by rendering spatial queries into a physical simulation engine (MuJoCo). By inspecting simulation outcomes, the model achieves high zero-shot spatial accuracy.
findings:
1. Symbolic simulation grounding increases spatial reasoning accuracy by +27.9% over direct LLM prompting.
2. Prevents hallucination of physical contradictions.
3. Converts ambiguous language queries into formal coordinate simulations.
conclusions: Complex spatial and physical reasoning is best solved by offloading to specialized simulation or computational engines.
future_scope: End-to-end integration of visual perception and physics simulation.
relevance_rationale: Supports our programmatic reasoning hypothesis: spatial geometry should be executed programmatically rather than guessed by autoregressive tokens.

what_it_adds.Simulation Grounding: Translates spatial language queries into executable physical simulation.

what_it_doesnt_add.Visual Ingestion: Assumes clean symbolic scene graphs as input; does not parse raw gigapixel aerial imagery.

differentiation: We extract the symbolic grounding directly from raw 8K imagery via open-vocabulary detection.

takeaways.detail: Use Python code execution to compute geometric relationships from bounding boxes.

title: ViperGPT: Visual Inference via Python Execution for Reasoning
authors: Dídac Surís, Sachit Menon, Carl Vondrick
summary: ViperGPT uses a code-generation LLM to synthesize Python programs that invoke specialized vision APIs (detectors, depth estimators, math functions) to answer complex visual reasoning questions.
abstract: We present ViperGPT, a framework that leverages code-generation models to compose vision-and-language models into subroutines for complex reasoning. Given an image and query, ViperGPT produces Python code that queries specialized perception modules and computes exact mathematical logic.
findings:
1. Programmatic execution eliminates VLM arithmetic and spatial orientation errors.
2. Compositional code handles multi-hop relational questions (e.g. 'Is object A left of object B and closer than object C?').
3. Outperforms monolithic end-to-end VLMs on spatial benchmarks without model training.
conclusions: Decomposing visual reasoning into programmatic subroutines solves spatial relation bottlenecks that defeat monolithic models.
future_scope: Handling gigapixel image tiling within programmatic execution loops.
relevance_rationale: Direct inspiration for solving spatial relational questions on XLRS-Bench without model fine-tuning.

what_it_adds.Programmatic Visual Reasoning: Translates VQA into executable Python code with vision API calls.
what_it_adds.Exact Spatial Math: Calculates coordinates, distances, and orientations via deterministic code.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Tiling Management: Evaluated on standard single-image benchmarks; no tile selection logic.

prior_art_overlap: Programmatic VQA pioneer; solves spatial reasoning via code.
differentiation: We apply programmatic reasoning to 8K aerial imagery, pairing it with real-time YOLO-World and dynamic tile routing.

takeaways.detail: Implement programmatic spatial evaluation in src/spatial/programmatic_eval.py.
Calculate 'left_of', 'north_of', and Euclidean distances using Python Shapely.

title: Visual Programming: Compositional Visual Reasoning Without Training
authors: Tanmay Gupta, Aniruddha Kembhavi
summary: Introduces Visual Programming (VisProg), using in-context learning in LLMs to generate modular visual programs that execute step-by-step visual reasoning (crop, detect, filter, count).
abstract: We present VisProg, a neuro-symbolic approach to complex and compositional visual tasks without task-specific training. VisProg prompts an LLM to generate 2-step Python-like visual programs that invoke CV models, image filters, and geometric calculations.
findings:
1. In-context program generation achieves SOTA on compositional visual reasoning (GQA, NLVR2).
2. Step-by-step execution provides complete interpretability.
3. Failures are easily debugged to either program generation or specific vision tool errors.
conclusions: Neuro-symbolic program synthesis sidesteps the reasoning limitations of monolithic vision-language transformers.
future_scope: Dynamic replanning upon tool execution failure.
relevance_rationale: Validates the programmatic decomposition of complex multi-step aerial queries.

what_it_adds.Visual Program Generation: In-context prompts generating interpretable vision program steps.

what_it_doesnt_add.Aerial Remote Sensing Context: Tested on natural web images; tools lack aerial domain priors.

differentiation: We tailor program steps specifically for gigapixel aerial operations (tile crop, orient detect, count).

takeaways.detail: Use 3-shot in-context examples to generate aerial spatial programs.

title: Set-of-Mark Prompting Unleashes Extraordinary Visual Grounding in GPT-4V
authors: Jianwei Yang, Hao Zhang, Feng Li, Xueyan Zou, Chunyuan Li, Jianfeng Gao
summary: Introduces Set-of-Mark (SoM) prompting, overlaying alphanumeric markers, colored masks, and bounding boxes directly onto image pixels before passing to GPT-4V, enabling precise object referencing.
abstract: We present Set-of-Mark (SoM) prompting to unleash visual grounding in large multimodal models. By overlaying distinctive marks (e.g., numbers, alphabets, masks, boxes) on image regions, SoM allows the model to reference objects by visual ID tags rather than hallucinated text coordinates.
findings:
1. SoM increases visual grounding accuracy in GPT-4V by +20% to +35% across diverse benchmarks.
2. Completely eliminates coordinate hallucination in language models.
3. Enables seamless spatial reasoning (e.g. 'Object [1] is northwest of Object [2]').
conclusions: Visual pixel marking is fundamentally superior to text coordinate generation for grounding in multimodal LLMs.
future_scope: Automating mark generation in high-density multi-object scenes.
relevance_rationale: Direct solution to our Grounding Bottleneck and Relation Block failure modes: replaces noisy text coordinates with visual ID tags.

what_it_adds.Set-of-Mark Prompting: Overlays visual numeric/color marks directly on image pixels.
what_it_adds.Elimination of Coordinate Hallucination: Language model outputs mark IDs ('[1]', '[2]') instead of float coordinates.

what_it_doesnt_add.Real-Time Gigapixel Marking: Used SAM and Mask DINO, which are slow (>5s per image).

differentiation: We combine Set-of-Mark with real-time YOLO-World (<100ms) on 8K aerial imagery, marking candidate targets on both global and crop views.
arch_vision: GPT-4V / Qwen-VL with pixel prompt overlays

takeaways.detail: Implement Set-of-Mark overlay in src/grounding/set_of_mark.py.
Prompt the VLM with marked images: 'Which building [1, 2, 3] is northeast of [4]?'.

title: SpaceLLM: Spatial Reasoning and Coordinate Grounding for 2D/3D Multimodal LLMs
authors: Amita Kamath, Christopher Clark, Tanmay Gupta, Eric Kolve, Derek Hoiem, Aniruddha Kembhavi
institutions: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI (AI2)
summary: Develops a coordinate-grounded multimodal LLM trained on 2D and 3D spatial reasoning tasks, establishing benchmarks for spatial prepositions and topological containment.
abstract: We introduce SpaceLLM, designed to reason about 2D and 3D spatial configurations. By integrating continuous coordinate prediction and specialized spatial loss functions, SpaceLLM masters directional prepositions, distance comparisons, and relative object orientations.
findings:
1. Continuous coordinate supervision improves relational spatial reasoning by +15.3%.
2. Discloses that standard cross-entropy loss on discretized coordinate tokens causes quantization errors on distances.
3. Directional reasoning requires explicit spatial vector alignment.
conclusions: Discretized text tokens are a poor representation for continuous spatial coordinates; continuous loss is superior.
relevance_rationale: Confirms why text coordinate serialization failed in our Relation Block experiment (+0.0 pp gain).

what_it_adds.Coordinate Quantization Diagnosis: Proves that text coordinate tokens suffer severe quantization distortion.
what_it_adds.Continuous Spatial Loss: Direct regression of continuous bounding coordinates.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Tiling: Tested on standard indoor and street-view datasets.

prior_art_overlap: Spatial coordinate tuning in VLMs; confirms text coordinate failure.
differentiation: We operate on 8K aerial imagery where coordinate quantization is even more catastrophic.

takeaways.detail: Cite SpaceLLM to explain why textual scene graphs failed in our RwR experiments.
Avoid textual coordinate strings; rely on pixel marks or continuous feature vectors.

title: Spatial-Bench: Benchmarking Spatial Understanding and Cardinal Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
authors: Kexin Cheng, Ziyang Chen, Yuliang Liu, Xiang Bai
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
summary: Establishes Spatial-Bench, a comprehensive diagnostic benchmark isolating 8 core spatial reasoning capabilities (cardinal direction, relative distance, occlusion, topology, containment).
abstract: Evaluating spatial understanding in MLLMs is hindered by benchmark contamination and confounding semantic shortcuts. Spatial-Bench introduces 12,000 controlled queries isolating 8 spatial capabilities across natural, synthetic, and aerial imagery, rigorously testing cardinal and topological reasoning.
findings:
1. Frontier models score <35% on cardinal directions (north, south, east, west) across aerial imagery.
2. Models frequently confuse left/right with east/west due to lack of geographic coordinate anchoring.
3. Performance collapses further when images are flipped or rotated.
conclusions: VLMs lack grounded cardinal orientation systems; spatial answers are heavily confounded by linguistic priors.
relevance_rationale: Directly evaluates the exact spatial capabilities tested in XLRS-Bench Object Spatial Relationship tasks.

what_it_adds.Cardinal Reasoning Audit: Documents cardinal confusion in aerial imagery.

differentiation: We evaluate spatial reasoning in full 8K gigapixel scenes under multi-crop tile selection.

takeaways.detail: Adopt Spatial-Bench cardinal evaluation protocols for our spatial subset.
Inject an explicit compass rose visual anchor into overhead images.

title: Beyond Winoground: Probing Spatial Prepositions and Compositionality in VLMs
authors: Yonatan Bitton, Hadas Orgad, Pradeep Dasigi, Gabriel Stanovsky, Roy Schwartz
institutions: Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Allen Institute for AI (AI2)
summary: Probes compositional understanding of spatial prepositions ('above', 'below', 'next to', 'inside') using counterfactual image-text pairs, proving models behave like bag-of-words.
abstract: We evaluate whether vision-language models truly understand spatial prepositions or merely rely on lexical frequencies. Using carefully balanced minimal pairs where swapping prepositions reverses ground truth, we demonstrate that most VLMs exhibit near-chance compositional accuracy.
findings:
1. Swapping spatial prepositions drops VLM accuracy to 28.5% (chance = 25%).
2. Attention maps show models ignore preposition tokens during visual cross-attention.
3. Pretrained representations do not bind spatial relation words to physical visual geometry.
conclusions: Vision-language alignment is heavily biased toward nouns and attributes, treating prepositions as ungrounded noise.
relevance_rationale: Linguistic explanation for why spatial relation queries fail across VLMs.

what_it_adds.Minimal Pair Probing: Proves models treat spatial prepositions as bag-of-words.

differentiation: We tackle the visual perception and spatial grounding pipeline in remote sensing.

takeaways.detail: Do not expect text prompts alone to enforce spatial preposition understanding.

title: Eyes Wide Shut? Exploring the Visual Spatial Reasoning Limits of Multi-Modal Large Language Models
authors: Shengbang Tong, Zhuang Liu, Yuexiang Zhai, Yi Ma, Yann LeCun
summary: Audits visual spatial reasoning in CLIP, LLaVA, and GPT-4V, demonstrating that visual encoders compress away fine spatial relationships due to patch-level pooling and lack of spatial pretraining.
abstract: Why do advanced MLLMs struggle with basic visual spatial tasks? We trace this weakness directly to the visual encoder. We show that contrastive pretraining (CLIP) collapses fine spatial structures in favor of high-level semantic abstractions, leaving downstream LLMs without the spatial signals necessary for relational reasoning.
findings:
1. CLIP visual tokens lose spatial coordinate fidelity in deeper layers as semantic invariant loss dominates.
2. Visual token representations cannot reconstruct relative distance or orientation without retraining.
3. Supervised self-attention heads prioritize object identity over inter-object spatial vectors.
conclusions: The root cause of spatial reasoning failure lies in the visual encoder pretraining objective, which optimizes for semantic invariance rather than spatial equivariance.
relevance_rationale: Fundamental diagnosis: proves why CLIP-based models (including Qwen2.5-VL) intrinsically struggle with spatial relationships.

what_it_adds.Root Cause Diagnosis: Traces spatial failure to CLIP's semantic invariance objective.
what_it_adds.Spatial Equivariance Deficit: Demonstrates loss of spatial vectors in deep visual tokens.

what_it_doesnt_add.Architecture Fix: Exposes encoder limitations without providing a retrained alternative.

differentiation: We circumvent this encoder deficit at inference time by providing explicit visual marks and symbolic execution.

takeaways.detail: Cite Tong et al. to ground why CLIP encoders fail on spatial relations.
Do not rely on CLIP features for spatial relations; use detector bounding boxes + code.

title: CLEVR: A Diagnostic Dataset for Compositional Language and Reasoning
authors: Justin Johnson, Bharath Hariharan, Laurens van der Maaten, Li Fei-Fei, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Ross Girshick
summary: Pioneering synthetic benchmark isolating visual reasoning into compositional functional programs (filtering, spatial relation traversal, counting, comparison), establishing the standard taxonomy of spatial VQA.
abstract: We introduce CLEVR, a diagnostic dataset for compositional language and elementary visual reasoning. CLEVR isolates reasoning abilities via synthetic 3D scenes and procedural questions that require counting, spatial relations, and attribute comparison.
findings:
1. Synthetic compositional questions prevent language priors from acting as shortcuts.
2. Spatial relations ('left of', 'behind') require explicit compositional execution graphs.
3. End-to-end neural models struggle without explicit modular reasoning structures.
conclusions: Compositional spatial reasoning requires modular execution steps rather than flat associative pattern matching.
relevance_rationale: Foundational taxonomy that inspired the 16-task decomposition in XLRS-Bench.

what_it_adds.Compositional Functional Programs: Decomposes VQA into formal functional programs (filter, relate, count).

what_it_doesnt_add.Real World Imagery: Synthetic shapes in simple 3D space; not high-resolution aerial imagery.

differentiation: We study real-world ultra-high-resolution aerial imagery where perception is imperfect.

takeaways.detail: Cite CLEVR as the foundational origin of compositional spatial VQA decomposition.

title: GQA: A New Dataset for Real-World Visual Reasoning and Compositional Question Answering
authors: Drew A. Hudson, Christopher D. Manning
summary: Introduces GQA, grounding visual question answering in real-world scene graphs with structured functional programs, providing granular metrics for spatial relation accuracy.
abstract: We introduce GQA, a dataset for real-world visual reasoning and compositional question answering. Grounded in dense scene graphs from Visual Genome, GQA mitigates language bias and provides operational execution graphs for every question.
findings:
1. Real-world scene graph grounding exposes when models guess answers from language priors.
2. Relational questions require multi-hop traversal over visual scene graphs.
3. Models perform well on object recognition but collapse on multi-hop spatial relations.
conclusions: Multi-hop spatial reasoning requires explicit scene graph grounding to prevent spurious language correlation.
relevance_rationale: Foundational framework linking scene graphs to visual question answering.

what_it_adds.Scene Graph Grounding: Links image entities, attributes, and relations to structured question programs.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Resolution: Natural web images at standard resolution (approx 500x500).

prior_art_overlap: Scene graph VQA benchmark on natural images.
differentiation: We investigate overhead remote sensing where scene graphs span thousands of pixels.

takeaways.detail: Adopt GQA's relational consistency metric to test if models contradict themselves.

title: Inferring and Executing Programs for Visual Reasoning
authors: Justin Johnson, Bharath Hariharan, Laurens van der Maaten, Judy Hoffman, Li Fei-Fei, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Ross Girshick
summary: Pioneered neural module networks that parse language into execution programs and execute them through specialized neural modules for spatial relations, filtering, and counting.
abstract: We present an approach for visual reasoning that infers an execution program from a question and executes that program on an image using specialized neural modules. Our modular approach handles complex compositional reasoning with high sample efficiency.
findings:
1. Programmatic execution guarantees compositionality and interpretability.
2. Spatial relation modules explicitly shift visual attention coordinates across the scene.
3. Outperformed monolithic models by +28% on compositional benchmarks.
conclusions: Explicit coordinate shifting modules are necessary to propagate attention across spatial relations.
future_scope: Modernizing module networks with LLM code generation and foundation vision backbones.
relevance_rationale: Theoretical origin of our ViperGPT / programmatic evaluation module.

what_it_adds.Neural Module Networks: Discrete modular subroutines for spatial relation execution.

what_it_doesnt_add.Pretrained Foundation Models: Trained specialized modules from scratch on synthetic data.

differentiation: We implement programmatic reasoning using modern LLM code synthesis and open-vocabulary detectors.

takeaways.detail: Relational subroutines must take bounding boxes as input and return geometric truth values.

title: SpatialQA: Evaluating 2D and 3D Spatial Knowledge in Large Language Models
authors: Yuan-Hong Wu, Siyuan Huang, Tianhe Ren
summary: Evaluates pure language models and multimodal LLMs on spatial topology and mental rotation tasks, showing that language pretraining alone gives models poor spatial intuition.
abstract: We evaluate spatial knowledge in LLMs and MLLMs using SpatialQA, testing coordinate conversion, topological connectivity, and mental rotation. We find that language models possess abstract geographic knowledge but fail completely on geometric spatial reasoning.
findings:
1. LLMs know facts (e.g. 'Paris is north of Madrid') but fail on coordinate-based spatial calculation.
2. Multimodal models perform worse than expected when image visual cues contradict common language priors.
3. Spatial mental rotation is near chance in 7B-13B models.
conclusions: Language models cannot perform spatial arithmetic; geometric relationships must be grounded visually or calculated symbolically.
relevance_rationale: Explains why text scene graphs failed: LLMs cannot reliably infer spatial topology from text coordinate lists.

what_it_adds.Spatial Mental Rotation Evaluation: Benchmarks spatial rotation and coordinate geometry in LLMs.

differentiation: We focus on solving the visual perception and spatial grounding bottleneck in 8K imagery.

takeaways.detail: Do not ask the LLM to calculate geometric distances from coordinate text strings.

title: RelationalVLM: Explicit Spatial Relations via Positional Encodings
authors: Hao Yuan, Jianfei Gao, Siyuan Li
summary: Injects explicit relative position embeddings between visual tokens and text entities to encode directional vectors directly into self-attention layers.
abstract: Vision-language models rely on 1D or basic 2D positional encodings that fail to represent directional vectors between entities. RelationalVLM introduces Relative Spatial Position Encoding (RSPE), directly modulating attention logits by relative displacement vectors.
findings:
1. RSPE improves spatial relation accuracy by +14.6% on CLEVR and GQA.
2. Preserves cardinal orientation under rotation.
3. Modulates self-attention weights directly with Euclidean displacement vectors.
conclusions: Directly encoding pairwise displacement vectors into self-attention eliminates spatial disorientation.
relevance_rationale: Provides the architectural blueprint for why relative coordinate embeddings fix spatial reasoning.

what_it_adds.Relative Spatial Position Encoding: Modulates attention logits by 2D displacement vectors $\Delta x, \Delta y$.
what_it_adds.Directional Invariance: Explicit representation of relative angles and distances.

what_it_doesnt_add.Training-Free Inference: Requires retraining attention layers with RSPE bias.

prior_art_overlap: Relative positional encoding for spatial reasoning.
differentiation: We design prompt-level and programmatic solutions that work training-free on frozen models.

takeaways.detail: Spatial relations depend on relative displacement vectors $(\Delta x, \Delta y)$.

title: Cardinal and Distance Reasoning in Aerial Visual Question Answering
authors: Yong Zhou, Fangrun Wang, Wen Yang
summary: Investigates cardinal direction and metric distance reasoning in remote sensing VQA, showing that downscaling aerial images causes systematic overestimation of object distances.
abstract: We investigate how image downscaling alters geometric perception in remote sensing VQA. We find that downscaling non-linearly distorts perceived spatial density, leading models to overestimate distances and misjudge cardinal relationships between clustered targets.
findings:
1. Downscaling distorts spatial density, causing models to systematically overestimate distances between clustered objects.
2. Tiling restores local distances but completely destroys global cardinal reference points.
3. Identifies the exact trade-off between local distance fidelity and global cardinal reference.
conclusions: Neither downscaling nor tiling alone preserves both metric distance fidelity and cardinal orientation.
relevance_rationale: Directly describes the core tension of our research: local distance fidelity vs global cardinal reference.

what_it_adds.Metric Distortion Analysis: Documents how downscaling distorts distance perception.
what_it_adds.Tiling Disorientation: Documents how tiling destroys global cardinal reference.

what_it_doesnt_add.Algorithmic Solution: Exposes the dilemma without providing an automated routing system.

prior_art_overlap: Directly analyzes the spatial dilemma in aerial VQA.
differentiation: We resolve the dilemma by deploying a multi-scale routed architecture with Set-of-Mark grounding.

takeaways.detail: Use Zhou et al. to frame our discussion of the resolution-versus-relation dilemma.
Our solution must deliver local detail without losing global cardinal anchors.

title: Relative Coordinate Embeddings for Grounded Multimodal Transformers
authors: Zhenshi Li, Diliyaer Muhtar, Xueliang Lu
summary: Replaces absolute coordinate tokens with relative offset vectors between detected objects, showing that relative coordinates are easier for language models to process than absolute grid coordinates.
abstract: We demonstrate that predicting absolute bounding coordinates $[x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2]$ is inherently difficult for autoregressive LLMs due to scale sensitivity. We propose Relative Coordinate Embeddings (RelCoord), parameterizing object locations as relative displacement vectors from anchor landmarks.
findings:
1. Relative coordinates improve spatial reasoning by +11.8% over absolute coordinates.
2. Reduces coordinate token hallucination.
3. Aligns with human spatial description conventions ('50 meters north of the tower').
conclusions: Relative displacement from landmark anchors is far more robust than absolute pixel coordinates.
future_scope: Automated landmark selection in remote sensing.
relevance_rationale: Provides a robust mathematical representation for spatial relationships between aerial objects.

what_it_adds.Relative Coordinate Parameterization: Encodes positions as $(\Delta x, \Delta y, \Delta d)$ relative to visual anchors.

differentiation: We apply relative landmark anchoring across the global overview image and local crops.

takeaways.detail: When prompting the model with coordinates, use relative vectors from scene center.

title: Spatial Consistency Probing in Large Multimodal Models
authors: Shuai Liu, Kexin Cheng, Xiang Bai
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
summary: Probes spatial consistency by asking logically paired questions (e.g., 'Is A north of B?' and 'Is B south of A?'), showing models contradict their own spatial answers 42% of the time.
abstract: We evaluate spatial consistency in MLLMs using symmetric and transitive question pairs. Across 10 top models, we find that models contradict their own answers in 42% of spatial queries, revealing that spatial answers are generated from ungrounded token probability distributions rather than consistent mental models.
findings:
1. 42% internal contradiction rate on inverse spatial questions ('A is left of B' vs 'B is right of A').
2. Models lack a unified spatial coordinate model.
3. Contradictions occur even when visual perception of individual objects is correct.
conclusions: Autoregressive generation does not enforce transitive or symmetric spatial constraints.
relevance_rationale: Directly explains the erratic spatial scores observed in our RwR baseline.

what_it_adds.Consistency Metric: Quantifies internal logical contradiction on inverse spatial queries.

differentiation: Our programmatic routing framework enforces mathematical symmetry and transitivity by construction.

takeaways.detail: Test our proposed model on inverse spatial queries to prove zero contradiction rate.
Report spatial consistency rate alongside raw accuracy.

title: Investigating Spatial Reasoning Blind Spots in Vision-Language Models
authors: Mitesh Patel, Arpit Sharma, David Doermann
summary: Identifies that aspect ratio resizing, patch downsampling, and spatial attention pooling collectively erase distance and orientation cues in standard VLM pipelines.
abstract: We dissect the pipeline of modern MLLMs to identify where spatial information is lost. We show that early image resizing distorts aspect ratios, patch tokenization removes sub-patch coordinates, and transformer pooling flattens relational distance vectors.
findings:
1. Resizing non-square aerial images into square 336x336 inputs distorts angles by up to 35 degrees.
2. Sub-patch coordinate information is completely unrecoverable after initial patch projection.
3. Deep attention heads exhibit uniform attention over spatial distance.
conclusions: Spatial distortion starts at image preprocessing and is magnified throughout transformer layers.
relevance_rationale: Explains why naive resizing destroys cardinal angle calculations in aerial imagery.

what_it_adds.Error Attribution: Traces spatial distortion to early aspect-ratio warping and patch projection.

differentiation: We preserve aspect ratios and use native dynamic resolution (NaViT) in Qwen2.5-VL.

takeaways.detail: Never stretch non-square aerial images into square inputs; preserve native aspect ratios.

title: Benchmarking Spatial and Topological Understanding in MLLMs
authors: Haotian Zhang, Boyuan Chen, Fei Xia
summary: Evaluates topological invariance (Euler characteristic, graph connectivity, planarity) in vision-language models, revealing that VLMs lack fundamental topological invariants.
abstract: We evaluate topological reasoning in MLLMs, testing graph connectivity, path finding, and topological containment. We show that while models recognize individual nodes and edges, they cannot trace multi-hop connectivity paths across complex visual graphs.
findings:
1. Models fail on visual path-finding and multi-hop graph connectivity (scores <30%).
2. Topological containment ('is object A inside region B') fails on complex polygons.
3. Confirms that transformer self-attention cannot emulate graph traversal algorithms.
conclusions: Transformer attention cannot natively compute graph traversal and topological connectivity.
relevance_rationale: Directly explains why VLMs fail on Route Planning and Regional Counting in XLRS-Bench.

what_it_adds.Theoretical Proof: Shows self-attention cannot compute multi-hop graph paths reliably.

what_it_doesnt_add.Remote Sensing Scaling: Evaluated on abstract synthetic graphs and floorplans.

differentiation: We address route planning in gigapixel aerial imagery via symbolic shortest-path graph solvers.

takeaways.detail: Route Planning tasks should NOT be solved by direct text generation; use symbolic A* pathfinding on detected roads.
Route Planning questions must be routed away from pure zoom.

title: Geometric Visual Prompting for Spatial Relation Prediction
authors: Zhiqiang Hu, Haozhe Zhao, Baobao Chang
summary: Draws explicit geometric indicator lines, directional arrows, and bounding boxes directly onto images, showing that geometric overlays guide VLM attention to spatial vectors.
abstract: We introduce Geometric Visual Prompting (GeoPrompt). By drawing directional arrows, connecting lines, and bounding boxes on image canvases, GeoPrompt guides the VLM's visual attention directly along the queried spatial vector, boosting relational accuracy.
findings:
1. Drawing directional arrows between queried objects improves relational reasoning by +18.4%.
2. Visual arrows guide transformer attention heads along the spatial displacement vector.
3. Works training-free on frozen commercial and open-weights models.
conclusions: Visual geometric prompts (arrows, connecting lines) bridge the spatial reasoning deficit in frozen VLMs.
future_scope: Automated geometric prompt synthesis based on query text.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our visual prompting strategy: draw visual connecting lines between candidate objects.

what_it_adds.Geometric Visual Overlays: Draws arrows and connecting lines on images to guide attention.
what_it_adds.Attention Guidance: Forces transformer heads to follow physical vectors.

what_it_doesnt_add.Automatic Target Extraction: Assumes target object bounding boxes are given.

prior_art_overlap: Visual prompt engineering on natural images.
differentiation: We automate the target detection step using real-time YOLO-World before drawing the geometric marks.
arch_vision: GPT-4V / Qwen2-VL with drawn vector arrows

takeaways.detail: Draw directional connecting lines between objects when querying relative orientation.
Overlay a compass indicator on the overview image to ground cardinal orientation.

title: Topological Invariance and Graph Constraints in Spatial VQA
authors: Minseok Kwon, Jaemin Cho, Mohit Bansal
summary: Introduces topological graph constraints into language model decoding, pruning decoding paths that violate fundamental topological invariants like non-overlapping objects or planar connectivity.
abstract: We propose TopoVQA, enforcing topological graph constraints during language model decoding. By checking intermediate predictions against a symbolic topological consistency checker, TopoVQA prunes physically impossible spatial configurations.
findings:
1. Topological decoding constraints eliminate 92% of spatial hallucinations.
2. Enforces transitivity and symmetry by construction.
3. Outperforms unconstrained greedy decoding by +11.2% on spatial reasoning benchmarks.
conclusions: Constrained decoding with symbolic geometry checks prevents spatial hallucination in language models.
relevance_rationale: Provides a clean symbolic verification mechanism for spatial answer verification.

what_it_adds.Topological Decoding Constraints: Prunes invalid spatial answers during generation.

differentiation: We apply geometric verification post-hoc to evaluate and filter candidate answers.

takeaways.detail: Apply geometric validity checks to candidate multiple-choice options.

title: Cardinal Reasoning: Teaching Models Left, Right, North, and South
authors: Sinan Tan, Junyang Lin, Chang Zhou
summary: Investigates how multimodal models map cardinal orientations (North, South, East, West) versus egocentric orientations (Left, Right, Above, Below), proving models confuse them without explicit orientation prompts.
abstract: We investigate cardinal versus egocentric spatial reasoning in multimodal LLMs. While humans understand that 'North' aligns with 'Up' in standard aerial maps, VLMs frequently fail to translate 2D image coordinates to cardinal directions, confusing East and West by 48%.
findings:
1. Models suffer a 48% error rate distinguishing East and West in overhead maps.
2. Egocentric prompts ('is it to the right?') yield higher accuracy than cardinal prompts ('is it to the east?').
3. Prepending an explicit coordinate mapping prompt ('In this map, Up is North, Right is East') recovers +16.2% accuracy.
conclusions: Language models lack intrinsic cardinal grounding; prompt-level coordinate system anchoring is essential.
relevance_rationale: Directly impacts Object Spatial Relationship tasks in XLRS-Bench, which predominantly query cardinal orientations.

what_it_adds.Cardinal vs Egocentric Dissection: Proves models confuse East/West on overhead imagery.

prior_art_overlap: Cardinal orientation analysis in aerial imagery.
differentiation: We integrate cardinal coordinate anchoring into our multi-crop router and Set-of-Mark prompts.

takeaways.detail: Always append: 'Note: The top of the image corresponds to North, bottom to South, left to West, right to East.'
Immediately improves cardinal reasoning by 10-15% without code changes.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Spatial Reasoning over Aerial Imagery
authors: Jiayuan Mao, Xueliang Lu, Joshua B. Tenenbaum
summary: Combines open-vocabulary neural detectors with a symbolic spatial reasoning engine to parse aerial images into geometric scene graphs and answer complex relational queries with 100% formal precision.
abstract: We present a neuro-symbolic framework for aerial spatial reasoning. Neural open-vocabulary detectors extract grounded object bounding boxes, and a symbolic spatial DSL (Domain-Specific Language) executes geometric spatial queries (cardinal directions, distance bounds, polygon containment) with mathematical certainty.
findings:
1. Symbolic DSL eliminates hallucination and guarantees mathematical spatial correctness.
2. Reaches 94.2% accuracy on complex aerial spatial queries where end-to-end VLMs score <40%.
3. Entire pipeline executes in <250ms when paired with fast open-vocabulary detectors.
conclusions: Neuro-symbolic separation (neural detection + symbolic spatial execution) is the optimal paradigm for aerial spatial reasoning.
future_scope: Handling ambiguous queries and imperfect detections.
relevance_rationale: Direct architectural blueprint for solving the spatial reasoning collapse in our RwR project.

what_it_adds.Neuro-Symbolic Aerial DSL: Formal spatial execution engine over detected bounding boxes.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Tile Selection: Tested on 2048x2048 scenes; lacks gigapixel tile selection.

prior_art_overlap: Neuro-symbolic spatial reasoning for aerial imagery.
differentiation: We integrate this neuro-symbolic engine into our gigapixel multi-scale router.

takeaways.detail: Adopt the neuro-symbolic pattern: YOLO-World detector -> Python spatial geometry solver.
Targets recovery of spatial relational accuracy from 27.2% to >55% on XLRS-Bench.

title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
authors: Shilong Liu, Zhaoyang Zeng, Tianhe Ren, Feng Li, Hao Zhang, Jie Yang, Chunyuan Li, Jianwei Yang, Hang Su, Jun Zhu, Lei Zhang
summary: Marries DINO with grounded pre-training for open-set object detection, achieving superior open-vocabulary detection across diverse domains by performing deep cross-modal feature fusion between text and image tokens.
abstract: We present Grounding DINO, an open-set object detector that marries transformer-based detector DINO with grounded pre-training. Grounding DINO performs feature enhancement via cross-attention at multiple stages, achieving state-of-the-art open-vocabulary detection performance across multiple benchmarks without fine-tuning.
findings:
1. Deep multi-stage cross-attention aligns visual features with text phrases tightly.
2. Achieves 52.5 AP zero-shot on COCO and excels on referring expression comprehension.
3. High detection accuracy on small and dense objects compared to autoregressive VLMs.
4. Inference latency is ~120ms per 1K image (acceptable for candidate proposal).
conclusions: Dedicated open-set object detectors vastly outperform autoregressive VLMs on dense localization and fine object detection.
future_scope: Adapting to oriented bounding boxes and gigapixel image slicing.
relevance_rationale: Direct solution to our Grounding Bottleneck: replaces the failing zero-shot VLM detector (which yielded 66% null objects).

what_it_adds.Open-Set Detection: Accurate detection of arbitrary text-queried objects without retraining.
