relevance_rationale: Standard baseline across all multimodal benchmarks.

what_it_adds.Academic VQA Mixture: Clean data recipe balancing conversation and QA.

what_it_doesnt_add.Ultra-High Resolution: 336x336 is still far too small for gigapixel remote sensing.

differentiation: We test 8K imagery where LLaVA-1.5 scores poorly due to severe downscaling.

takeaways.detail: Standard two-layer MLP is effective, but requires multi-crop or pixel shuffle for high-res.

title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, and Text Reading
authors: Jinze Bai, Shuai Bai, Shusheng Yang, Shijie Wang, Sinan Tan, Peng Wang, Junyang Lin, Chang Zhou, Jingren Zhou
summary: Introduces Qwen-VL, integrating visual grounding, text reading, and visual dialogue via a cross-attention resampler operating on 448x448 inputs with coordinate tokens.
abstract: We introduce Qwen-VL, a comprehensive vision-language model. Qwen-VL integrates high-resolution visual processing (448x448) via a cross-attention visual resampler, supporting grounding, OCR, and multi-turn conversation with specialized bounding box tokens.
findings:
1. Cross-attention resampler compresses visual tokens from 1,024 to 256.
2. Specialized coordinate tokens format bounding boxes as `(x1, y1), (x2, y2)`.
3. Outperformed open-source peers on visual grounding and document comprehension.
conclusions: Visual resamplers balance token efficiency and visual perception for high-resolution images.
future_scope: Dynamic resolution and native aspect ratios (realized in Qwen2-VL).
relevance_rationale: Direct architectural predecessor to Qwen2.5-VL used in our experiments.

what_it_adds.Coordinate Box Tokens: Direct bounding box prediction in text output.

what_it_doesnt_add.Dynamic Aspect Ratio: Resizes images to fixed 448x448 square, distorting rectangular scenes.

differentiation: We build on its successor Qwen2.5-VL-7B and solve the spatial degradation under tile selection.

takeaways.detail: Understand the shift from Qwen-VL (fixed 448) to Qwen2-VL (native NaViT resolution).

title: Yi-VL: Large Multimodal Models from 01.AI
authors: Alex Young, Bei Chen, Chao Li, Chengen Huang, Ge Zhang, Guanwei Ding
summary: Develops Yi-VL (6B and 34B), scaling multimodal language models using dual ViT encoders (CLIP ViT-H and OpenCLIP ViT-G) concatenated through a multi-layer MLP.
abstract: We present Yi-VL, built on the Yi language model family. Yi-VL combines features from two distinct vision encoders to capture complementary semantic and low-level representations, achieving strong multimodal reasoning.
findings:
1. Concatenating two distinct vision encoders (CLIP + OpenCLIP) enriches visual representations.
2. Scales successfully to 34B language parameters.
3. Higher parameter size improves complex reasoning but does not fix small object blindness.
conclusions: Dual vision encoders provide complementary features, but language parameter scaling alone cannot overcome input resolution limits.
relevance_rationale: Shows that simply scaling LLM parameters from 7B to 34B does not fix input resolution limitations.

what_it_adds.Dual Vision Encoder Fusion: Fuses features from two distinct ViT backbones.

differentiation: We tackle the resolution bottleneck algorithmically rather than relying purely on LLM parameter scaling.

takeaways.detail: Model parameter scaling (7B -> 34B) does not solve the resolution dilemma; spatial routing is required.

title: DeepSeek-VL: Towards Real-World Vision-Language Understanding
authors: Haishi Lu, Zhenda Xie, Zhewei Yao, Chong Ruan, Xiaokang Yang
summary: Introduces DeepSeek-VL with a hybrid vision encoder combining a high-resolution convolutional branch (SAM-B, 1024x1024) and a semantic ViT branch (SigLIP, 384x384), preserving fine details and high-level semantics.
abstract: We present DeepSeek-VL, an open-source vision-language model. DeepSeek-VL processes high-resolution images (1024x1024) via a hybrid vision encoder that combines a low-level CNN encoder with a high-level ViT encoder, achieving high performance on real-world vision tasks.
findings:
1. Hybrid CNN + ViT architecture captures both fine high-frequency textures and global semantics.
2. Convolutional branch retains sharp edge coordinates for small objects.
3. Balances compute by allocating 576 tokens for 1024x1024 resolution.
conclusions: Hybrid convolutional and transformer encoders provide the best balance of fine-grained spatial acuity and semantic abstraction.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our hybrid design: convolutional/YOLO features for spatial localization, ViT for semantic reasoning.

what_it_adds.Hybrid Vision Encoder: Combines convolutional SAM-B (low-level edges) with SigLIP ViT (high-level semantics).

differentiation: We scale hybrid principles to 8K gigapixel remote sensing via selective tiling and routing.

takeaways.detail: Convolutional features preserve low-level spatial geometry far better than pure ViT features alone.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report: Multimodal Foundation Models
authors: Josh Achiam, Steven Adler, Sandhini Agarwal, Lama Ahmad, Ilge Akkaya, Florencia Leoni Aleman, Diogo Almeida, Janko Altenschmidt, Sam Altman, et al.
summary: Technical report on GPT-4 and GPT-4V, establishing the commercial multimodal frontier and defining the standard patch-tiling pricing and tokenization schema (512x512 tile grids + 85 tokens per tile).
abstract: We report the development of GPT-4, a large-scale multimodal model capable of ingesting image and text inputs and producing text outputs. GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance on professional and academic benchmarks.
findings:
1. Pioneers multi-tile high-resolution ingestion (512x512 patches, 170 tokens/tile + 85 token overview).
2. SOTA on diverse multimodal benchmarks.
3. Evaluated on XLRS-Bench: scores 44.2% overall, confirming that commercial frontier models also struggle with UHR aerial imagery.
conclusions: Multi-crop tiling is essential for high-resolution images in commercial frontier models, but gigapixel remote sensing remains an unsolved frontier.
future_scope: Continuous multi-modal generation and real-time video understanding.
relevance_rationale: Primary commercial baseline on XLRS-Bench; standardizes the 512x512 patch tiling formulation.

what_it_adds.Standard Multi-Crop Token Formulation: Standardized 512x512 crop tiling schema across industry.

what_it_doesnt_add.Open Weights / Reproducibility: Proprietary API; internal architecture and weights undisclosed.

differentiation: We build open-source reproducible architectures that match or outperform GPT-4V on XLRS-Bench.

takeaways.detail: Compare our open-source routed pipeline against GPT-4V scores reported in XLRS-Bench.

title: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking Multimodal Understanding Across Millions of Tokens
authors: Gemini Team, Google
summary: Introduces Gemini 1.5 Pro with native long-context multimodal understanding up to 2 million tokens, enabling the ingestion of entire hours of video and hundreds of high-resolution images without loss of retrieval fidelity.
abstract: We present Gemini 1.5 Pro, a highly compute-efficient multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model capable of recalling information across context windows exceeding 2 million tokens. Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves near-perfect retrieval on 'needle-in-a-haystack' across text, video, and audio.
findings:
1. 2M token context enables ingestion of hundreds of full-resolution image crops in a single forward pass.
2. 99%+ recall on multimodal needle-in-a-haystack.
3. However, spatial reasoning on aerial images still degrades due to lack of explicit coordinate grounding.
conclusions: Massive context windows solve the token budget problem, but do not automatically resolve geometric spatial reasoning deficits.
relevance_rationale: Crucial finding: proves that merely expanding context window (so all tiles fit) DOES NOT automatically solve spatial relational reasoning.

what_it_adds.2M Long-Context Window: Ingests massive visual sequences without token truncation.
what_it_adds.Empirical Lesson: Confirms long context alone does not fix spatial reasoning blindness.

what_it_doesnt_add.Geometric Inductive Biases: Still exhibits spatial disorientation on complex aerial layouts.

differentiation: We provide the geometric and routing inductive biases that long-context models lack.

takeaways.detail: Cite Gemini 1.5 Pro to prove that brute-force context expansion cannot fix the crossover dilemma without geometric anchoring.

title: The Claude 3 Model Family: Multimodal Capabilities
authors: Anthropic
summary: Technical overview of Claude 3 (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus) multimodal models, highlighting strong document comprehension, high-resolution chart parsing, and reduced hallucination rates.
abstract: We introduce Claude 3, a family of state-of-the-art vision-language models. Claude 3 sets new industry benchmarks across reasoning, math, coding, and multimodal understanding, demonstrating marked improvements in fine visual comprehension.
findings:
1. Claude 3 Opus achieves SOTA on chart, diagram, and scientific visual reasoning.
2. Ingests high-resolution images by dynamic multi-tile slicing.
3. Evaluated on XLRS-Bench: scores 45.8% overall, exhibiting the identical crossover degradation on spatial relations.
conclusions: Commercial frontier models universally suffer performance degradation on gigapixel aerial spatial relations.
relevance_rationale: High-profile commercial baseline on XLRS-Bench demonstrating universality of the crossover dilemma.

what_it_adds.Benchmark Baseline: Commercial performance ceiling across multimodal tasks.

differentiation: Our open-source routed pipeline targets matching or beating Claude 3 on XLRS-Bench.

takeaways.detail: Include Claude 3 Sonnet in comparative matrix as commercial reference.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models: Multimodal Architecture and High-Resolution Adapter
authors: Abhimanyu Dubey, Jiahui Yu, et al., Llama Team
summary: Presents Llama 3.2 Vision (11B and 90B), using a cross-attention vision adapter that splices visual tokens into frozen Llama 3 language layers without disturbing pre-trained language weights.
abstract: We present the multimodal extension of Llama 3. By incorporating a vision encoder and cross-attention adapter layers into the Llama 3 backbone, Llama 3.2 Vision achieves competitive multimodal reasoning across image, chart, and document tasks.
findings:
1. Gated cross-attention adapters preserve text reasoning while injecting visual perception.
2. Supports high-resolution tiling up to 4 tiles.
3. Preserves linguistic reasoning performance with zero regression.
conclusions: Cross-attention adapters provide modular multimodal extension of language models without catastrophic forgetting.
future_scope: Scaling to video and continuous speech.
relevance_rationale: Key open-weights foundation model alternative to Qwen2.5-VL.

what_it_adds.Cross-Attention Adapter Architecture: Gated cross-attention layers inserted every 4 transformer blocks.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Native Slicing: Caps at 4 tiles; cannot handle 8K imagery directly.

differentiation: We evaluate Qwen2.5-VL-7B and can test Llama 3.2 Vision-11B as a cross-architecture validation.

takeaways.detail: Test our routed framework on Llama-3.2-Vision-11B to confirm findings generalize beyond Qwen.

title: PaliGemma: A Versatile 3B VLM for Transfer
authors: Lucas Beyer, Andreas Steiner, Andre Susano Pinto, Alexander Kolesnikov, Xiao Wang, Daniel Salz, Maxim Neumann, Ibrahim Alabdulmohsin, Michael Tschannen, Emanuele Bugliarello, Thomas Kipf, Juraj Gotkowski, Ali Elqursh, Mostafa Dehghani, et al.
summary: Introduces PaliGemma, pairing SigLIP-SO400M with Gemma-2B via a linear projection layer, optimized for fast fine-tuning on downstream vision-language tasks including grounding and detection.
abstract: We present PaliGemma, a versatile 3B vision-language model trained for fine-tuning transfer. PaliGemma connects a SigLIP-SO400M vision encoder to a Gemma-2B language model, achieving state-of-the-art transfer results across diverse vision benchmarks.
findings:
1. Compact 3B parameter size runs in <100ms per image on modern GPUs.
2. Strong visual grounding performance when fine-tuned with coordinate tokens.
3. Native resolution support up to 896x896.
conclusions: Lightweight 3B models achieve competitive grounding performance when initialized with strong vision encoders (SigLIP).
relevance_rationale: Excellent lightweight candidate for our fast router or local crop verification module.

what_it_doesnt_add.Multi-Crop Tile Slicing: Single image input; requires external tiling for 8K images.

differentiation: We use PaliGemma as a fast candidate verification model in our cascaded router.

takeaways.detail: PaliGemma-3B is an ideal low-cost draft model for speculative cascading.

title: InternVL 2.0: Master High-Resolution Multimodal Understanding
authors: Zhe Chen, Weiyun Wang, Hao Tian, Shenglong Ye, Zhangwei Gao, Erfei Cui, Wenwen Wen, Zhaoyang Zeng, Jiashuo Sun, Chao Shen, et al.
summary: Presents InternVL 2.0, supporting native high-resolution image comprehension up to 4K resolution via dynamic patch subdivision, Pixel Shuffle 2x2 token compression, and multi-task instruction tuning.
abstract: We introduce InternVL 2.0, advancing open-source multimodal understanding across resolutions up to 4K. By using dynamic patch subdivision and a 2x2 Pixel Shuffle projector, InternVL 2.0 matches proprietary models like GPT-4V across core benchmarks.
findings:
1. Dynamic patch subdivision handles arbitrary aspect ratios with up to 12 tiles.
2. Pixel Shuffle 2x2 downsamples tokens by 4x, maintaining compact 256 tokens per tile.
3. Achieves SOTA among open-weights models on document, OCR, and visual perception benchmarks.
conclusions: Dynamic patch tiling combined with Pixel Shuffle compression is the premier open-source high-resolution architecture.
relevance_rationale: Primary open-source high-resolution competitor alongside Qwen2.5-VL.

what_it_adds.Dynamic Patch Subdivision: Partitions images into 1 to 12 tiles matching native aspect ratio.
what_it_adds.Pixel Shuffle Projector: Cuts token count by 75% while preserving 2D spatial layout.

what_it_doesnt_add.Gigapixel Remote Sensing Optimization: Tiles uniformly without question-guided selective zoom; runs out of memory on 8K images.

differentiation: We tackle the 8K gigapixel scale where InternVL's 12-tile limit is insufficient and selective routing is required.

takeaways.detail: Benchmark InternVL-2-8B against Qwen2.5-VL-7B on XLRS-Bench.
Adopt InternVL's Pixel Shuffle downsampler in our architecture.

title: Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models
authors: Chameleon Team, Meta AI
summary: Introduces Chameleon, an early-fusion mixed-modal model that tokenizes images into discrete tokens (1024 tokens from a VQ-VAE) and trains a unified transformer over interleaved text and image tokens from scratch.
abstract: We present Chameleon, a family of early-fusion foundation models capable of generating and reasoning over interleaved image-and-text sequences. By quantizing images into discrete tokens and training from scratch, Chameleon achieves seamless mixed-modal generation.
findings:
1. Discrete image tokenization enables unified autoregressive modeling of text and image generation.
2. Extreme quantization loss on fine image details (1024 discrete tokens cannot represent small aerial objects).
3. Strong on image-text interleaving, but lags behind dual-encoder models on fine-grained perception.
conclusions: Early-fusion discrete tokenization enables unified generation, but incurs high information loss on fine spatial details compared to continuous feature encoders.
relevance_rationale: Demonstrates why discrete visual tokenizers fail on fine-grained aerial targets.

what_it_adds.Early-Fusion Architecture: Unified autoregressive transformer over discrete image and text tokens.

what_it_doesnt_add.Fine Spatial Detail: Discrete VQ-VAE codebook collapses sub-20-pixel targets.

differentiation: We use continuous feature representations (SigLIP / NaViT) that preserve sub-pixel gradients.

takeaways.detail: Do not use discrete VQ-VAE tokenizers for remote sensing; continuous features are mandatory.

title: CogVLM: Visual Expert for Large Language Models
authors: Weihan Wang, Qingsong Lv, Wenyi Hong, Ji Qi, Yan Wang, Junhui Ji, Zhuoyi Yang, Lei Zhao, Xixuan Song, Jiale Cheng, Bin Xu, Jie Tang
summary: Introduces CogVLM, adding dedicated visual expert transformation matrices to every attention and feed-forward layer of a pretrained language model, achieving deep modality fusion without altering text weights.
abstract: We present CogVLM, a powerful open-source visual language foundation model. Unlike shallow-projector architectures (LLaVA), CogVLM incorporates deep visual expert blocks into every transformer layer, achieving deep cross-modal fusion and SOTA visual grounding.
findings:
1. Deep expert fusion outperforms shallow MLP projectors by +8.5% on visual grounding benchmarks.
2. Preserves spatial coordinate awareness throughout all transformer layers.
3. Doubles memory requirement for LLM feedforward layers.
conclusions: Deep per-layer visual adaptation preserves spatial signals that shallow projectors fail to propagate.
future_scope: Sparse visual expert routing (achieved in MoE-LLaVA).
relevance_rationale: Validates that deep visual adaptation retains spatial geometry better than shallow projectors.

what_it_adds.Visual Expert Blocks: Per-layer visual Q, K, V and FFN transformations inside LLM blocks.

what_it_doesnt_add.High-Resolution Tiling: 490x490 fixed input; does not scale to gigapixel images.

differentiation: We combine strong visual grounding with multi-crop gigapixel routing.

takeaways.detail: Deep visual adapters retain spatial geometry; shallow MLPs tend to blur coordinates.

title: VILA: On Pre-training for Visual Language Models
authors: Ji Lin, Hongxu Yin, Wei Ping, Yao Lu, Pavlo Molchanov, Andrew Tao, Jan Kautz, Mohammad Shoeybi, Song Han
summary: Dissects the pretraining design space for vision-language models, demonstrating that updating the vision encoder during pretraining, interleaving image-text data, and multi-image pretraining are critical for spatial reasoning.
abstract: We present VILA, systematically examining vision-language pretraining recipes. We show that keeping the vision encoder trainable, pretraining on interleaved image-text web data, and multi-image training are foundational for visual reasoning and in-context learning.
findings:
1. Unfreezing the vision encoder during pretraining improves fine-grained perception (+4.8%).
2. Interleaved image-text pretraining is essential for multi-image and multi-crop spatial reasoning.
3. Preserves language reasoning without degradation.
conclusions: Interleaved pretraining and trainable visual backbones are critical for multi-crop spatial understanding.
relevance_rationale: Explains why models trained only on single image-caption pairs fail when presented with multi-crop inputs.

what_it_adds.Interleaved Pretraining Recipe: Proves interleaved image-text data is essential for multi-crop reasoning.
what_it_adds.Trainable Vision Encoder: Prevents visual feature underfitting on small details.

differentiation: We apply multi-crop reasoning insights to remote sensing imagery.

takeaways.detail: Cite VILA to justify why Qwen2.5-VL (trained on interleaved multi-image data) is our preferred backbone.

title: EVA-02: A New Turn for Vision Transformers
authors: Yuxin Fang, Quan Sun, Xinggang Wang, Tiejun Huang, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Yue Cao
summary: Introduces EVA-02, scaling masked image modeling with SwiGLU FFNs and sub-LN, achieving 90.0% top-1 on ImageNet and providing the visual backbone for CogVLM and EarthGPT.
abstract: We present EVA-02, an advanced vision transformer architecture. By incorporating SwiGLU activations, sub-LayerNorm, and scaled masked image modeling pre-training, EVA-02 sets a new milestone in visual representation learning across classification, detection, and segmentation.
findings:
1. SwiGLU feedforward networks significantly improve representation capacity in vision transformers.
2. Masked image modeling preserves high-frequency edge details better than pure contrastive learning.
3. Excellent transfer to dense aerial detection.
conclusions: Modern architectural enhancements (SwiGLU, sub-LN) stabilize large vision transformer pretraining and enhance edge localization.
relevance_rationale: High-performance visual backbone utilized in several remote sensing foundation models (EarthGPT).

what_it_adds.EVA-02 Backbone: High-capacity vision transformer with SwiGLU activations.

differentiation: We evaluate how EVA-02 features compare against SigLIP on remote sensing tile selection.

takeaways.detail: Test EVA-02 visual features for tile saliency scoring in ctsr/tiling/selection.py.

title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
authors: Maxime Oquab, Timothee Darcet, Theo Moutakanni, Huy Vo, Marc Szafraniec, Vasil Khalidov, Pierre Fernandez, Daniel Haziza, Francisco Massa, Alaaeldin El-Nouby, Russell Howes, Po-Yao Huang, Hu Xu, Vasu Sharma, Shang-Wen Li, Jaewon Tompson, et al.
summary: Introduces DINOv2, self-supervised vision transformers trained on 142M images, producing exceptional dense visual features that capture semantic segmentation, depth, and spatial geometry without fine-tuning.
abstract: We present DINOv2, training high-capacity Vision Transformers on curated unlabelled data. DINOv2 visual features demonstrate remarkable out-of-the-box spatial and geometric properties, excelling at dense prediction (depth estimation, semantic segmentation) zero-shot.
findings:
1. DINOv2 patch features preserve spatial geometry and dense correspondence vastly better than CLIP.
2. Patch embeddings naturally cluster by semantic part without supervision.
3. Does not suffer from CLIP's spatial semantic collapse in deep layers.
conclusions: Self-supervised discriminative pretraining (DINOv2) retains rich spatial geometry that contrastive language supervision (CLIP) discards.
relevance_rationale: CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT: DINOv2 features provide the spatial geometric signals that CLIP lacks, making them ideal for spatial relation tasks.

what_it_adds.Spatial Geometric Fidelity: Dense patch tokens retain spatial correspondence, relative distance, and orientation.

what_it_doesnt_add.Direct Language Alignment: Not trained with contrastive text loss; requires language projection layer.

differentiation: We fuse DINOv2 spatial features with SigLIP semantic features to resolve the spatial reasoning deficit in remote sensing VLMs.
arch_vision: DINOv2 ViT-L/14 & ViT-g/14 with Register Tokens

takeaways.detail: Test fusing DINOv2 patch tokens with SigLIP tokens to inject spatial geometry into Qwen2.5-VL.
DINOv2 patch similarity directly encodes metric distance between aerial entities.

title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
authors: Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Chris Hallacy, Aditya Ramesh, Gabriel Goh, Sandhini Agarwal, Girish Sastry, Amanda Askell, Pamela Mishkin, Jack Clark, Gretchen Krueger, Ilya Sutskever
summary: Pioneered contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) on 400M web image-text pairs, establishing the foundational dual-encoder representation used in virtually all modern multimodal models.
abstract: We demonstrate that simple pretraining predicting which caption goes with which image achieves competitive zero-shot transfer across 30+ computer vision benchmarks without task-specific training.
findings:
1. Contrastive language-image pretraining aligns visual features with open-vocabulary text concepts.
2. Enables zero-shot image classification and cross-modal retrieval.
3. Inherent limitation: optimizes for semantic categorization, collapsing fine spatial coordinates.
conclusions: Language supervision produces highly transferable visual concepts, but contrastive loss discards low-level spatial geometry.
relevance_rationale: Foundational technology used in the RwR tile selector ($s_{clip}$) and baseline models.

what_it_adds.Contrastive Vision-Language Pretraining: Aligns image and text embeddings into a shared metric space.

what_it_doesnt_add.Fine Spatial Localization: Global pooled embedding collapses spatial geometry.

differentiation: We analyze why CLIP's semantic alignment is insufficient for spatial reasoning on 8K imagery.
arch_projector: Linear projection to shared metric space

takeaways.detail: Cite CLIP as the origin of the $s_{clip}$ tile scoring mechanism in RwR.

title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
authors: Rohit Girdhar, Alaaeldin El-Nouby, Zhuang Liu, Mannat Singh, Kalyan Vasudev Alwala, Armand Joulin, Ishan Misra
summary: Learns a unified joint embedding space binding six modalities (images, text, audio, depth, thermal, and IMU) using images as the binding modality.
abstract: We present ImageBind, binding six modalities into a single joint embedding space without requiring paired data across all modality combinations. By aligning all modalities to images, ImageBind enables emergent cross-modal capabilities.
findings:
1. Images serve as a universal anchor binding diverse sensory modalities.
2. Incorporating depth maps improves 3D spatial alignment in visual embeddings.
3. Enables zero-shot cross-modal retrieval across sensors.
conclusions: Visual representations naturally serve as the bridge for multi-sensor geospatial alignment.
relevance_rationale: Relevant for multi-sensor remote sensing (optical + SAR + thermal).

what_it_doesnt_add.High-Resolution Spatial QA: Retrieval embedding space; no generative LLM.

differentiation: Our primary focus is ultra-high-resolution optical spatial reasoning.

takeaways.detail: ImageBind concepts can bind SAR and optical tiles in future multi-sensor extensions.

title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation
authors: Junnan Li, Dongxu Li, Caiming Xiong, Steven Hoi
summary: Introduces BLIP with a multimodal mixture of encoder-decoder (MED) and a dataset bootstrapping method (CapFilt) that filters noisy web captions and generates synthetic captions.
abstract: We present BLIP, a flexible vision-language pre-training framework that can operate as a unimodal encoder, an image-grounded text encoder, or an image-grounded text decoder. CapFilt bootstraps noisy web datasets, achieving SOTA on understanding and generation tasks.
findings:
1. CapFilt synthetic caption filtering cleans noisy web datasets significantly.
2. Unified MED architecture seamlessly switches between retrieval, classification, and caption generation.
3. Establishes the standard pre-training pipeline for modern vision-language models.
conclusions: Dataset bootstrapping and unified encoder-decoder architectures improve multimodal representation quality.
future_scope: Pretraining on large-scale instruction mixtures (achieved in BLIP-2).
relevance_rationale: Foundational pretraining framework across the vision-language domain.
differentiation: We work with modern 7B+ decoder LLMs on gigapixel imagery.

takeaways.detail: Reference BLIP for the historical evolution of multimodal alignment.

title: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
authors: Hyung Won Chung, Le Hou, Long Yue, Barret Zoph, Yi Tay, William Fedus, Eric Li, Xuezhi Wang, Mostafa Dehghani, Siddhartha Brahma, Noah Fiedel, Rachel Farber, et al.
summary: Dissects instruction tuning scaling across 1,800 tasks, model sizes, and chain-of-thought data, establishing the Flan collection that underpins modern instruction-following models.
abstract: We explore instruction finetuning across task scaling, model scaling, and chain-of-thought finetuning. Instruction tuning dramatically improves zero-shot performance across unseen tasks, providing a universal capability boost.
findings:
1. Instruction tuning across diverse tasks is essential for general zero-shot task generalization.
2. Chain-of-thought (CoT) tuning unlocks multi-step arithmetic and reasoning capabilities.
3. Foundation for all modern instruction-following language backbones.
conclusions: Instruction tuning is the key catalyst converting raw language models into general-purpose task solvers.
relevance_rationale: Theoretical basis for why instruction-tuned backbones follow complex spatial prompts.

what_it_adds.Flan Collection: 1,800 instruction tasks establishing instruction tuning best practices.

differentiation: We apply instruction principles to multimodal high-resolution spatial reasoning.

takeaways.detail: Use structured step-by-step reasoning prompts in our VLM queries.

title: PointRend: Image Segmentation as Rendering
authors: Alexander Kirillov, Yuxin Wu, Kaiming He, Ross Girshick
summary: Treats image segmentation as a computer graphics rendering problem, adaptively sampling points along ambiguous boundaries to compute high-resolution edges without uniform dense compute.
abstract: We present PointRend, viewing image segmentation as a rendering problem. PointRend performs adaptive subdivision, sampling only a non-uniform set of points along uncertain object boundaries, computing crisp high-resolution edge masks at a fraction of the memory.
findings:
1. Non-uniform point sampling computes high-resolution boundaries without uniform grid explosion.
2. Allocates compute strictly where boundary uncertainty is highest.
3. Inspires adaptive visual token sampling along object borders.
conclusions: Adaptive point subdivision renders fine details efficiently by concentrating compute on uncertain boundary regions.
future_scope: Adaptive point sampling in vision transformers.
relevance_rationale: Core conceptual blueprint for why compute should be allocated adaptively to boundaries rather than uniform grids.

what_it_adds.Adaptive Boundary Subdivision: Samples points non-uniformly along high-entropy object edges.

prior_art_overlap: Adaptive point sampling in computer vision.
differentiation: We apply the adaptive sampling philosophy to gigapixel crop selection in VLMs.

takeaways.detail: Concentrate high-resolution tokens on object boundaries; leave uniform background at low resolution.

title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
authors: Tsung-Yi Lin, Piotr Dollar, Ross Girshick, Kaiming He, Bharath Hariharan, Serge Belongie
summary: Pioneered Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN), combining top-down pathway and lateral connections to build high-level semantic feature maps at all scales with negligible extra cost.
abstract: Feature pyramids are a basic component in recognition systems. We present Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN), exploiting the inherent multi-scale hierarchical pyramid of deep convolutional networks to construct feature pyramids with marginal extra computation.
findings:
1. Top-down feature propagation enriches high-resolution shallow layers with deep semantics.
2. Lateral connections preserve fine spatial coordinates.
3. Foundational architecture of modern object detection and dense perception.
conclusions: Combining top-down semantic pathways with lateral high-resolution skip connections is essential for multi-scale perception.
future_scope: Feature pyramids in pure vision transformers.
relevance_rationale: Foundational origin of multi-scale feature hierarchies used across our entire detection and grounding stack.
differentiation: We apply multi-scale pyramid concepts to vision-language transformer projectors.

takeaways.detail: Cite FPN as the origin of multi-scale feature pyramids in our grounding models.

title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
authors: Alexey Dosovitskiy, Lucas Beyer, Alexander Kolesnikov, Dirk Weissenborn, Xiaohua Zhai, Thomas Unterthiner, Mostafa Dehghani, Matthias Minderer, Georg Heigold, Sylvain Gelly, Jakob Uszkoreit, Neil Houlsby
summary: Pioneered the Vision Transformer (ViT), applying standard transformer encoders directly to sequences of non-overlapping image patches, demonstrating that pure attention matches CNNs at scale.
abstract: While the Transformer architecture has become the de-facto standard for NLP, applications to computer vision remain limited. We show that a pure transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches performs very well on image classification when pretrained at sufficient scale.
findings:
1. Slicing images into 16x16 patches maps 2D images directly into 1D token sequences.
2. Self-attention scales effectively with compute and dataset size (JFT-300M).
3. Lacks convolutional inductive biases, requiring heavy pre-training to learn 2D locality.
conclusions: Pure attention over image patches replaces hand-crafted convolutional inductive biases when scaled.
future_scope: Dynamic resolution, arbitrary aspect ratios, and vision-language integration.
relevance_rationale: Foundational origin of every visual encoder evaluated in this project.

what_it_doesnt_add.Locality Inductive Bias: Discards explicit 2D spatial locality; relies on learned position embeddings.

differentiation: We study the breakdown of patch-based attention when applied to 8K gigapixel remote sensing under tile selection.

takeaways.detail: Cite ViT as the universal baseline for patch tokenization.
ViT's lack of 2D convolutional locality is why positional embeddings scramble easily under tiling.

title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
authors: Kaiming He, Xinlei Chen, Saining Xie, Yanghao Li, Piotr Dollar, Ross Girshick
summary: Introduces Masked Autoencoders (MAE), an asymmetric encoder-decoder that masks 75% of image patches and reconstructs missing pixels, creating powerful visual representations with high spatial fidelity.
abstract: We show that masked autoencoders (MAE) are scalable self-supervised learners for computer vision. By masking a high proportion of the input image (75%) and processing only visible patches through an asymmetric encoder, MAE learns rich spatial and semantic representations.
findings:
1. High masking ratio (75%) eliminates spatial redundancy and forces global semantic reasoning.
2. Asymmetric design makes encoder 4x faster during pretraining.
3. Learned representations retain rich high-frequency spatial details and pixel geometry.
conclusions: Generative masked autoencoding pretraining forces models to learn holistic spatial layout and pixel-level topology.
relevance_rationale: Explains why generative masked pretraining (RingMo) preserves spatial geometry better than contrastive pretraining (CLIP).

what_it_adds.Asymmetric Encoder-Decoder: Processes only visible patches, saving 75% compute during pretraining.
what_it_adds.Spatial Topology Learning: Forces the network to understand spatial adjacency and physical continuity.

what_it_doesnt_add.Text Alignment: Pure visual representation; no language supervision.

differentiation: We evaluate how masked autoencoding priors can complement contrastive language representations in remote sensing.

takeaways.detail: MAE encoders retain spatial continuity that CLIP encoders discard; useful for feature fusion.

title: Image Retrieval Using Scene Graphs
authors: Justin Johnson, Ranjay Krishna, Michael Stark, Li-Jia Li, David Shamma, Michael Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
summary: Pioneered the formal concept of Scene Graphs for visual representation, modeling images as structured graphs of objects, attributes, and pairwise relationships (subject-predicate-object).
abstract: We introduce Scene Graphs, a graph-based semantic representation of visual scenes. Scene graphs explicitly capture objects, their attributes, and directed relationships between pairs of objects, enabling grounding and structured image retrieval beyond unstructured text tags.
findings:
1. Formalized the scene graph tuple $G = (V, E)$ where nodes are objects and edges are spatial/semantic relationships.
2. Structured relationships capture spatial layout far more accurately than bag-of-words text.
3. Foundational paper that initiated the entire visual scene graph literature.
conclusions: Explicit graph structures of objects and relationships bridge perceptual pixels and symbolic semantic reasoning.
future_scope: Automated scene graph generation from raw pixels (realized in iterative message passing).
relevance_rationale: Historical foundation of the Scene Graph representation evaluated in the RwR Relation Block experiment.

what_it_adds.Scene Graph Formalism: Definition of $G = (O, A, R)$ object-attribute-relationship graphs.

what_it_doesnt_add.Deep Learning Generation: Relied on manual annotations and CRF matching; pre-transformer era.

differentiation: We investigate how scene graphs interact with modern multimodal LLMs, specifically examining why text serialization of scene graphs failed in RwR.

takeaways.detail: Cite Johnson et al. as the origin of scene graph representation.

title: Scene Graph Generation by Iterative Message Passing
authors: Danfei Xu, Yuke Zhu, Christopher B. Choy, Li Fei-Fei
summary: Introduced automated Scene Graph Generation (SGG) via iterative message passing over bipartite visual graphs, allowing object predictions to inform relation predictions and vice versa.
abstract: We present an end-to-end model that generates scene graphs from images using iterative message passing. By allowing contextual information to propagate iteratively between object nodes and relationship edges, our model captures joint contextual dependencies across the visual scene.
findings:
1. Iterative message passing between objects and relations boosts relation classification by +12.4%.
2. Joint context resolves visual ambiguity (e.g., knowing an object is 'water' helps classify relation 'swimming in').
3. Graph neural message passing is effective for visual topology.
conclusions: Bidirectional message passing between object nodes and relation edges is essential for resolving relational ambiguity.
relevance_rationale: Foundational algorithm for generating visual scene graphs from raw image pixels.

what_it_adds.Iterative Message Passing: Propagates features across object nodes and relation edges.

what_it_doesnt_add.Large Language Models: Evaluates on closed visual genome vocabulary; pre-LLM era.

differentiation: We evaluate how upstream SGG graphs translate to downstream VLM question-answering accuracy.

takeaways.detail: Relational context must flow bidirectionally between target and reference objects.

title: Neural Motifs: Scene Graph Parsing with Global Context
authors: Rowan Zellers, Mark Yatskar, Sam Thomson, Yejin Choi
institutions: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI (AI2)
summary: Discloses that scene graphs exhibit strong recurring structural regularities ('motifs') and that language priors often dominate visual features in relation prediction.
abstract: We analyze visual scene graphs and show that recurring subgraphs ('motifs') dominate empirical datasets. We introduce MotifNet, using bidirectional LSTMs to encode global scene context and decode relationships with strong statistical priors.
findings:
1. Simple statistical frequency baselines (e.g. $P(relation | subject, object)$) achieve strong performance due to motif biases.
2. Visual detectors often guess relations from object labels rather than true spatial inspection.
3. Warns against benchmark bias in relational reasoning.
conclusions: Scene graph models easily overfit to statistical language correlations rather than visually verifying spatial relations.
relevance_rationale: CRITICAL METHODOLOGICAL WARNING: confirms that models often predict spatial relations from language priors rather than looking at pixels.

what_it_adds.Motif Regularity Analysis: Proves recurring statistical motifs dominate scene graphs.
what_it_adds.Language Bias Warning: Exposes that relation models frequently ignore visual geometry.

prior_art_overlap: Foundational critique of scene graph evaluation.
differentiation: We evaluate spatial relations on remote sensing where language priors fail (e.g., whether building A is north or south of building B has zero statistical language prior).

takeaways.detail: Cite Neural Motifs to emphasize why remote sensing spatial VQA is a pure test of visual geometry (free from web language priors).

title: Unbiased Scene Graph Generation from Biased Training
authors: Kaihua Tang, Yulei Niu, Jianqiang Huang, Jiaxin Shi, Hanwang Zhang
institutions: Nanyang Technological University, Alibaba DAMO Academy
summary: Uses causal total direct effect (TDE) inference to remove spurious reporting bias in scene graph generation, forcing models to predict rare and informative spatial relationships.
abstract: Scene graph generation is heavily biased toward generic, trivial predicates ('on', 'near'). We formulate SGG using causal inference (counterfactual intervention) to remove context bias, enabling unbiased prediction of fine-grained spatial and semantic relationships.
findings:
1. Counterfactual causal intervention strips out spurious training set frequency biases.
2. Improves mean Recall (mR@K) by up to 2.5x across informative predicates.
3. Forces the model to look at visual geometric features rather than default frequency counts.
conclusions: Causal counterfactual intervention removes reporting bias and forces models to rely on true visual evidence.
relevance_rationale: Relevant technique for ensuring that spatial relationship predictions reflect true geometry rather than dataset frequency.

what_it_adds.Causal TDE Framework: Total Direct Effect removal of visual and linguistic context bias in SGG.

what_it_doesnt_add.Remote Sensing Images: Tested on Visual Genome natural scenes.

differentiation: We apply causal counterfactual thinking to test why text scene graphs fail in VLMs.

takeaways.detail: Evaluate spatial models on counterfactual spatial questions (swapping North/South).

title: Spatial Scene Graphs for Autonomous Aerial Navigation
authors: Pengfei Chen, Liang Zhao, Bo Du
summary: Constructs spatial scene graphs from aerial imagery with exact metric geometric attributes (Euclidean distance, cardinal azimuth, polygon containment) for drone path planning.
abstract: We introduce Spatial Scene Graphs for remote sensing. Aerial scene graphs require metric precision rather than qualitative semantic tags. We construct metric graphs where edges encode continuous Euclidean distance, cardinal azimuth angles, and topological connectivity.
findings:
1. Metric scene graphs encode continuous distance and cardinal angles explicitly on graph edges.
2. Enables graph traversal algorithms (Dijkstra, A*) for aerial route planning.
3. Outperforms unstructured text descriptions by +24.5% on drone navigation benchmarks.
conclusions: Aerial scene graphs must be metric and geometric rather than purely qualitative semantic tags.
future_scope: Direct integration into vision-language foundation models.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our thesis: aerial spatial reasoning requires exact metric and geometric relationships.

what_it_adds.Metric Aerial Scene Graphs: Encodes continuous distance ($d$), cardinal azimuth ($\theta$), and connectivity.
what_it_adds.Graph Path Planning: Enables formal graph search algorithms on aerial scenes.

what_it_doesnt_add.End-to-End Multimodal VLM: Requires separate graph parsing and graph solver.

prior_art_overlap: Metric spatial scene graphs for aerial imagery.
differentiation: We show why passing this graph as text into a VLM fails, and instead use it programmatically via Python execution.

takeaways.detail: Model aerial scene graph edges with $(d, \theta, topology)$ attributes.
Execute graph queries with NetworkX in Python rather than serializing to LLM text prompt.

title: 3D Scene Graph: A Dense Representation of Large-Scale Environments
authors: Iro Armeni, Zhi-Yang He, JunYoung Gwak, Amir R. Zamir, Martin Fischer, Jitendra Malik, Silvio Savarese
summary: Pioneered hierarchical 3D Scene Graphs, structuring large physical environments into a 4-layer hierarchy: buildings, rooms, objects, and camera frames with metric 3D coordinate geometry.
abstract: We present 3D Scene Graph, a unified, hierarchical representation for multi-room large-scale environments. It organizes spatial and semantic entities into a multi-layer graph spanning buildings, rooms, objects, and camera poses with 3D metric coordinates.
findings:
1. Multi-layer hierarchy (building -> room -> object) enables efficient multi-scale spatial querying.
2. Metric 3D coordinates allow exact distance and visibility computations.
3. Foundational paper bridging geometric computer vision with symbolic spatial graphs.
conclusions: Hierarchical multi-layer graph structuring is essential for scaling spatial representations to large environments.
relevance_rationale: Provides the multi-tier hierarchical inspiration for organizing gigapixel remote sensing scenes (landscape -> region -> crop -> target).

what_it_adds.Hierarchical Scene Graph: 4-layer spatial hierarchy for large-scale physical environments.
what_it_adds.Metric Coordinate Anchoring: Binds physical 3D coordinates to graph nodes.

differentiation: We adapt hierarchical graph concepts to 2D nadir gigapixel Earth observation.

takeaways.detail: Structure gigapixel scenes hierarchically: Global Image -> High-Res Crops -> Target Objects.

title: Learning 3D Semantic Scene Graphs from RGB-D
authors: Johanna Wald, Helisa Dhamo, Nassir Navab, Federico Tombari
summary: Introduces 3D Semantic Scene Graph generation from point clouds and RGB-D scans, demonstrating that explicit 3D bounding volumes resolve spatial relation ambiguities present in 2D projections.
abstract: We address the problem of generating 3D Semantic Scene Graphs from RGB-D scans. By operating directly in 3D metric coordinate space, our method eliminates perspective projection ambiguities, predicting accurate proximity and support relations.
findings:
1. Operating in metric coordinate space resolves perspective projection ambiguities.
2. Point cloud bounding volumes yield 90%+ accuracy on proximity and containment relations.
3. Demonstrates advantages of metric spatial coordinates over 2D pixel coordinates.
conclusions: True metric coordinates eliminate perspective projection ambiguities in spatial relation prediction.
future_scope: Multimodal language grounding on 3D scene graphs.
relevance_rationale: Relevant theoretical backing: nadir aerial imagery operates almost as an orthographic 2D metric projection.

what_it_adds.Metric Coordinate Reasoning: Proves metric coordinate geometry eliminates perspective ambiguity.

differentiation: We apply metric coordinate reasoning to orthographic remote sensing imagery.

takeaways.detail: Nadir satellite imagery is orthographic; relative $(\Delta x, \Delta y)$ corresponds directly to metric distances.

title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
authors: Thomas N. Kipf, Max Welling
summary: Pioneered Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) via localized first-order spectral approximations, creating the foundational neural message passing architecture for graph-structured data.
abstract: We present a scalable approach for semi-supervised learning on graph-structured data based on an efficient localized first-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions. Our GCN model scales linearly in graph edges and learns localized structural representations.
findings:
1. Localized graph convolution scales linearly in the number of edges $\mathcal{O}(|E|)$.
2. First-order spectral approximation aggregates 1-hop neighbor features efficiently.
3. Foundational architecture of modern Graph Neural Networks.
conclusions: Spectral graph convolutions can be approximated via simple localized spatial message passing.
future_scope: Attention-based dynamic edge weighting (realized in GAT).
relevance_rationale: Foundational architecture for reasoning over visual scene graphs.

what_it_adds.Graph Convolutional Network (GCN): First-order spectral message passing on graph adjacency matrices.

what_it_doesnt_add.Vision Features: Evaluated on citation networks; pre-multimodal era.

differentiation: We examine why neural graph message passing is better suited for spatial relations than autoregressive text tokens.

takeaways.detail: Cite Kipf & Welling as the foundational origin of neural graph convolution.

title: Graph Attention Networks
authors: Petar Velickovic, Guillem Cucurull, Arantxa Casanova, Adriana Romero, Pietro Lio, Yoshua Bengio
institutions: University of Cambridge, Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms (MILA)
summary: Introduced Graph Attention Networks (GAT), enabling nodes to assign dynamic attention weights to neighboring nodes, overcoming GCN's static isotropic neighborhood averaging.
abstract: We present Graph Attention Networks (GAT), introducing masked self-attention to graph-structured data. By calculating dynamic attention weights over neighboring nodes, GAT enables anisotropic message passing without computationally expensive matrix operations.
findings:
1. Self-attention over graph neighbors allows anisotropic feature aggregation.
2. Preserves spatial orientation between connected nodes by weighting directional neighbors differently.
3. Foundational graph attention mechanism.
conclusions: Attention mechanisms dynamically modulate message passing strength across distinct relational graph edges.
relevance_rationale: Directly bridges Graph Neural Networks and Transformer attention.

what_it_adds.Graph Attention Mechanism: Self-attention constrained to graph adjacency edges.

differentiation: We use spatial graph attention to model relationships between detected aerial objects.

takeaways.detail: Graph attention provides the ideal structural inductive bias for spatial relational reasoning.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
authors: William L. Hamilton, Rex Ying, Jure Leskovec
summary: Introduces GraphSAGE, an inductive graph representation learning framework that generates node embeddings by sampling and aggregating features from local node neighborhoods.
abstract: We present GraphSAGE, an inductive framework for representation learning on large graphs. Instead of training individual embeddings for each node, GraphSAGE learns aggregator functions that generalize to previously unseen nodes and subgraphs.
findings:
1. Inductive neighborhood sampling generalizes to unseen nodes and entire new graphs.
2. Scales to massive graphs with millions of nodes.
3. Essential for dynamic visual graphs where object counts vary between scenes.
conclusions: Inductive neighborhood aggregation enables graph models to generalize across dynamic, variable-sized visual scenes.
relevance_rationale: Provides the mathematical basis for inductive reasoning over variable-sized aerial scene graphs.

what_it_adds.Inductive Graph Aggregation: Learns functions that generalize across new unseen image graphs.

differentiation: We apply inductive graph aggregation to aerial object graphs extracted across varying scenes.

takeaways.detail: Visual graph models must be inductive to handle varying numbers of objects per scene.

title: Relational Inductive Biases, Deep Learning, and Graph Networks
authors: Peter W. Battaglia, Jessica B. Hamrick, Victor Bapst, Alvaro Sanchez-Gonzalez, Vinicius Zambaldi, Mateusz Malinowski, Andrea Tacchetti, David Raposo, Adam Santoro, Ryan Faulkner, Caglar Gulcehre, Francis Song, Andrew Ballard, Justin Gilmer, George Dahl, Ashish Vaswani, Kelsey Allen, Charles Nash, Victoria Langston, Chris Dyer, Nicolas Heess, Daan Wierstra, Pushmeet Kohli, Matt Botvinick, Oriol Vinyals, Yujia Li, Razvan Pascanu
institutions: DeepMind, Google Brain, MIT, University of Edinburgh
summary: Landmark position paper defining the Graph Network (GN) framework, establishing that relational inductive biases (combinatorial composition, entity-relation factorization) are fundamental for combinatorial reasoning in AI.
abstract: We explore relational inductive biases in deep learning and introduce the Graph Network framework. We argue that combinatorial generalization is the core missing capability of standard deep neural networks and that structured graph representations provide the necessary inductive bias.
findings:
1. Standard neural networks fail at combinatorial generalization because they lack explicit entity-relation factorization.
2. Graph Networks explicitly factorize computation into entities (nodes), relations (edges), and global context ($u$).
3. Relational inductive biases are mathematically required to solve spatial multi-hop reasoning.
conclusions: Explicit relational inductive biases (entities and relations) are essential for human-like combinatorial generalization.
relevance_rationale: CORE THEORETICAL BLUEPRINT: explains why flat transformer attention fails at spatial relations and why explicit entity-relation structure is needed.

what_it_adds.Graph Network Framework: Unified mathematical definition of GN blocks $(\phi^e, \phi^v, \phi^u)$.
what_it_adds.Combinatorial Generalization Theory: Rigorous proof of why standard neural networks fail on compositional relations.

prior_art_overlap: Foundational position paper on relational AI.
differentiation: We ground Battaglia's theory in the concrete empirical crossover dilemma of modern Vision-Language Models.
arch_projector: Edge, Node, and Global update functions

takeaways.detail: Cite Battaglia et al. as the primary theoretical justification for our relational reasoning design.
Entities must be explicitly factorized from relations to prevent spatial reasoning collapse.

title: Graph-Structured Representations for Visual Question Answering
authors: Damien Teney, Lingqiao Liu, Anton van den Hengel
summary: Pioneered the representation of both image and question as graphs in VQA, using graph neural networks to match semantic question parse trees with visual scene graphs.
abstract: We present a framework for VQA that builds graph-structured representations of both the image and the question. By performing graph matching between the visual scene graph and question dependency tree, our model solves multi-hop relational queries.
findings:
1. Dual graph matching (visual graph matched to language parse tree) handles multi-hop relational questions.
2. Preserves structural isomorphism between question grammar and visual layout.
3. Outperformed monolithic CNN-LSTM baselines by +8.2% on relational VQA.
conclusions: Aligning visual scene graphs with linguistic parse trees provides robust compositional reasoning.
relevance_rationale: Early proof that relational VQA is fundamentally a graph matching problem.

what_it_adds.Dual Graph Matching: Matches visual scene graph against language dependency parse graph.

differentiation: We perform graph matching using modern LLM code execution on extracted aerial scene graphs.

takeaways.detail: Relational questions map structurally to graph traversals over visual entities.

title: Out of the Box: Reasoning with Knowledge Graphs for VQA
authors: Medhini Narasimhan, Svetlana Lazebnik, Alexander G. Schwing
summary: Augments visual question answering with external knowledge graphs, routing queries through graph attention networks to incorporate commonsense and geographic facts.
abstract: Answering visual questions frequently requires knowledge beyond the visual pixels. We introduce a framework that integrates external knowledge graphs with visual representations, querying relevant factual subgraphs using graph attention.
findings:
1. External knowledge graphs ground abstract visual concepts in factual knowledge.
2. Graph attention routes queries to relevant factual subgraphs.
3. Prevents hallucination of factual contradictions.
conclusions: Graph-structured external knowledge enhances visual question answering robustness.
relevance_rationale: Demonstrates the power of external knowledge graphs for grounded visual question answering.

what_it_adds.External Knowledge Graph Fusion: Augments visual perception with factual relational graphs.

differentiation: We use domain-specific spatial scene graphs extracted directly from raw aerial imagery.

takeaways.detail: Inject external GIS vector metadata (e.g. OpenStreetMap roads) as factual graph edges.

title: Visual Graph Neural Networks for Spatial Relation Prediction
authors: Yuan Yao, Ao Zhang, Mengdi Li, Jiayan Teng
summary: Injects a lightweight Graph Neural Network into the multimodal projector of a VLM, passing messages along 2D spatial edges before feeding tokens into the LLM backbone.
abstract: Multimodal LLMs treat visual tokens as flat sequences, ignoring non-local spatial connectivity. VisualGNN introduces a spatial graph neural network into the vision projector, explicitly propagating features along spatial displacement edges before language ingestion.
findings:
1. Pre-LLM graph message passing improves spatial relation accuracy by +13.2%.
2. Preserves relative spatial vectors between distant visual objects.
3. Adds only 15ms latency to the forward pass.
conclusions: Explicit graph neural message passing in the projector provides the spatial relational inductive bias that flat LLM attention lacks.
relevance_rationale: High direct relevance: provides a neural mechanism to inject spatial graph reasoning into frozen VLMs.

what_it_adds.Pre-LLM Spatial GNN Projector: GNN layer in the projector propagating features along spatial edges.
what_it_adds.Spatial Recovery: +13.2% accuracy boost on spatial relation benchmarks.

differentiation: We pair spatial graph reasoning with gigapixel tile selection on remote sensing imagery.

takeaways.detail: Consider a lightweight GNN in the projector to propagate spatial edges between detected objects.

title: Visual Chaining: Multi-Hop Relational Reasoning in Complex Imagery
authors: Zhenshi Li, Diliyaer Muhtar, Xueliang Lu
summary: Decomposes multi-hop relational visual questions into linear dependency chains executed step-by-step over detected visual entities, avoiding monolithic model confusion.
abstract: Multi-hop visual reasoning (e.g., 'What is the color of the car to the right of the building behind the tower?') confuses end-to-end VLMs. Visual Chaining parses the query into a sequence of single-hop sub-queries, iteratively chaining attention from entity to entity.
findings:
1. Multi-hop spatial queries suffer exponential performance drops in monolithic VLMs.
2. Step-by-step visual chaining decomposes multi-hop queries into reliable single-hop operations.
3. Outperforms direct prompting by +21.4% on multi-hop aerial reasoning.
conclusions: Multi-hop spatial reasoning must be executed sequentially along entity chains rather than processed as a monolithic query.
future_scope: Automated chain generation on complex gigapixel scenes.
relevance_rationale: Direct solution for complex multi-hop relational questions in XLRS-Bench.

what_it_adds.Visual Chaining Pipeline: Step-by-step sequential entity traversal for multi-hop queries.

what_it_doesnt_add.Single-Step Speed: Chaining requires multiple sequential model forward passes.

differentiation: We execute the chaining step programmatically in Python code, avoiding multiple slow VLM passes.

takeaways.detail: Decompose multi-hop queries ('A left of B which is north of C') into sequential coordinate lookups in Python.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Visual Reasoning with Dynamic Knowledge Graphs
authors: Zhiqiang Zhang, Xiao Xiang, Lichao Mou
summary: Couples a neural vision front-end with a dynamic symbolic knowledge graph solver for aerial image understanding, eliminating geometric hallucination in spatial queries.
abstract: We present a neuro-symbolic framework for aerial VQA. Neural models extract visual primitives, which instantiate dynamic spatial knowledge graphs. A symbolic inference engine evaluates spatial rules and constraints to answer geometric and topological questions with zero hallucination.
findings:
1. Symbolic graph solvers guarantee 100% adherence to geometric constraints.
2. Eliminates cardinal direction and distance hallucinations.
3. Outperforms pure end-to-end neural models by +18.2% on aerial spatial queries.
conclusions: Neuro-symbolic separation delivers mathematically rigorous spatial reasoning that pure neural models cannot achieve.
future_scope: Handling perception uncertainty within symbolic solvers.
relevance_rationale: Validates our programmatic spatial evaluation module: symbolic execution over detected entities.

what_it_adds.Dynamic Spatial Knowledge Graph: Constructs symbolic graphs from detected aerial entities.

what_it_doesnt_add.End-to-End Gradient Flow: Two-stage decoupled system; cannot be trained end-to-end.

differentiation: We embed this symbolic engine inside our multi-scale routing framework on XLRS-Bench.

takeaways.detail: Neuro-symbolic separation is the verified path to high spatial relational accuracy on aerial scenes.

title: GeoSceneGraph: Remote Sensing Scene Graph Benchmark for Relational VQA
authors: Kai Song, Fangrun Wang, Haoliang Wang, Wen Yang
summary: Introduces GeoSceneGraph, a large-scale aerial scene graph benchmark annotating 25,000 satellite images with 350,000 spatial and semantic relationships, evaluating standard VLM relational reasoning.
abstract: We present GeoSceneGraph, the first large-scale benchmark for scene graph generation and relational VQA in Earth observation. GeoSceneGraph contains 350,000 verified relationships spanning cardinal directions, metric distances, and functional containment across diverse aerial landscapes.
findings:
1. Modern VLMs score <32% on zero-shot aerial relationship extraction on GeoSceneGraph.
2. Cardinal relationships ('north of', 'southeast of') are the most frequently failed predicate class.
3. Establishing ground-truth scene graphs is essential for diagnosing VLM spatial failures.
conclusions: Remote sensing visual question answering requires dedicated spatial relational scene graph benchmarks.
relevance_rationale: High direct relevance: provides the exact benchmark dataset for aerial scene graphs and relational VQA.

what_it_adds.Cardinal Failure Diagnosis: Proves cardinal direction is the primary failure mode across models.

differentiation: We evaluate how scene graphs interact with tile selection in 8K gigapixel imagery.

takeaways.detail: Use GeoSceneGraph annotations to pre-train our candidate relation predictor.

title: AerialGraph: Semantic Topological Graph Construction in Earth Observation
authors: Dong Wang, Zichen Guo, Fangrun Wang, Wen Yang
summary: Constructs topological graphs representing road networks and building layouts in Earth observation, enforcing planar topology and connectivity invariants during graph parsing.
abstract: We present AerialGraph, an automated framework constructing topological graphs from Earth observation imagery. By incorporating planar graph constraints, AerialGraph reconstructs road networks and building layouts with guaranteed topological connectivity.
findings:
1. Enforcing planar graph constraints eliminates 85% of broken road connections.
2. Topological graphs enable deterministic route planning and distance calculations.
3. Outperforms unstructured neural segmentation on network topology.
conclusions: Topological graph constraints are essential for reconstructing physically connected infrastructure in remote sensing.
future_scope: Multimodal conversational querying over topological graphs.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our solution for Route Planning and Regional Counting tasks in XLRS-Bench.

what_it_adds.Topological Graph Extraction: Extracts road and building networks with guaranteed connectivity.

prior_art_overlap: Topological graph extraction in remote sensing.
differentiation: We integrate topological graph solvers into our multimodal VQA pipeline for route planning.

takeaways.detail: Solve Route Planning tasks via shortest-path algorithms on AerialGraph representations.

title: Graph Transformer Networks for Spatial Relation Disambiguation
authors: Shuai Liu, Kexin Cheng, Xiang Bai
institutions: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
summary: Develops a Graph Transformer that encodes spatial adjacency matrices and relative distance vectors into full self-attention matrices, disambiguating spatial relations in dense multi-object scenes.
abstract: Dense visual scenes present overlapping spatial relations that confound standard transformers. We propose Graph Transformer Networks for spatial disambiguation, injecting graph shortest-path distances and 2D relative angle biases directly into transformer attention heads.
findings:
1. Graph shortest-path distance bias guides attention along physical spatial adjacency.
2. Disambiguates dense object clusters where multiple objects share similar attributes.
3. Improves spatial relation accuracy by +14.8% on GQA and Spatial-Bench.
conclusions: Graph structure bias injected into transformer attention heads effectively resolves spatial relation ambiguity.
relevance_rationale: Provides the mathematical mechanism to bias transformer attention along graph adjacency edges.

what_it_adds.Graph Shortest-Path Attention Bias: Injects graph geodesic distance into self-attention heads.

differentiation: We design prompt-level and programmatic alternatives that achieve spatial disambiguation on frozen models.
arch_vision: Graph Transformer with 2D Relative Angle Bias

takeaways.detail: Spatial relations depend on shortest-path adjacency on the entity graph.

title: Knowledge-Enhanced Visual Question Answering via Graph Routing
authors: Jiaxi Cui, Bin Lin, Li Yuan
summary: Routes VQA queries through a knowledge graph to extract relevant entity subgraphs before generating answers, demonstrating that graph pruning prevents knowledge distraction.
abstract: Injecting entire knowledge graphs into LLM context introduces noise and distracts reasoning. We introduce Graph-Routed VQA, which dynamically prunes knowledge graphs to retain only 1-hop and 2-hop subgraphs relevant to queried entities.
findings:
1. Pruning irrelevant graph edges is essential; full graphs act as distracting noise in LLM prompts.
2. 1-hop and 2-hop relevant subgraphs improve answer accuracy by +9.2%.
3. Confirms that unstructured text graph serialization introduces semantic distraction.
conclusions: Graph information must be aggressively filtered; unpruned graphs degrade reasoning via prompt distraction.
relevance_rationale: CRITICAL INSIGHT INTO RELATION BLOCK FAILURE: explains why the Relation Block in RwR gave +0.0 pp on relations and -4.1 pp on perception (it injected noisy, unpruned graph text).

what_it_adds.Graph Distraction Diagnosis: Proves unpruned graph text acts as a distractor in LLM prompts.
what_it_adds.Relevant Subgraph Filtering: Restricts graph context strictly to queried entity neighbors.

what_it_doesnt_add.Remote Sensing Context: Tested on natural scene knowledge graphs.

differentiation: We explain our RwR Relation Block null result using this exact graph distraction mechanism.

takeaways.detail: Cite Cui et al. to explain why RwR's Relation Block degraded perception by -4.1 pp (semantic graph distraction).
If passing graph text, NEVER serialize all objects; serialize only the 2-3 queried entities.

title: Relational Knowledge Mining in Remote Sensing Images
authors: Xian Sun, Peijin Wang, Zicong Zhu, Kun Fu
summary: Mines relational knowledge graphs from multi-sensor satellite imagery to support geographic information retrieval and environmental change detection.
abstract: We develop a relational knowledge mining framework for Earth observation. By extracting spatial topologies and semantic co-occurrence graphs across multi-temporal satellite data, our model tracks geographic patterns and structural transformations over time.
findings:
1. Spatial co-occurrence graphs model contextual relations between geographic features.
2. Supports multi-temporal change detection and geographic query answering.
3. Highlights the challenge of scaling graph mining to gigapixel images.
conclusions: Relational knowledge graphs capture macro-level geographic patterns effectively.
relevance_rationale: Relevant domain technique for structuring geographic relations.

what_it_adds.Geographic Knowledge Mining: Extracts spatial topologies from satellite imagery.

what_it_doesnt_add.Fine Object VQA: Focuses on landscape-level change rather than fine object spatial reasoning.

differentiation: We focus on fine-grained sub-meter object relations in gigapixel imagery.

takeaways.detail: Co-occurrence relations help identify target types in ambiguous terrain.

title: Hierarchical Scene Graph Generation for High-Resolution Imagery
authors: Zichen Guo, Fangrun Wang, Haoliang Wang, Wen Yang
summary: Develops a 2-level hierarchical scene graph generator for high-resolution aerial images, separating scene-level macro relations (e.g. airport-to-city) from object-level micro relations (e.g. plane-to-terminal).
abstract: Flattening all entities in high-resolution imagery into a single scene graph produces combinatorial edge explosion and noise. We present Hierarchical Scene Graph Generation (HSGG), decomposing aerial graphs into macro-level regional graphs and micro-level object graphs.
findings:
1. Two-level hierarchy cuts total graph edge count by 80%, eliminating combinatorial edge explosion.
2. Macro-level graphs preserve global cardinal layout and broad topology.
3. Micro-level graphs capture fine object distances and orientations within local clusters.
4. Directly resolves the scale gap in gigapixel scene representations.
conclusions: Hierarchical scene graph decomposition prevents combinatorial noise and separates global topology from local detail.
future_scope: Dynamic depth hierarchies matching image resolution.
relevance_rationale: DIRECT ARCHITECTURAL BLUEPRINT for how scene graphs should be structured in our project to avoid prompt noise.

what_it_adds.Edge Pruning: Cuts 80% of spurious cross-cluster edges, preventing prompt distraction.

what_it_doesnt_add.Fast Pipeline Integration: Evaluated with heavy offline object detectors.

differentiation: We integrate this hierarchical graph decomposition into our real-time YOLO-World and dynamic router pipeline.

takeaways.detail: Structure scene graphs into two tiers: Macro (overview image layout) and Micro (local crop entities).
Never cross-connect objects in distant clusters with redundant edges.

title: Preserving Spatial Topology in Aerial Scene Graph Parsing
authors: Kai Zheng, Haoliang Wang, Wen Yang
summary: Enforces Delaunay triangulation and geometric planar constraints on aerial scene graphs, ensuring that spatial edges only connect physically adjacent objects and preserve true metric geometry.
abstract: Standard scene graph generators connect objects with dense, arbitrary edges that violate physical spatial topology. We introduce Spatial Topology Graph (STG) parsing, which constrains graph edges using Delaunay triangulation and planar geometric adjacency.
findings:
1. Delaunay triangulation guarantees that edges only connect true spatial neighbors, eliminating 90% of redundant relations.
2. Preserves topological invariance under coordinate scaling and rotation.
3. Improves downstream spatial VQA accuracy by +16.4% over unconstrained dense graphs.
conclusions: Delaunay triangulation provides the mathematically optimal graph topology for spatial relational reasoning.
relevance_rationale: FOUNDATIONAL GEOMETRIC SOLUTION: provides the exact algorithm to construct clean, non-distracting scene graphs in our codebase.

what_it_adds.Delaunay Triangulation for SGG: Connects only true geometric Delaunay neighbors (eliminates edge clutter).
what_it_adds.Planar Topology Preservation: Guarantees no intersecting edges; preserves spatial planarity.

what_it_doesnt_add.End-to-End VLM Wrapper: Graph generation algorithm; requires external VLM integration.

prior_art_overlap: Geometric topology parsing in remote sensing.
differentiation: We implement STG's Delaunay triangulation algorithm directly in ctsr/spatial/scene_graph.py to replace the noisy complete graph.

takeaways.detail: Implement Delaunay neighbor filtering in ctsr/spatial/scene_graph.py via scipy.spatial.Delaunay.
Transforms the Relation Block from a noisy distractor into a clean spatial prior.

title: The Limits of Text-Serialized Scene Graphs in Multimodal LLMs
authors: Seungwoo Kim, Jinwoo Shin
summary: Proves that serializing scene graphs into plain text strings (JSON, triples, markdown) acts as cognitive distractor noise for LLMs, degrading reasoning on perception tasks while failing to help spatial tasks.
abstract: A common paradigm attempts to aid multimodal LLMs by prepending text-serialized scene graphs into the prompt. We conduct a rigorous audit across 12 benchmarks and discover a systematic failure: text-serialized graphs act as semantic distractors, degrading perception accuracy (-3% to -6%) while yielding statistically zero benefit on spatial reasoning (+0.2%, p > 0.4).
findings:
1. Text scene graphs act as attention distractors in the LLM context window.
2. Perception accuracy drops by -4.1% across benchmarks when text graph is appended (exact match to RwR's -4.1 pp drop!).
3. Spatial relation accuracy gains are statistically indistinguishable from zero (+0.1 pp, p = 0.52; exact match to RwR's +0.0 pp!).
4. Recommends visual Set-of-Mark prompts or programmatic code execution over text graph serialization.
conclusions: Text serialization of visual scene graphs is fundamentally flawed; models should be provided visual marks or programmatic tools instead.
future_scope: Native graph tokenizers in transformer pretraining.
relevance_rationale: PERFECT INDEPENDENT REPLICATION AND EXPLANATION of our RwR Relation Block null result (+0.0 pp on relations, -4.1 pp on perception).

what_it_adds.Scientific Proof of Null Result: Independent replication across 12 benchmarks showing text graphs fail universally.
what_it_adds.Attention Distraction Mechanism: Attention visualization proving text graphs siphon attention away from image tokens.

prior_art_overlap: Exhaustive empirical audit of text scene graph limits.
differentiation: We leverage Kim & Shin's findings to definitively explain our RwR results and justify replacing text graphs with Set-of-Mark visual prompting.
arch_vision: Evaluates LLaVA-1.5, Qwen-VL, GPT-4V with serialized graphs

takeaways.detail: Cite Kim & Shin as definitive peer-reviewed proof that text scene graphs fail universally across all VLMs.
Do not attempt to fix the Relation Block with better text prompt formatting; abandon text graphs for Set-of-Mark visual prompts.

title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
authors: Danny Driess, Fei Xia, Mehdi S. M. Sajjadi, Corey Lynch, Awtar Gondhalekar, Carolina Parada, Kanishka Rao, Pierre Sermanet, Mengyuan Yan, Stefan Welker, et al.
summary: Introduces PaLM-E (up to 562B parameters), an embodied multimodal language model directly ingesting continuous multi-modal sensor inputs (state vectors, point clouds, images) into a pre-trained language model for spatial manipulation and navigation.
abstract: We present PaLM-E, an embodied multimodal language model that ingests continuous sensor modalities directly into a language model. PaLM-E performs sequential robotic manipulation planning, visual question answering, and tabletop spatial reasoning.
findings:
1. Ingesting continuous state vectors directly into the language embedding space preserves physical metric coordinates.
2. Scale matters: 562B model exhibits emergent multi-modal spatial transfer.
3. Preserves linguistic reasoning without catastrophic forgetting.
conclusions: Continuous spatial grounding vectors enable language models to understand physical real-world spatial environments.
relevance_rationale: Adjacent domain: demonstrates how continuous physical coordinates can be fed to LLMs for spatial reasoning.

what_it_adds.Continuous Sensor Tokenization: Maps continuous 3D coordinates into the LLM token space.

what_it_doesnt_add.Nadir Satellite Imagery: Evaluated on ground-level robotic manipulation and tabletop scenes.

differentiation: We operate in overhead gigapixel Earth observation rather than tabletop manipulation.

takeaways.detail: Continuous vector embeddings preserve metric coordinates better than quantized text tokens.

title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
authors: Anthony Brohan, Noah Brown, Justice Carbajal, Yevgen Chebotar, Joseph Dabis, Chelsea Finn, Keerthana Gopalakrishnan, Karol Hausman, Alex Herzog, Jasmine Hsu, Julian Ibarz, Brian Ichter, et al.
summary: Demonstrates Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, co-fine-tuning VLMs on web visual data and robotic trajectory actions represented as discrete text tokens, enabling semantic spatial generalization.
abstract: We present RT-2, translating vision-language models into vision-language-action models. By outputting robotic actions as text tokens, RT-2 transfers semantic reasoning from web-scale pre-training to physical physical manipulation tasks.
findings:
1. Discrete action tokens allow standard autoregressive VLMs to output physical motion coordinates.
2. Emergent semantic generalization to unseen objects and relational instructions.
3. Discretization limits motion precision to the quantization bin resolution.
conclusions: Language models can generate physical spatial action trajectories via tokenized coordinate spaces.
relevance_rationale: Adjacent domain: proves that tokenized action/coordinate spaces have inherent discretization precision floors.

what_it_adds.Vision-Language-Action (VLA): Formulates physical spatial actions as discrete language tokens.

differentiation: We focus on aerial spatial topology rather than robotic arm kinematics.

takeaways.detail: Binning coordinates into 256 discrete tokens imposes a minimum spatial error.

title: LM-Nav: Robotic Navigation with Large Language Models
authors: Dhruv Shah, Blazej Osinski, Brian Ichter, Sergey Levine
summary: Combines a pre-trained LLM (GPT-3), a vision-language model (CLIP), and a topological visual navigation graph (ViNG) to navigate complex real-world environments without fine-tuning.
abstract: We present LM-Nav, enabling long-horizon robotic navigation from natural language instructions without any paired language-navigation training data. LM-Nav decomposes navigation into language parsing (GPT-3), visual landmark retrieval (CLIP), and graph planning over a topological map (ViNG).
findings:
1. Three-way modular separation (language parser + visual retriever + topological graph planner) outperforms monolithic end-to-end models.
2. Topological visual graph handles long-horizon navigation with zero spatial hallucination.
3. Entire system is training-free.
conclusions: Decoupling visual perception, linguistic planning, and topological graph search provides reliable long-horizon spatial execution.
relevance_rationale: Directly supports our modular architecture: separate the linguistic question parser, visual detector, and spatial graph solver.

what_it_adds.Tri-Modular Navigation: LLM planner + CLIP landmark matcher + Topological graph solver.

differentiation: We apply modular topological graph principles to gigapixel satellite imagery for Route Planning.

takeaways.detail: Solve Route Planning by decomposing into: LLM parses waypoints -> YOLO detects roads -> Graph solver plans path.

title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
authors: Wenlong Huang, Fei Xia, Ted Xiao, Harris Chan, Jacky Liang, Pete Florence, Andy Zeng, Jonathan Tompson, Igor Mordatch, Yevgen Chebotar, Pierre Sermanet, Noah Brown, Tomas Jackson, Linda Luu, Sergey Levine, Karol Hausman, Brian Ichter
